# Getting Started with Kepler
URL: https://help.gitkraken.com/kepler/kepler-getting-started/
product: Kepler
feature: Getting Started
content_type: how-to
audience: developer
plan_required: all
status: GA
last_verified: 2026-11

Kepler is GitKraken's **agentic development environment** (**ADE**). Use it to direct coding agents on your real work, in as many repositories as you need, at the same time.

You use your own coding agent. Kepler pulls in the issues and pull requests already assigned to you, hands any of them to an agent with the context attached, and takes the result through review to a change you can merge.

Kepler is in **public preview**. To use it, you need only a free GitKraken account.

<div class="embed-container embed-container--16-9">
    <iframe width="560" height="315" src="https://www.youtube.com/embed/U0w18ZXrZ5M?rel=0&vq=hd1080" frameborder="0" allowfullscreen></iframe>
</div>

***

## Install Kepler

Kepler has installers for these platforms:

| Platform | Installer | Minimum OS |
|---|---|---|
| Windows | 64-bit, ARM64 | Windows 10+ |
| macOS | Apple Silicon, Intel | macOS 12+ |
| Linux (x64) | .deb, .rpm, .AppImage, Flatpak, AUR | Ubuntu LTS 18.04+ / Debian 10+ / RHEL 8+ / Fedora 39+ |
| Linux (ARM) | .deb, .rpm, .AppImage | Ubuntu LTS 20.04+ / RHEL 8+ / Fedora 39+ |

1. Go to [gitkraken.com/kepler/download](https://www.gitkraken.com/kepler/download) and pick the installer for your platform.
2. Run the installer.
3. Launch Kepler.

**If you open an older copy of Kepler** than the one that last used your data, Kepler stops at **Kepler is out of date** before it opens. The older copy cannot read everything the newer one saved, so sessions may seem to have disappeared. Click **Open Newer Version** when a newer copy is installed, or **Update and Restart** to update this copy (a Snap install does not offer it).

***

## Sign in

Kepler opens on a welcome screen, **Launch any agent. Land every PR.** Click **Sign in with GitKraken**. If you do not have an account, you'll create one in the next step.

Kepler opens the sign-in page in your browser. Once you sign in there, Kepler continues on its own. If no browser opened, click **Reopen browser**, or click **Copy link** and open the link in any browser. You can also paste the code from your browser under **Or paste the code from your browser**, then click **Sign in**.

**Behind a proxy.** Kepler uses your system's proxy settings, or the `HTTPS_PROXY` environment variable when you set it, and passes the same proxy to the agents and terminals it starts. If a request fails through the proxy, the error names the proxy's address.

To check for updates before you sign in, click the version in the screen's top corner. When an update has downloaded, click **Update and restart**.

In a window connected to another machine, you sign in from the Kepler window on this computer, and the remote window continues once you finish there.

To watch a short tour before you start, click the **Watch Quick Start Tour** tile on the welcome screen, or watch the <a href="https://www.youtube.com/playlist?list=PLXIji1KJqw9A" target="_blank" rel="noopener noreferrer">Kepler Quick Start Tour playlist</a> on YouTube.

***

## Choose your agents, repos, and look

After you sign in, a guided start walks you through setup. To skip it at any point, click **I'll explore on my own**.

**Choose your coding agents.** Kepler finds the coding agents installed on this computer. In this step:

- Switch on the agents you want Kepler to use, and make one the default. To add a missing agent, click its tile to install or locate it. After an install, Kepler offers to sign you in to the agent. See [Agent Integrations](/kepler/agent-integrations#install-an-agent).
- Under **New sessions start in**, pick **Chat**, Kepler's own view of the agent, or **Terminal**, the agent's command-line app.
- If your code is on another machine, use **Work on another machine?** to move this window there. Remote environments need a paid plan.

If you installed an agent that Kepler did not find, click **Rescan**. To go on without an agent, click **Continue without an agent**. You can set one up later in **Settings → Agents**.

**Bring in your repos.** Every task runs in a repo or folder you add here. Kepler lists the repos and folders it found where you have worked, with the ones you use most already checked. In this step:

- Check the repos you work in. To add one Kepler did not find, click **Add a folder**.
- Confirm the **Repos folder**. Kepler finds your repos there and clones new ones into it.

Then click the button that adds them, such as **Add 2 and continue**. Kepler adds only what you check. If you leave the guided start before you finish this step, Kepler adds the repos it checked for you.

**Make it yours.** Pick a theme, or open the **Theme gallery**, and choose how Kepler gets your attention under **Notify me**:

- **Everything**: every reply and request on the desktop as well
- **When I'm needed**: questions, approvals, and errors on the desktop, while replies stay in Kepler
- **Only in Kepler**: no desktop notifications

To try an alert, click **Send a test notification**. You can change these choices later in [Settings](/kepler/settings-app#notifications). Click **Finish** to open the **New task** composer on the Dashboard and start your first task.

***

## Finish the setup checklist

After the guided start, the **Setup** entry in the top bar tracks 2 setup items and shows **Setup · N/2** until you finish them. Open it to see **Finish setting up Kepler** and your progress. Once both items are done, the **Setup** entry disappears from the top bar.

| # | Item | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | **Connect an AI agent** | At least one coding agent. See [Agent Integrations](/kepler/agent-integrations) |
| 2 | **Connect issue & PR trackers** | Any provider, which fills your Todo list. See [Issue Tracker Integrations](/kepler/issue-tracker-integrations) and [Pull Request Integrations](/kepler/pull-request-integrations) |

Expand **More setup options** for optional items:

- **Set a default repositories folder**: where Kepler clones repositories it does not find locally
- **Set a default worktree folder**: where Kepler creates one worktree per repository, per task
- **Connect a remote environment**, covered in [Remote Environments](/kepler/remote-environments), where your plan can use it
- **Control Kepler remotely**, also in [Remote Environments](/kepler/remote-environments)
- **Add repo commands**, once you have a repository

If your project needs a setup step, use **Add repo commands** early. Save a repository's install or build command once, and Kepler can run it every time it creates a worktree, so an agent never starts in a checkout it cannot build. See [Tasks and Resources](/kepler/tasks-and-resources).

You can set folder paths and everything else on the checklist in [Settings](/kepler/settings-setup-account#setup). To remove the checklist from the top bar, click **Hide from toolbar (still available in Settings)**.

***

## Put an agent on real work

After you connect a tracker, the **Todo** view of [the Kepler interface](/kepler/kepler-interface) fills with the issues and pull requests related to you.

1. Pick an item in **Todo**.
2. Click its **Action** button.

Kepler then does the following on its own:

1. Creates a task.
2. Attaches the repository and the item.
3. Sets up an isolated worktree.
4. Starts an agent with the context already in place.

The left half of the button runs the default Action for the item:

- **Plan** for an issue
- **Review** for someone else's pull request
- **Address Feedback** for one of yours

The chevron next to the button offers the rest of the Actions.

You can change the prompt behind every Action and add Actions of your own. See [Actions](/kepler/actions).

***

## Start something that is not tracked yet

To start a task that has no issue or pull request behind it:

1. Click **New task** or press **Cmd/Ctrl+N**. From outside Kepler, press **Shift+Alt+N** to open the quick launcher.
2. Write a prompt.
3. If the task needs a repository, attach one.
4. Start the task.

You can also attach nothing at all and turn the task into real work later. See [Create a task](/kepler/create-task).

***

Pick the next step that fits what you want to do:

| If you want to | Read |

# Quick Answers
URL: https://help.gitkraken.com/kepler/quick-answers/
product: Kepler
feature: Quick Answers
content_type: how-to
audience: developer
plan_required: all
status: GA
last_verified: 2026-11

Find a short answer to a common Kepler question, then follow its link for the full details. Start here when you know what you want to do but not where to find it.

***

## Run agents where you work

Kepler runs agents on your computer, in WSL, or on another machine. Remote environments, which include WSL distros and SSH hosts, need a paid plan. The number of accounts you can add for one agent depends on your GitKraken plan.

Common questions about where and how your agents run:

| What you want to do | Short answer | Full details |
|---|---|---|
| Run several agents at once without their changes colliding | Give each task a **worktree**, a private Git working copy. Agents change files there, so several can run at once without touching each other's work or your own checkout. | [Tasks and Resources → Worktrees](/kepler/tasks-and-resources#worktrees-and-working-in-place) |
| Run Kepler on Windows | Kepler installs natively on Windows 10 and later, on 64-bit and ARM64. It also runs on macOS 12 and later, and on Linux. | [Getting Started → Install Kepler](/kepler/kepler-getting-started#install-kepler) |
| Run agents in Windows Subsystem for Linux (WSL) | Kepler treats a WSL 2 distro as a remote environment. It finds your version 2 distros and lists them under **Found on this machine** in Settings. | [Remote Environments → WSL environments](/kepler/remote-environments#wsl-environments) |
| Run agents on another machine | Add the machine as an SSH host. Kepler installs itself on the host over SSH, so you do not need to install anything there first. | [Remote Environments → Add an SSH host](/kepler/remote-environments#add-an-ssh-host) |
| Use several accounts of the same agent | Claude Code, Codex, GitHub Copilot, Auggie, and Grok Build can each hold more than one signed-in account. To add one, open **Settings → Agents**, expand the agent, and click **Add account**. | [Agent Sessions → Several accounts for one agent](/kepler/agent-sessions#several-accounts-for-one-agent) |

***

## Start work

You can start a task from an issue in your tracker or from nothing at all.

Common questions about starting work, giving agents your rules, preparing each new worktree, and running agents on their own:

| What you want to do | Short answer | Full details |
|---|---|---|
| Start an agent from a Jira, Linear, or GitHub issue | Connect your tracker, then run an Action from the issue's row. The issue becomes a task, and Kepler attaches what it read, so the agent starts with that context. | [Issue Tracker Integrations](/kepler/issue-tracker-integrations), [Actions](/kepler/actions) |
| Start without an issue | Click **New task** or press **Cmd/Ctrl+N**, then write a prompt. You can attach nothing at all and turn the task into real work later. | [Getting Started → Start something that is not tracked yet](/kepler/kepler-getting-started#start-something-that-is-not-tracked-yet) |
| Give every agent on a task your team's rules | Attach a **Note** to the task with the rule, constraint, or decision. Every session on the task gets it, including sessions you start later. | [Tasks and Resources → Notes](/kepler/tasks-and-resources#notes-are-how-you-give-standing-instructions) |
| Copy `.env` files into every new worktree | List them in a `.worktreeinclude` file at the repository's root, in `.gitignore` syntax. Kepler copies the matching Git-ignored files into each new worktree. | [Tasks and Resources → Make a new worktree ready to build](/kepler/tasks-and-resources#make-a-new-worktree-ready-to-build) |
| Install dependencies in every new worktree | Add a per-repository command, such as `pnpm install`, and turn on **Run on worktree creation**. | [Settings → Per-repository commands](/kepler/settings-repositories#per-repository-commands) |
| Keep agents in different worktrees from colliding on ports or databases | A worktree separates files, not ports, databases, or caches. Use a command that runs on worktree creation to give each worktree its own settings, such as its own port or database name. | [Tasks and Resources → What a worktree does not separate](/kepler/tasks-and-resources#what-a-worktree-does-not-separate) |
| Run an agent on a schedule, or when an issue or pull request changes | Click **Automations** on the Dashboard and create an automation. It runs an Action or your own prompt on a schedule, or when new GitHub or Jira activity matches its query. | [Automations](/kepler/automations) |

***

## Keep track of your agents

Kepler shows you what your agents are doing and when they need you, on your computer or your phone. Remote Access, which opens Kepler on a phone, needs a paid plan.

Common questions about watching and answering your agents:

| What you want to do | Short answer | Full details |
|---|---|---|
| See what every agent is doing | The **Agent Graph** draws every task, session, turn, tool call, subagent, and file the agents touch. It updates live as they work. | [The Agent Graph](/kepler/agent-graph) |
| Find out what needs you | Open **Ask Kepler** and ask. Its chat can see what's on your screen and check on your tasks and sessions. | [Ask Kepler](/kepler/ask-kepler) |
| Answer an agent's permission request | The request pins to the top of the session. Choose **Allow**, **Allow for this session**, **Allow always**, **Reject**, or **Reject always**. | [Agent Sessions → Permission requests](/kepler/agent-sessions#permission-requests) |
| Check on your agents from your phone | Turn on **Remote Access** and scan its QR code with your phone's camera. Kepler opens in your phone's browser, and your work keeps running on your computer. | [Remote Environments → Using Kepler on a phone](/kepler/remote-environments#using-kepler-on-a-phone) |

***

## Review and ship

When an agent finishes, its work is not necessarily ready to ship.

Common questions about reviewing an agent's work and getting it merged:

| What you want to do | Short answer | Full details |
|---|---|---|
| Have the agent prepare its work for review | Create an Action that asks the agent to summarize what it changed, what it tested, and what it did not test. The example **Prepare for review** Action shows the prompt. | [Actions → Example: Prepare for review](/kepler/actions#example-prepare-for-review) |
| Read what an agent changed | Open the task's worktree and read the diff in the **Changes** overlay. From there you can comment, stage, and commit. | [Review Changes](/kepler/review-changes) |
| Undo an agent's change to a file | Use **Discard changes**, which asks first. Your current version goes to the Trash (the Recycle Bin on Windows), so you can get it back. | [Review Changes → Staging and committing](/kepler/review-changes#staging-and-committing) |
| Have a different agent review the work | Set the **Review** Action to a different agent from the one that wrote the code. | [Actions → Review with a different agent](/kepler/actions#review-with-a-different-agent) |
| Apply the review comments on a pull request | Run **Address Feedback** on the pull request. It triages the comments, applies what's worth applying, and pushes back on the rest. | [Actions → The four built-in Actions](/kepler/actions#the-four-built-in-actions) |
| Open a pull request | Kepler has no "create pull request" button, so you or the agent opens the pull request, and Kepler attaches it to the task once it exists. The example **Open a pull request** Action has the agent open it, with a note that an agent helped write the change. | [Review Changes → Opening a pull request](/kepler/review-changes#opening-a-pull-request), [Actions → Example: Open a pull request](/kepler/actions#example-open-a-pull-request) |

---

# The Kepler Interface
URL: https://help.gitkraken.com/kepler/kepler-interface/
product: Kepler
feature: Kepler Interface
content_type: how-to
audience: developer
plan_required: all
status: GA
last_verified: 2026-11

Kepler's Dashboard shows your work: the issues and pull requests that involve you across your connected trackers and Git hosts, beside the tasks you already have running. To start work, pick an item from the list instead of describing it from scratch.

You can arrange the Dashboard to fit how you work. See [Arranging Your Work](/kepler/arranging-your-work). Besides the Dashboard, Kepler has a page for each task, Settings, and remote connections.

***

## The top bar

The top bar holds the following controls, from the leading edge:

- The window switcher
- **Back** and **Forward**, in the desktop app only
- **New task**
- The Dashboard's views, when you place them in the title bar. By default they sit in a row below it. See [The Dashboard's views](#the-dashboards-views).
- Your setup progress, until you finish the primary setup steps
- **Stop reading**, on every page while Kepler reads an agent's reply aloud. Click it to stop. Hover it to see the sentence being read. See [Read aloud](/kepler/voice-input#read-aloud).
- The remote indicator: the environment chip that shows which machine this window works on
- **Remote Access**, a monitor-and-phone button whose color shows whether Remote Access is on. Hover it to turn Remote Access on or off and, while it's on, to scan its QR code or copy its link. See [Remote access](/kepler/remote-environments#remote-access-reach-kepler-from-another-device).
- **Ask Kepler** (**Cmd/Ctrl+L** or **Cmd/Ctrl+K**), shown as Kep, Kepler's mascot, with the word **Ask**. It opens a chat and quick terminals in a panel beside the page. See [Ask Kepler](/kepler/ask-kepler).
- Feedback
- Settings
- Your account

The **Ask Kepler** button also shows the state of the panel's chats. When a chat needs you, has a new reply, or failed, the button becomes a **Needs you**, **New reply**, or **Failed** pill. Click the pill to open that chat. A focused shell keeps **Ctrl+L** for itself, so use **Ctrl+K** there. See [Ask Kepler](/kepler/ask-kepler).

While an update downloads, a chip near the trailing end of the top bar shows its progress. Hover the chip to see the version and about how long is left. You can keep working meanwhile.

When the update is ready, an **Update available** chip replaces the progress chip. It opens a popover that says what a restart does to running work, such as how many agents it stops and whether terminals close, and offers **Restart to update**. The chip shows on every screen.

On Windows and Linux, Kepler replaces the native title bar with its own. The menu button at the leading edge holds the full application menu (**File**, **Edit**, **View**, **Window**, **Help**), including **Settings**, **Check for Updates…**, and **About**. macOS keeps its native menu bar. Both menus open the same **About Kepler** dialog.

As the window narrows, the top bar hides the controls that no longer fit.

Menu items and button tooltips show a command's keyboard shortcut when the item does exactly what the key does, including a key you assigned yourself. To see every shortcut or change one, see [Keyboard shortcuts](/kepler/settings-app#keyboard-shortcuts).

### The window switcher

The **Windows** menu in the top bar lists every open Kepler window and what its agents are doing. Its button shows how many sessions are waiting or running in your other windows. In the menu:

- **This window** marks the window you're in.
- **New window** (**Cmd/Ctrl+Shift+N**) opens another window on the same connection as this one.
- **New local window**, in a remote window, opens a window on this computer instead.

The [tray icon](#the-tray-icon) has the same list.

Each window's title starts with the remote it's connected to and how many of its sessions are waiting on you. Each window keeps its own layout. If you close the last window while Kepler keeps running, the next window opens where that one was.

### The tray icon

Kepler's icon in the system tray (the menu bar on macOS) shows the most urgent thing your agents are doing, even when no window is open. The icon counts every agent session Kepler runs on this computer and on each remote machine that an open window connects to. It counts each session at one level, listed here from most urgent:

| Level | Which sessions |
|---|---|
| Needs your answer | Waiting on your answer or on an approval |
| Failed | A turn that ended in an error and that you have not opened |
| Finished | A finished turn you have not read |
| Working | Running a turn |

The icon does not count idle sessions, sessions started outside Kepler, plain terminals, archived sessions, or sessions whose only work is a background task.

Hover the icon to see a count of each level. On macOS, a count of the agents that need a look (waiting, failed, or finished) appears beside the icon, in red while any of them is waiting or failed.

On Windows and Linux, click the icon to open the window that needs you. The icon's menu holds:

- **Open Kepler**
- **Windows**, a submenu with **New Window**, **New Local Window** when the window you used last is remote, and every open window, with a check beside the one you used last
- **Quit** and **Quit & End Sessions**

### New task

**New task** (**Cmd/Ctrl+N**) opens the **New task** composer. To start a task from a conversation you began outside Kepler, use **Open an external session** in the composer. A session that's still live in its terminal opens read-only in its task, and **Continue here** and **Fork** become available once it's idle. See [Create a task](/kepler/create-task#from-a-session-you-already-started).

***

## The Dashboard's views

The Dashboard shows your work in views. To move between them, click a view in the row of views, which sits below the top bar by default.

Kepler starts you with 3 views:

| View | What it shows |
|---|---|
| **Todo** | Issues and pull requests from your connected integrations |
| **Tasks** | The tasks you already have running in Kepler |
| **Agent Graph** | A live graph of every task, session, turn, tool call, and file. See [The Agent Graph](/kepler/agent-graph) |

Each view keeps its own layout, grouping, sort, filters, search and, on a Todo view, scope. Changes you make in the view's **View** menu save automatically, and switching to another view and back restores its open panels. See [Arranging Your Work](/kepler/arranging-your-work).

The **Automations** button, after the views, opens your automations: agents that run on a schedule or when new GitHub or Jira activity matches a query. A count on the button shows the runs that need you. See [Automations](/kepler/automations).

To work with views:

- **New view** adds a **Todo**, **Tasks** or **Agent Graph** view, or a copy of the one you're on. Name it, pick its **Icon** and layout, then choose **Done**.
- Click the view you're on, or right-click any view, for its menu, with **Rename** (**F2**), **Change icon**, **Duplicate view**, **Views position**, **Delete view**, and more.
- Double-click a view to rename it. Drag a view to reorder the row.
- You always keep at least 1 **Todo** and 1 **Tasks** view.

The views show on every page. Pick one to go back to the Dashboard on that view.

Views can also sit in the top bar or down the left side of the window, as **Tabs** or **Pills**. Choose in the view menu's **Views position**, or in [Settings → Appearance → Dashboard](/kepler/settings-app#dashboard).

What a Todo view lists depends on its **Scope**, a switch in its **View** menu:

- **Mine**, the default: work created by you, assigned to you, mentioning you, or awaiting your review
- **All**: everything open in Kepler's repositories, plus your work elsewhere

Under **Mine**, each provider lists:

| Integration | Issues | Pull requests |
|---|---|---|
| **GitHub**, **GitHub Enterprise** | Yours, assigned to you or mentioning you | Yours, assigned to you or ones you review |
| **GitLab**, **GitLab Self-Hosted**, **Azure DevOps**, **Azure DevOps Server** | Yours or assigned to you | Yours or awaiting your review |
| **Bitbucket Cloud** | None | Yours, or awaiting your review in your workspaces and repositories added to Kepler |
| **Bitbucket Data Center** | None | Yours or awaiting your review |
| **Jira**, **Jira Server**, **Linear**, **Trello**, **Asana** | Assigned to you | None |

**Mine** covers every organization you belong to.

**All** adds every open pull request and issue of the repositories added to Kepler. On Bitbucket and Azure DevOps it adds pull requests only, and issue trackers add nothing. Under **All**, 2 more rows narrow the list:

- **Repos**: **All repos in Kepler**, or **Custom** to choose from a searchable list of your repositories with their open counts.
- **Updated**: **Last 7 days**, **Last 30 days**, **Last 90 days** (the default), or **Last year**.

**All repos in Kepler** skips a very large repository, one with 1,000 or more open pull requests or 2,000 or more open issues, and Todo says so. To load it anyway, click **Choose repos** and add it under **Repos**.

To browse issues outside the scope, use **New task** → **Issues** → **All visible**.

Work starts in **Todo** and moves to **Tasks** while it's underway. The **Agent Graph** view shows tasks as a graph instead of a list.

The Dashboard opens on the view you used last. The first time you start Kepler, a guided setup helps you connect your agents. See [Getting Started with Kepler](/kepler/kepler-getting-started). If you have no tasks yet, **Tasks** shows the **New task** composer. See [Empty states](#empty-states).

To fill **Todo**, connect at least one provider. See [Issue Tracker Integrations](/kepler/issue-tracker-integrations) and [Pull Request Integrations](/kepler/pull-request-integrations).

### External sessions

Todo lists only issues and pull requests. Agent conversations running outside Kepler do not have a section of their own in the list, and they do not open as panels. To pick one up, open **New task** and use **Open an external session** in the **New task** composer. See [Create a task](/kepler/create-task#from-a-session-you-already-started).

To learn what external sessions are and what you can do with them, see [Agent Sessions](/kepler/agent-sessions#sessions-started-outside-kepler).

***

## Reading a row

Todo rows and task rows show different information. A Todo row describes an issue or pull request. A task row describes a task you already started.

### Todo rows: issues and pull requests

Each Todo row shows, from left to right:

- The provider
- A type badge (Issue or PR) with the reference (issue key or PR number)
- The title
- On a pull request, what it needs from you, such as **Changes requested**, or else your role: **Yours** or **Review**
- A **Task** badge (or **{count} tasks**) when tasks were already started from the item, or **Archived task** (**{count} archived tasks**) when every one of them is archived
- The repository
- A status pill
- Any session activity: the session dots of the task linked to the item, and that task's running terminals
- The people: a pull request's author and an avatar for each reviewer, ringed in the color of their review (green for approved, red for changes requested), or an issue's assignee
- When it last changed
- An Action button

Hover the avatars to see a card that names everyone on the item and shows where each review stands. An issue that's on your list only because it mentions you carries a muted **Mentioned** badge, so you can tell it apart from work assigned to you.

When a Linear issue is synced with a GitHub issue and both copies are listed, Todo shows one row for them: the Linear row. The 2 copies share one task history. A task started from either copy counts as the issue's task, and a task started from the Linear row works in the GitHub copy's repository. If you filter the list to GitHub, the GitHub copy shows on its own.

When a provider fails to load, Kepler keeps showing its rows from the last successful load, with a crossed-out cloud on their provider chip. A notice above the list names the provider and the fix, such as signing in again or **Retry**. If you do not need that provider, click **Filter out {provider}** beside its fix to hide it from Todo, so the notice stops reporting it. To show it again, clear it in **Filter**.

Right-click a Todo row to open its menu. The menu does not change which panel is open. It holds:

- **Open task page**, when the item already has a task
- **Open on {provider}**
- **Copy link** (**Cmd/Ctrl+C** on a focused row)
- **Copy title**
- **Copy number**
- **Copy branch name**, on a pull request

When the list is narrow, each row wraps onto 2 lines instead of dropping cells. On the **Board** layout, a pull request's card also shows its branch.

The **Your role** grouping and filter sort items by your part in them:

| Role | Meaning |
|---|---|
| **Yours** | You authored the pull request. The row shows **Yours** |
| **Review** | You're a reviewer on it. The row shows **Review** |
| **Unattributed** | The provider did not say. The row shows no role |
| **Not mine** | Under the **All** scope, you have no part in the pull request or issue. The row shows no role |

### Task rows

Each task row shows:

- The title
- The repository, or every repository when the task spans several
- The task's pull request and issue as chips, each with its state
- Its group, when it's in one: a colored bar on the **List** layout, or a chip on a **Board** card
- A progress control
- What the task needs from you
- Session activity, and a pill for its running terminals
- Time
- A **Star** button, shown when you hover or focus the row, and kept in view once the task is starred
- An **Automation** badge, on a task an automation started. Hover it to see the automation's query. See [Automations](/kepler/automations).

Star a task to mark it important. In the **Inbox** grouping, a starred task lists under **Important**, and in every sort except **Manual**, starred tasks list first in their section. To take the star off, click **Unstar**. On a touch screen, use **Star** in the task's menu.

The needs cell gives the most pressing reason first, such as **Approval needed for {tool}**, **Waiting for you**, **Turn failed**, **Agent stopped** or **CI failing**. **Turn failed** means an agent's turn ended in an error. **Agent stopped** means the agent itself stopped with an error. On a task on hold, it says what the hold waits for, or why the hold lifted.

A failed turn, a stopped agent, failing CI, a new **Changes requested** review, or a hold that lifted on bad news moves the task into **Needs attention**.

Hover **Approval needed for {tool}** to answer the request, such as with **Allow** or **Reject**, without opening the task.

When a session or a terminal in a task waits on you, the task's title shows in bold. Click the terminals pill to open the most urgent terminal, or the session dots to open the most urgent session.

Hover a pull request or issue chip to see its card, or click the chip to keep the card open. When the task has more than one link of that kind, the card lists them all. Right-click the chip for the link's menu.

On a **Board** card, hover the group chip to see a summary of the group's tasks. Click the chip for **Open group**, **Show only this group**, **Remove from group** and the grouping options. See [Arranging Your Work](/kepler/arranging-your-work).

A Done task that's ready to archive also gets an **Archive task** button on its row.

When the list is grouped by repository, a task that spans several repositories appears under each of them.

To manage a task, open its **⋮** menu or right-click its row. The menu holds:

- **Open task page** and **Open in new window**
- **Reopen**, while the task is Done, and a **Progress** submenu. See [Arranging Your Work](/kepler/arranging-your-work).
- **Mark as read** or **Mark as unread**
- **Star** or **Unstar**
- **Rename task** (**F2** on a focused panel) and **Add to group**
- **Move up**, **Move down**, and **Move to top of {section}**, while the list is sorted by **Manual**. See [Arranging Your Work](/kepler/arranging-your-work#sort).
- **Manage resources**, which opens the task's **Resources** screen
- **Refresh**, which re-reads the task's worktrees and its linked pull requests and issues
- **Copy task link** (**Cmd/Ctrl+C** on a focused row), a `kepler://` link to the task
- **Copy task prompt**
- **Panel**, a submenu with the panel's own items, on a task open in a panel. See [The side panel](#the-side-panel).
- **Shut down all agents**, which asks first while an agent is still working
- **Archive task**, or **Restore task** when the task is already archived
- **Delete task**

**Act on several tasks at once.** Open 2 or more tasks with **Shift-click** or **Cmd/Ctrl-click** (see [Open a panel](#open-a-panel)), then right-click any of them. The menu acts on the whole selection, and each label counts the tasks:

- **Progress of {count} tasks**, which sets the stage of every selected task
- **Mark {count} tasks as read** or **Mark {count} tasks as unread**
- **Star {count} tasks** or **Unstar {count} tasks**
- **New group with {count} tasks…**
- **Add {count} tasks to group**
- **Remove {count} tasks from group**
- **Shut down agents in {count} tasks**, which asks first while an agent is still working
- **Archive {count} tasks**
- **Restore {count} tasks**
- **Delete {count} tasks**

The menu shows only the items that apply, and grouping and **Progress** leave archived tasks out. **Archive**, **Restore**, and **Delete** ask first, with the same confirmation as a section's **Select** bar. If you right-click a task outside the selection, or use a row's **⋮** menu, the action applies to that task alone.

Drag any selected task to move the whole selection to another section or column or, under **Manual** sort, to a new place in the list. Press **Escape** to cancel the drag. Each task moves only where it can, and Kepler tells you how many moved and how many stayed where they were.

### Status

Task rows and Todo rows both show a status, but the 2 statuses mean different things:

| Where | Values | What it means |
|---|---|---|
| **Task rows** | **Exploration**, **In Development**, **In Review**, **On hold**, **Later**, **Done**, **Archived** | How far the *work* has got. Kepler derives it from the task's checkouts and pull requests, unless you or an agent set it by hand |
| **Todo rows** | **Open**, **Draft**, **Merged**, **Closed** for a pull request; the tracker's own state for an issue | The provider's own state on the pull request, and the workflow state your tracker uses for the issue (such as a Linear *In Progress* or a Jira *To Verify*) rather than a flat Open |

Kepler derives a task's stage from this evidence:

- **In Development**: uncommitted changes, or commits not yet merged into the base branch.
- **In Review**: an open or draft pull request of the task's own.
- **Done**: at least one of the task's branches has landed, the task has no open pull request of its own, and no checkout still carries commits that have not landed.
- **On hold**, **Later**, and **Archived**: filing decisions, not evidence.

A task sits at the furthest stage any of its checkouts reached, except **Done**, which follows its own rule.

**Done** waits for the work to land, however it got there, including a rebase or squash merge, or a merge with no pull request. A task that's done but still has uncommitted changes or unpushed commits in a checkout reads **Done · local changes**, so you can decide whether to keep them before you archive.

To set the stage yourself, or to set the task aside, click the progress control on its row. A stage you set stays until the evidence moves past it. There are 2 ways to set a task aside:

- **On hold** pauses the task while its agents keep running. Hold it **Indefinitely**, for a set time, or until something happens, such as CI finishing or a review arriving. A hold with a condition lifts by itself, and the row says why.
- **Later** sets the task aside until you bring it back. It stops the task's agents and keeps their sessions, so you can resume them later.

A Done task offers neither. See [Arranging Your Work](/kepler/arranging-your-work#set-a-tasks-progress).

Each task row also shows one dot for each distinct session state, with a count of each.

The dots show what the *agents* are doing, which is separate from where the work stands, such as **Running**, **Waiting**, **Unread** or **Error**.

A waiting session also says what it's waiting on, such as **Permission** or **Question**. A session with an unanswered Kepler approval request counts as waiting, even while its agent keeps working, and reads **Approval needed** (or **Approval needed, destructive**). A live session that stopped after a failed turn, such as a rate limit, an exhausted quota, or an overloaded agent, reads **Error**.

When a session's turn ends but something it started keeps going in the background, such as a shell or a monitor, the session reads **Background task running**. Its dot is solid green and does not pulse. It has its own count in the hover card rather than joining **Running**, and it does not keep the machine awake. See [Agent Sessions](/kepler/agent-sessions).

A dormant session shows as an outlined dot rather than a filled one. Hover the dots to see a count of each state, most urgent first.

***

## Starting work from a row

Click the **Action** button on a Todo row to hand the item to an agent with its context already attached: the repository, the issue body, the branch, and the diff. You do not need to copy or paste anything.

The left half of the button runs the suggested Action for that kind of item, and the chevron opens the full list. The defaults are:

- **Plan** for issues
- **Address Feedback** for pull requests you authored
- **Review** for everyone else's

You can change all of these defaults. See [Actions](/kepler/actions).

### Open a panel

- **Click a row** to select it and open the side panel. A plain click replaces whatever was open, except for panels you've pinned. If the row's panel is already open, the click moves focus to that panel instead, and a second click closes the others.
- **Shift-click** a second row to open both side by side. The panel holds one column per open item, each with its own chat, so you can work several tasks at once without leaving the list.
- **Cmd-click** (**Ctrl-click** on Windows and Linux) to add one row to the open set, or to close it again.
- **Double-click a row** to open the item's full task page. From a Todo row that's the page of the task behind it. A row with no task yet has no page, so a double-click opens its panel with the cursor in the prompt box instead.

**From the keyboard**, the list is a single tab stop. Move through it like a tree with these keys:

| Key | What it does |
|---|---|
| **↑** / **↓** | Move between section headers and rows. Landing on a header opens nothing |
| **→** | Unfold a folded section, or step into an open one |
| **←** | Fold an open section, or climb from a row to its section header |
| **Home** / **End** | Jump to the first or last row |
| **Page Up** / **Page Down** | Move by a screenful |
| **Space** | Open the focused row's panel, or close it if it's open |
| **Enter** | On a row whose panel is open, move focus into that panel |
| **Alt+Enter** | Open the item's task page, like a double-click |

On the **Board** layout, **←** and **→** move between columns. **Tab** leaves the list.

**Alt+Shift+↑** and **Alt+Shift+↓** (**⌥⇧↑** and **⌥⇧↓** on macOS) open the previous or next item in the list.

A new task appears in the list as soon as you press **Start** in the **New task** composer. While Kepler sets it up, its row shows a **Preparing** pill, and its panel shows each step, with **Cancel** while a repository clones. If setup fails, the row shows **Failed**. Choose **Edit and retry** to change the task and start it again, or **Dismiss**.

Shift-click selects a range from your last plain click, as it does in Finder or VS Code. You can open up to 16 panels at once. Once they're all open, opening another closes the unpinned panel you opened longest ago. To arrange the panels in rows, see [Lay panels out in a grid](#lay-panels-out-in-a-grid).

Each panel gets its own column as soon as you open it. Until its item loads, the column shows a placeholder, with **Try again** if the item could not be loaded, or **Sign in** if you're signed out. You can close any placeholder.

**Resize.** Drag the divider between 2 columns to resize the one on its left. Hold **Shift** as you drag to give every panel the same width or, with **Auto columns** on, to set how wide the columns should be. Double-click the divider to split the space evenly again. Each view remembers its own widths.

**Scroll.** Once the panel strip grows wider than the window, it scrolls instead of squeezing the columns below a readable width. Scroll it sideways with **Shift** and the mouse wheel, or a sideways trackpad swipe, even over a terminal.

**Reorder.** Drag a panel by its header to a new place in the strip. A panel's **Panel actions** menu (**⋮**) offers **Move panel left** and **Move panel right**, and so do **Cmd/Ctrl+Alt+Shift+←** and **Cmd/Ctrl+Alt+Shift+→**.

**Solo.** Once 2 or more panels are open, **Solo panel** in the **⋮** menu (or **Cmd/Ctrl+Shift+M**) widens one panel across the strip. Drag the soloed panel's edges to resize it, or click **Maximize** in its header to fill the space. Click outside it, or click **Unsolo panel** in its header, to put the layout back.

**Move between panels.** **Ctrl+Tab** opens **Recent panels**, a switcher of your open panels and the ones you replaced recently, so you can switch back to an item you moved away from. **Delete** or **Backspace** closes the highlighted panel, or removes it from the list. **Cmd/Ctrl+1** through **Cmd/Ctrl+8** jump to a panel by its position from the left, and **Cmd/Ctrl+9** to the last.

If you start a task from **New task** while you're on the list, the new task opens as a panel and the list stays where it was, instead of switching to the task's page. The panel opens beside the one you're reading, or at the end in a grid. To always open it at the end, change **Where a new task opens on the Dashboard** in [Settings → Tasks](/kepler/settings-tasks#new-tasks).

**Open several at once.** Each section's header has a button that opens that section's rows in panels, up to the panel limit. A group's chip offers **Open group** for its tasks.

**Hide the list.** With at least one panel open, the toggle at the start of the Dashboard header, **Hide list** (**Cmd/Ctrl+B**), hides the list so the panels get the full width. While the list is hidden:

- Hover the toggle, now **Dock list**, to see the list float over the panels as the **Task list** (or **Todo list**). **Cmd/Ctrl+Shift+B** shows the floating list or hides it again.
- Click a row in the floating list to open it. The list closes and focus moves into that panel; **Escape** closes the list while focus is in it.
- Drag the floating list's edge (**Resize list**) to resize it, and double-click the edge to reset it.
- When a task in the hidden list needs you and has no panel open, the toggle shows its status dot.
- **Dock list**, or **Cmd/Ctrl+B** again, brings the list back beside the panels.

A hidden list always uses the **List** layout. **Cmd/Ctrl+B** works from a terminal on macOS only; on Windows and Linux a focused shell keeps **Ctrl+B**.

When the window is too narrow for the list beside the open panels, Kepler hides the list, and the toggle reads **Show list**. Click it to float the list over the panels. The list returns when you widen the window.

### Lay panels out in a grid

By default, open panels sit side by side in 1 row, with **Auto columns**: as many columns as the window has room for. To see more panels at once, lay them out in a grid. Click **Panel layout** in the toolbar, whose button shows the current size, such as **Auto × 1** or **3 × 2**:

- Pick a size in the **Grid size** matrix. 1 row puts panels side by side, and 2 or more rows make a grid.
- Turn off **Auto columns** to choose a fixed number of columns.
- **Reset sizes** evens out rows and columns you've resized.

A grid holds up to 16 panels, fewer in smaller windows. In a grid:

- Drag the dividers between grid columns (**Resize grid column**) and rows (**Resize grid row**). Hold **Shift** to resize every track at once, and double-click a divider or press **Home** on it to even them out.
- Panels that do not fit the grid go on further pages that scroll sideways.
- Drag a panel by its header to reorder it, row by row. **Move panel up** and **Move panel down** (**Cmd/Ctrl+Alt+Shift+↑** and **Cmd/Ctrl+Alt+Shift+↓**) join the left and right moves.
- **Solo panel** spreads one panel over its page.
- Panels in short cells start with their headers folded, until you unfold them.
- Clicking rows opens and closes panels the same way as in 1 row. See [Open a panel](#open-a-panel).

### Pin a panel

An unpinned panel is for browsing: a plain click on another row replaces it. To keep a panel in place, choose **Pin panel** from the panel's **⋮** menu (on a task, under **Panel**). After you pin a panel:

- A plain click on a row opens beside your pinned panels instead of replacing them.
- Following a link in **Related** replaces an unpinned panel in place, but opens the linked item beside a pinned one.
- The pin stays with the view you pinned it in.
- Kepler never closes a pinned panel to make room when the maximum number of panels is open.

Kepler always keeps one panel unpinned for browsing, so browsing never has to close a pinned panel. Once every other panel is pinned, the menu item reads **Keep one panel unpinned for browsing** and you cannot pin another. To release a pinned panel, click **Unpin panel** in its header.

***

## The side panel

Select a row to open its side panel beside the list. The side panel shows everything about the item in a stack of collapsible, resizable sections.

A section appears only when it has something to show:

| Section | What's in it | When it's there |
|---|---|---|
| **Summary** | The description and labels, which you can select and copy | An issue or pull request with a description |
| **Related ({count})** | Every task linked to the issue or pull request, archived ones included | An issue or pull request with at least one linked task |
| **What's running** | The chat: session tabs and draft session tabs | Always, on an item you can start work on. You can resize it but not fold it |
| **Plan** | The plan the conversation on screen has proposed | The agent produced one |
| **Changes** | The checkout's commits, working changes, and file diffs, in the [side pane](#the-side-pane) | You opened a worktree's changes from its worktree button |
| **Terminals** | Terminal tabs across the task's checkouts, each with its program's status when it reports one | While a terminal is open. **Cmd/Ctrl+J** shows or hides it without stopping the shells |

In **Related**, click a live task to open it in the panel, or an archived one to open its task page without restoring it. A task shows its own pull requests and issues as chips instead.

To reorder the tabs in **What's running** or **Terminals**, drag a tab to a new place. Kepler keeps each task's terminal tab order.

To archive a session from the keyboard, focus its tab in **What's running** and press **Delete**. Kepler asks first. The tab's own archive control and its menu item archive in one click, without asking.

A plain shell tab takes the name of what's running in it, such as `pnpm dev`, and returns to its own label at the prompt. Hover a tab with a program status to see how long the program has been in that state, its progress, and, for a blocked or failed program, what to do next.

If an agent fails after you start a session, **What's running** shows **{agent} was unable to start** with the agent's message. Press **Retry** to launch it again, or **Open agent settings** to fix the problem.

For an issue or pull request with no task yet, the side panel's primary button runs the item's suggested Action, such as **Plan**, **Implement**, **Review**, or **Address Feedback**. If the suggested Action is **None**, no longer exists, or cannot apply to this kind of item, the button reads **Start** instead.

In the side panel for a task, the primary button reads **Start**. Once a session exists, the composer becomes that session's chat, and the button reads **Send**.

If you created a task with a prompt but have not started it, press **Start** with the box empty to send the task's prompt as the first message, or type something to send that instead.

The side panel's header holds:

- The item's badges and reference
- On an issue or pull request, the people on it: a pull request's author, assignees and reviewers, each reviewer marked with the state of their review, or an issue's assignee
- The title, with a dot when a session needs you: blue for an unread turn, orange for one waiting on you
- The progress control, on a task
- The terminal control, on a task
- **Unsolo panel** and **Maximize**, while the panel is soloed
- **Unpin panel**, when the panel is pinned
- **Close panel** (**Cmd/Ctrl+W** on the focused panel)
- **Panel actions** (**⋮**): **Close panel**, **Open task page**, **Open on {provider}** for an issue or pull request, **Pin panel**, **Solo panel**, **Move panel left**, **Move panel right**, **Close other panels**, and **Close all panels**. On a task, these items are part of its **Task actions** menu. **Solo panel**, the move items, **Close other panels**, and **Close all panels** appear only when more than one panel is open

An issue or pull request also has a status line with its provider state, session dots, repository, and last activity.

Each pull request, issue, or artifact linked to a task has a chip under the header. While a pull request is open or in draft, its chip ends with its CI status: failing, pending, or passing. Hover a chip to see its card, or click it to read the item in the side pane. The **Resources** chip opens the task's **Resources** list in the [side pane](#the-side-pane), or closes it.

Hover a task's title to read its prompt. To copy the whole prompt, use **Copy task prompt** in the **⋮** menu. The prompt also appears first among the task's notes, labeled **Prompt**, and you cannot delete it.

To rename a task, choose **Rename task** from its **⋮** menu, or press **F2** on its focused panel, then edit the name in place. While only one panel is open, you can also double-click the title. With several open, click the focused panel's title to rename it, or double-click it to solo the panel. Press **Enter** to save the change, or **Escape** to discard it.

To fold the header down to its title row, use the chevron beside the title. A folded task header has a run control, and a row of icons that each open a view in the side pane.

The run control runs the worktree's command, or opens the worktree in your editor when it has no commands. Its menu lists every command and an **Open in** submenu. The icons are:

- **Show changes**: the changes of the worktree on its worktree button
- **Show pull request**: the pull request that asks the most of you
- **Show issue**: the unfinished issue updated last
- **Show resources**: the **Resources** list

In the narrowest panels, the icons fold into one paperclip icon that opens the **Resources** list.

A Done task with no unpushed work, and no agent working, waiting on you, or keeping background work alive (such as a dev server), shows *Ready to archive?* in its header. See [Arranging Your Work](/kepler/arranging-your-work).

An archived task reads **Archived** where its progress control would be, in both its panel and its task page.

### The side pane

A task panel opens its linked items, resources, and changes in a **side pane**, so you can read them without leaving the list for the task page. The following open in the side pane:

- A linked pull request or issue chip
- The **Resources** list, from the **Resources** chip, and any row in it
- The uncommitted or commits chip on a worktree button

The **Resources** list holds everything the task carries: **Pull requests**, **Issues**, notes, files, folders, links, and **Related tasks**. Click a group's heading to fold the group. Each row has a **⋮** menu. To add a resource of one kind, click the **+** on its group's heading. To add or change resources, click **Manage resources**, which opens the task's **Resources** screen.

In a wide panel, the pane opens beside the sessions. Drag its edge to resize it, and close it with **Close side pane** or **Escape**. In a narrower panel, the pane takes the sessions' place, with **Back to sessions** to return.

Click the same chip again to close the pane. To move between the task's linked items and resources without closing the pane, use the switcher in the pane's title row. On the focused panel, 2 shortcuts show or hide the pane:

- **Cmd/Ctrl+Shift+G** shows or hides the worktree's changes.
- **Cmd/Ctrl+Shift+E** shows or hides the **Resources** list.

### Issue comments

An issue you open in a side pane, or on the task page, shows its discussion under the summary as **Comments**. Kepler loads the newest 100 comments. **Show earlier comments** reveals older ones, and **Refresh comments** reads them again.

Comments work for GitHub, GitHub Enterprise, GitLab, GitLab Self-Hosted, Jira, and Jira Server issues. Kepler shows comments to you but does not pass them to the agent as task context.

### The worktree button

Below the header, each of the task's checkouts appears as a **worktree button** with 2 rows: what identifies the checkout on top, and what's in it below.

The button's rows hold:

| Row | What it shows |
|---|---|
| **Top** | The branch and repository, the worktree's own pull request with its CI status, and the upstream control |
| **Bottom** | Chips for uncommitted files, commits, and the merge target, plus **Open in** and **Run** |

The button's controls do the following:

- **Branch name**: opens or closes the worktree's changes in the side pane. Its **⋮** opens the [worktree menu](#the-worktree-menu).
- **Upstream control**: runs the action its counts call for. It offers **Pull** when the branch is behind, **Push** when it's ahead, and **Publish** when the branch is not on a remote yet. When the branch has diverged, or after you apply a rebase, it offers **Force push** after a confirmation. **Fetch** and the upstream row are in its chevron menu.
- **Uncommitted** and **commits** chips: open the worktree's changes in the side pane, on that scope. Click the chip that's showing again to close the side pane, or the other chip to switch scope.
- **Merge target** chip: shows how the branch compares with its merge target. While the target is ahead, its menu offers **See what's new on {target}**. See [What's new on the merge target](/kepler/review-changes#whats-new-on-the-merge-target). The menu also offers **Rebase onto {target}** and **Merge {target} into this branch**. See [Review Changes](/kepler/review-changes#updating-from-the-base).
- **Open in**: opens the checkout in your default editor. Other editors are in its chevron menu.
- **Run**: runs one of the repository's commands.

The button also tells you what needs doing, such as unpushed commits, or a paused rebase or merge you can continue or abort from the button. Hover any chip to see what a click does, or right-click the chip for the worktree's menu.

#### The worktree menu

The worktree menu is the same wherever a worktree appears, on the worktree button and on the task page. It holds:

- **Open changes** (or **Close changes** while they're showing), **Open in**, and the worktree's pull request
- **Continue {operation}** and **Abort {operation}** during a stopped rebase or merge
- A **Branch** submenu: **Rename branch**, **Rebase onto {target}** and **Merge {target} into this branch**, **Push**, **Pull** and **Fetch**, **Set upstream** or **Change upstream**, and **Change merge target…**
- **New session here**, **New terminal here**, and **Run command here**
- **Copy branch name**, **Copy worktree path**, and **Copy remote URL**
- **Detach worktree…** and **Delete worktree…**, or **Recreate worktree** for a checkout that's gone

**Set or change the upstream.** **Set upstream** or **Change upstream** opens a searchable list of remote branches. Any remote branch can be the upstream, under any name, and **Push** then pushes there. See [Set or change the upstream](/kepler/review-changes#set-or-change-the-upstream).

**More than one worktree.** A task's worktrees collapse into one worktree button. Step through them with the switcher on the branch name, or with the up and down arrow keys on the button. Until you pick one, the button shows the worktree with the latest changes. To see them all at once, use the toggle on the button's leading edge (**Show all {count} worktrees**). Worktrees whose branches have merged share a single row, from which you can delete them through the same cleanup list that archiving uses.

From the keyboard, a worktree button is 2 tab stops, one for its changes and one for its actions. Use the left and right arrow keys to move inside each.

When a task has more than one checkout, the terminal strip's **+** opens a chooser that lists the checkouts by branch.

***

## Go to a task or file

To jump to a task, a pull request or issue, or a file, or to run a command, open the Go to palette from anywhere. It has 4 tabs: **Tasks**, **Todo**, **Files** and **Commands**. To open it:

- **Cmd/Ctrl+Shift+P** or **F1** (**View › Command Palette…**) opens **Go to task**, on **Tasks**.
- **Cmd/Ctrl+P** (**File › Go to File…**) opens **Go to file**, on **Files**.

To switch tabs, click a tab or press **Shift+Tab**. In an empty field, you can also type **#** for **Todo**, **@** for **Files**, or **>** for **Commands**, and press **Backspace** to return to **Tasks**.

**Tasks** lists your tasks in the same groups as the Dashboard, with the one you're in marked **Current**. Type to narrow the list, or paste a Kepler task link. Press **Enter** to switch to the highlighted task, or **→** to search that task's files. Below the matches, 3 rows turn what you typed into something else:

- **Search files for “{query}”** searches every task's files for it.
- **New task: “{query}”** puts it in the **New task** composer.
- **Ask Kepler: “{query}”** starts an [Ask Kepler](/kepler/ask-kepler) chat with it.

**Files** searches the files of the task you're in, whose name shows as a pill at the end of the field. Before you type, it lists the files **Changed in this task**, then **Recent in this task**. Type a name, or a full path to open it. To search every task's files, click the pill's **×**.

**Todo** finds the pull requests and issues in your Todo by title, number, or pasted link. Its **Mine** and **All** switch sets which ones it searches. Press **Enter** to open the item's panel on the Dashboard.

**Commands** lists the commands you can run from where you are, each with its keyboard shortcut, and a row for each Settings page and for actions such as switching windows. Press **Enter** to run the highlighted command.

Each row has a menu of its actions, also on **Alt+Enter**. For how a file opens on the task page, see [The Task View](/kepler/task-view#opening-a-file).

***

## Back and forward

**Back** leaves the place or mode you're in. It does not undo a search you typed, a filter you set, or a change of layout. If you narrow the list and then press **Back**, you leave the list instead of stepping back through every keystroke.

Use these shortcuts to go back and forward:

| Command | Mac | Windows / Linux |
|---|---|---|
| **Back** | ⌘ [ | Alt + ← |
| **Forward** | ⌘ ] | Alt + → |

The **Back** and **Forward** buttons in the top bar do the same, and so do a mouse's side buttons. On macOS, a sideways swipe on a trackpad or Magic Mouse also goes back and forward. On Windows and Linux, a sideways scroll never goes back.

Each set of open panels gets its own history entry, so **Back** closes the set you just opened rather than the whole visit. Each Settings page you open gets its own entry too, so **Back** steps through the Settings pages you visited. To leave Settings in one step, use the back arrow in the Settings header, which returns you to what you were doing before you opened it.

***

## Empty states

When a view has nothing to show, or Kepler cannot load it, you see one of these messages:

| What you see | What it means |
|---|---|
| **Your agents' work lives here** | You have no tasks. **Tasks** shows the **New task** composer, plus an **Import from {app}** card if Kepler finds another agent app's work. See [Create a task](/kepler/create-task#from-another-agent-app) |
| **No tasks yet** | The tasks list is empty |
| **No assigned PRs or issues** | Providers are connected, but nothing related to you is open. Open **View** to see what the view's scope covers |
| **Nothing matches your search** | Your search excludes everything. Use **Clear search** beneath it |
| **Nothing matches these filters** | Your filters exclude everything. Use **Clear filters** beneath it |
| **Nothing here** | One column of the **Board** layout is empty |
| **Hand your issues and PRs to agents** | You have no provider connected. Connect one from the list |
| **Unable to load your work** | Every connected provider failed to load. The notice below names each fix, such as **Reconnect** or **Retry** |
| **Unable to load your issues and pull requests.** | Loading the whole list failed. Press **Retry** |
| **Sign in to see your assigned work** | Connect a GitKraken account to load your work |
| **Unable to find this task** | The task was deleted, or its link is from another machine |

### Kep

Kep, Kepler's planet mascot, appears on empty, loading and error screens. On a crash screen, **Show details** reveals **Error details**, with **Copy details** for a bug report.

Kep's eyes follow your pointer unless your system is set to reduce motion.

---

---
# Arranging Your Work
URL: https://help.gitkraken.com/kepler/arranging-your-work/
product: Kepler
feature: Kepler Interface
content_type: how-to
audience: developer
plan_required: all
status: GA
last_verified: 2026-11

Arrange the Dashboard so it shows the work you need to see. The Dashboard is a set of views, such as **Todo** and **Tasks**, and each view keeps its own arrangement. Above a view's list, the toolbar has these controls:

- **View** opens a menu that sets the layout (**List**, **Board**, or **Graph**), the grouping, the sort, and the filters.
- The search box finds items in the list, and also takes filters. See [Search](#search).
- **Panel layout** arranges open panels side by side in 1 row, or in a grid of several rows. See [Lay panels out in a grid](/kepler/kepler-interface#lay-panels-out-in-a-grid).
- **Refresh** fetches the view's items from your providers again.

What you choose in the **View** menu is saved to the view at once. To learn what each part of the screen is, see [The Kepler Interface](/kepler/kepler-interface).

To open several tasks at once, use the open button on a section header, or **Open group** on one of [your groups](#your-groups).

In a narrow window, the search box becomes a search icon. Click it, or press **Cmd/Ctrl+F**, to open the search box.

***

## Views

Each view lists one kind of work:

- A **Todo** view lists pull requests and issues from your connected providers.
- A **Tasks** view lists your tasks.

Kepler starts you with a **Todo** view, a **Tasks** view, and an **Agent Graph** view, which is a Tasks view in the **Graph** layout (see [Layouts](#layouts)). The views appear on every page. Click a view to open the Dashboard on it.

A view keeps its own layout, grouping, sort, filters, and search text. Every window shares the same views.

**A view's menu.** Click the view you are on, or right-click any view, to open its menu:

| Menu item | What it does |
|---|---|
| **Rename** (**F2**) | Renames the view. Double-clicking the name does the same |
| **Change icon** | Picks the view's icon |
| **Show counts on views** | Shows or hides task counts on every view |
| **View options** | Opens the **View** menu |
| **Duplicate view** | Adds a copy of the view with the same settings |
| **Move left**, **Move right** | Moves the view 1 place |
| **Views position** | Sets where the views sit |
| **Delete view** | Removes the view after a confirmation |

You cannot delete your last Todo view or your last Tasks view.

**Add a view.** Click **New view** after the views, then choose **Todo**, **Tasks**, **Agent Graph**, or **Duplicate current view**. Name the new view, set it up in the menu that opens, and choose **Done**.

**Reorder the views.** Drag a view to a new place, or use **Move left** and **Move right** in its menu. On the Dashboard, **Cmd/Ctrl+Shift+[** and **Cmd/Ctrl+Shift+]** show the previous or next view, and **Cmd+Option+[** and **Cmd+Option+]** (**Ctrl+Alt+[** and **Ctrl+Alt+]** on Windows and Linux) move the view you are on. See [Keyboard shortcuts](/kepler/settings-app#keyboard-shortcuts).

If the views run out of room, they fold into 1 button. Click it to see every view.

### Change a view's icon

To pick another icon for a view, open the view's menu and point to **Change icon**. Search for an icon or choose one from the grid. The first icon is the view type's default.

### Where the views sit

By default, the views sit in a row below the title bar. To move them, choose **Views position** in any view's menu, then **Title bar**, **Below title bar**, or **Left side**. On the left side, **Settings** moves to the foot of the column.

Along the left side, the views start as icons. To show their names, click **Expand views** at the foot of the column, or drag the column's edge. **Collapse views** returns to icons.

**Settings → Appearance → Dashboard** has the same choices, and also **View style**: **Tabs** or **Pills**. See [Dashboard settings](/kepler/settings-app#dashboard).

### Status and counts on views

A Tasks view shows its agents' most urgent state as a mark on its icon, using the same levels as the [tray icon](/kepler/kepler-interface#the-tray-icon), such as **Needs your answer**. Only the tasks that the view's filters keep count.

A view with filters also shows how many tasks match them. To hide the counts, turn off **Show counts on views** in any view's menu.

Hover a view to see its state, its task count, and its filters.

### Choose what a Todo view lists

A Todo view's **View** menu has a **Scope** switch:

- **Mine**, the default, lists work created by you, assigned to you, mentioning you, or awaiting your review.
- **All** lists everything open in Kepler's repos, plus your work elsewhere.

Under **All**, **Repos** and **Updated** choose which repositories and how recent the work is. See [The Dashboard's views](/kepler/kepler-interface#the-dashboards-views).

***

## Layouts

The layout switch at the top of the **View** menu sets how Kepler shows the view:

| Layout | What you get | Use it to |
|---|---|---|
| **List** | A compact list you read from top to bottom | Scan everything at once |
| **Board** | One column per section of the list | See how far along tasks are, and move tasks between stages |
| **Graph** | The Agent Graph of the view's tasks. Tasks views only | See what every agent is doing. See [The Agent Graph](/kepler/agent-graph) |

**List** is the default. Each view remembers its own layout, so a Todo view can show a list while a Tasks view shows a board. **List** and **Board** both use the view's grouping and filters.

**Board** shows the sections of the *current* grouping as columns side by side, so **Group by** sets what the columns are. When you group by **Progress**, the columns are the stages, from **Exploration** to **Done**, and they stay in place even when empty. **On hold**, **Later**, and **Archived** appear only when they hold a task, or while you drag a card. On every other grouping, Kepler hides empty sections, except your own groups.

When **Your groups** is on and another grouping is chosen, the **Board** becomes a grid. Each group is a row (a lane), and the grouping's sections are columns across every lane. See [Your groups](#your-groups).

All columns on the board have the same width. To resize them, use one of these methods:

- Drag the gap after any column. All columns resize at once.
- Focus the gap and press the arrow keys. **Home** sets the narrowest width and **End** the widest.
- Double-click the gap to return to the default width.

Each view remembers its own column width. When a column has more tasks to load, **Load more** appears at the bottom of the column. From the keyboard, **←** and **→** move to the nearest column that has a card.

<div class="note" markdown="1">

**Panel layout** arranges the panels you open, not the list. Its **Auto columns** are not the **Board** layout's columns.

</div>

On the board grouped by **Progress**, you can also move a task to another stage by hand. See [Set a task's progress](#set-a-tasks-progress).

**Graph** replaces the list instead of arranging it. While it is chosen, the **View** menu shows the graph's own controls in place of **Group by** and **Sort by**. See [The Agent Graph](/kepler/agent-graph).

***

## Group

**Group by** in the **View** menu divides the list into sections.

Each type of view has its own groupings:

| View | Group by | Default |
|---|---|---|
| **Todo** | Type, Needs my attention, Priority, Age, Your role, Assignee, Provider, Repository, Milestone, Status, None | Type |
| **Tasks** | Inbox, Progress, Activity, Repository, None, and the **Your groups** switch above them | Inbox |

On a Tasks view, the **Your groups** switch above **Group by** divides the list by groups you make yourself, either alone or with another grouping inside each group. See [Your groups](#your-groups).

### Inbox

**Inbox** is the default on Tasks views. It groups tasks by what each task needs from *you*, not by how far the work has progressed. Sections that need you come first, and the sections for work you have put away come last:

| Section | What it holds |
|---|---|
| **Needs attention** | Something waits on you, such as a question, an approval request, a failed turn, failing CI, or a review that requests changes |
| **Unread** | A session finished a turn you have not looked at, or a hold lifted |
| **Running** | An agent is working on it |
| **Important** | A task you starred with **Star** in its menu |
| **Recent** | Moved in the last 24 hours |
| **On hold** | You or an agent put it on hold. Starts folded |
| **Earlier** | Moved more than 24 hours ago. Starts folded |
| **Done** | Finished, waiting only on the decision to archive it |
| **Not started** | No session has started in it yet. Starts folded |
| **Later** | You or an agent set it aside for later. Starts folded |
| **Archived** | Tasks you archived. Starts folded |

A finished turn stays unread until you look at it.

To step through the tasks that need you in Inbox order, use **Go to next task needing attention**, **Go to next unread task**, or **Go to next task needing attention or unread**. Run them from the palette's **Commands** tab, or give them a key in [Keyboard shortcuts](/kepler/settings-app#keyboard-shortcuts). They have no key by default.

**Inbox** lists every task exactly once:

- A task that is both unread *and* blocked on you appears under **Needs attention**.
- A task under **Running** or **Done** appears only there, not also in a time section.
- A starred task lists under **Important** unless it needs you, is unread, is held, is running, or is done.

**Drop a card on an Inbox section.** To act on a task, drag its card onto another Inbox section:

| Drop on | What happens |
|---|---|
| **Unread** | Marks the task unread |
| **Recent** or **Earlier** | Marks an unread task read |
| **Important** | Stars the task |
| **On hold** or **Later** | Puts the task on hold, or sets it aside for later |
| **Done** | Marks the task done. Refused while an agent is still working |
| **Archived** | Opens the archive confirmation |

A section that refuses the card fades, and says why when you hover over it. To see what a drag looks like, see [Set a task's progress](#set-a-tasks-progress).

Tasks in **Running** keep their places while they work, so the list does not jump. Moves into **Unread** and **Needs attention** happen at once.

**On hold** and **Later** are for tasks you do not want to work on now, so a held task stays there even while an agent works on it. A held task still moves up when something needs you: an unread turn or a blocked prompt lists it under **Unread** or **Needs attention**.

### The other groupings

**Progress** and **Activity** group the same tasks in 2 different ways:

- **Progress** shows how far the work has progressed: **Exploration**, **In Development**, **In Review**, **On hold**, **Later**, **Done**, **Archived**. Group by Progress to see where each task is in your workflow.
- **Activity** shows what the task's agent sessions are doing now, from **Waiting** and **Error** down to **Idle** and **Ended**. A task lists under its most urgent session's state, or under **No sessions**, **Done**, or **Archived**. Group by Activity to see what needs a person.

**Repository** is the only grouping that can list a task twice. A task with worktrees in several repositories appears under each repository.

Tasks views have no Status grouping. A task's status is its progress stage, so group by **Progress** instead.

On Todo, **Needs my attention** groups each item by what it needs from you now, most urgent first, from **Ready to merge** and **Changes requested** down to **No action needed**. Each section header has a **?** button that explains what the section holds.

On Todo, **Priority** reads an item's priority from its labels, such as *P0* to *P4* or *urgent*. Kepler does not read a tracker's own priority field, so an issue with no priority label is **Unprioritised**, and every pull request goes under **Not applicable**.

**Age** groups by when an item was created: **Today**, **This week**, **This month**, **Older**, and **No date**. **Assignee** groups by who an item is assigned to on each provider, with **Unassigned** for the rest.

On Todo, **Milestone** groups items by their milestone, with open milestones before closed ones. Items with no milestone go under **No milestone**, and items from trackers without milestones, such as Jira, go under **No milestones**.

On Todo, **Status** groups issues by their tracker's own workflow state, such as a Linear *In Progress* or a Jira *To Verify*, instead of putting every open issue in one section.

Items with no repository or provider go under **No repository** and **No provider**. A pull request whose provider did not report its author goes under **Unattributed**. An issue goes under **Not applicable**, because issues have no author or reviewer role to group by.

### Your groups

The other groupings arrange tasks by what Kepler can see. A group is one you make yourself: a name and a color you give to tasks that belong together, such as the tasks for one feature or one release. A task can be in 1 group at a time, and groups are available only on Tasks views.

**Create a group.** The **New group** form asks for a **Group name** and a **Color**. Choose **Create group** to save the group. Each active group needs its own name, regardless of capitalization. You can reuse an archived group's name.

**Put tasks in a group.** You can add tasks to a group in 4 ways:

- **From a task's menu.** A task's **⋮** and right-click menus, on the Dashboard and on the task page, have **Add to group**. Its submenu lists your groups with their colors, with the task's current group checked. Below them, **New group…** opens the form with this task already in it, and **Remove from group** appears for a task that has a group. A task with sub-tasks also offers **Group with its {count} sub-tasks**, which opens the form with the task's name and with the task and its sub-tasks in it.
- **By dragging one task onto another.** Hold a dragged task over another task until a pill appears: **Create group**, or **Add to {group}** when that task has a group. Drop the task on the pill. **Create group** opens the form with both tasks in it. From the keyboard, use the menu.
- **From a selection.** Right-click inside a selection of 2 or more tasks and choose **New group with {count} tasks…**, **Add {count} tasks to group**, or **Remove {count} tasks from group**. See [Act on several tasks at once](#act-on-several-tasks-at-once).
- **By dropping into a group's section.** With the list grouped by your groups, drag a task into another group's section to move it there, or onto **Ungrouped** to remove it from its group.

To add an archived task to a group, restore the task first.

**See a task's group.** Under any grouping, a task in a group shows its group's color: a bar on the left edge of a **List** row, or a chip with the group's name after a **Board** card's title. Hover over the bar or chip to see the group's name and a summary of its tasks. Click it to open the group's menu without opening the task:

| Item | What it does |
|---|---|
| **Open group** | Opens every active task in the group in panels. Offered when the group has more than 1 |
| **Show only this group** | Sets the **Group** filter to this group |
| **Group by your groups** | Turns on the **Your groups** switch, keeping the current grouping inside each group |
| **Remove from group** | Takes this task out of the group |
| **Edit group…**, **Archive group**, **Delete group…** | Act on the group itself, as from its header (below) |

**Group the list by your groups.** Turn on the **Your groups** switch in the **View** menu:

- **With None chosen**, each group is a section, in your own order whatever the sort, followed by **Ungrouped** for tasks without a group. Each group's archived tasks are in a folded **Archived** section just after the group. A group with no tasks still has its section, so you can drop tasks into it.
- **With another grouping chosen**, such as **Inbox**, each group has its own sections of that grouping. On the **Board**, each group becomes a lane, and the grouping's sections become columns across every lane.

**A group's header.** Each group's header shows the group's color and name, then its count of active tasks and a dot for each state its tasks' sessions are in. A folded group therefore still shows whether something in it needs you. **Select** on a group header selects every task in the group.

To open the group's menu, right-click the header or click its **⋮**. The menu acts on the group, never on its tasks:

| Item | What it does |
|---|---|
| **Edit group…** | Renames the group or changes its color, in the same form |
| **Move group to top**, **Move group up**, **Move group down**, **Move group to bottom** | Moves the group in your order |
| **Manage groups…** | Opens **Settings → Tasks → Groups** (below) |
| **Archive group** | Archives the group. Offered only when every task in it is archived |
| **Delete group…** | Removes the group after a confirmation. Its tasks stay, ungrouped |
