You can also drag a group's header to move the group before or after another group. **Ungrouped**, and the sections inside a group, cannot be moved.

**Archive or delete a group.** When a group's work is done and every task in it is archived, archive the group. The group leaves the Dashboard, and you can reuse its name. If you restore one of its tasks, the group comes back too, and the task stays in it. Deleting a group never deletes its tasks. They stay where they are, without a group.

**Manage every group in Settings.** **Settings → Tasks → Groups** lists every group, including archived groups. There you can create, edit, reorder, restore, and delete groups. See [Groups](/kepler/settings-tasks#groups).

Agents can put tasks into groups too, through Kepler's workspace tools. See [What an agent can do with a task's resources](/kepler/tasks-and-resources#what-an-agent-can-do-with-a-tasks-resources).

### Fold a section

To fold or unfold a section, click its header. The header shows the section's count beside its name.

On the **Board** layout, a folded column shrinks to a narrow strip with its name and count, and is marked when it holds the open item. Click the strip to expand the column.

Some sections start folded:

- **Archived**, when you group by Activity or Inbox, because it holds work you have put away.
- **On hold**, **Earlier**, **Not started**, and **Later**, in the Inbox grouping.

Under **Your groups**, folding a group hides the sections inside it, and you can fold each of those sections separately too.

Kepler remembers folds across restarts, for each view and grouping. A section you folded stays folded, and a section you unfolded, such as **Archived**, stays open.

***

## Sort

**Sort by** in the **View** menu orders the items inside each section. It does not change the order of the sections, with 2 exceptions:

- **Repository** sections follow the sort, and each section's place depends on its first task.
- Your own groups always keep the order you gave them.

Each type of view has its own sort options:

| View | Sort by | Default |
|---|---|---|
| **Todo** | Updated, Created, Name, ID, Type | Updated |
| **Tasks** | Updated, Created, Name, Manual | Updated |

Dates sort newest first. **Name** and **ID** sort in ascending order. **ID** compares numbers by value, so *#9* comes before *#10*. **Type** puts pull requests before issues, with the most recent first within each. On a Tasks view, starred tasks come first in each section, except under **Manual**. Each view remembers its own sort.

### Put tasks in your own order

**Manual** sorts a Tasks view in an order you set yourself, inside each section, in any grouping, on **List** or **Board**. Each Tasks view keeps its own Manual order. To move a task, use one of these methods:

- Drag its row or card to a place in its own section. A line with a dot shows where it will land. Under **Manual**, a row shows a drag grip when you hover over it.
- Choose **Move up**, **Move down**, or **Move to top of {section}** from the task's **⋮** or right-click menu. These items appear only while the list is sorted by **Manual**.
- Drag one task of a selection to move all the selected tasks together. They land as one block, in the order they were listed. See [Act on several tasks at once](#act-on-several-tasks-at-once).

You do not have to switch to **Manual** first. If you drop a task in a new place in its own section while the list is sorted another way, Kepler saves the order you see, including your move, as the view's **Manual** order, and switches the sort to **Manual**. If you switch to **Manual** yourself, Kepler also keeps the current order, so no task changes place.

If the view already has a saved **Manual** order, a drop under another sort would replace it, so Kepler asks first. To keep the move, choose **Switch and replace Manual**. To put the task back, choose **Cancel**, press **Escape**, or click away.

***

## Set a task's progress

By default, Kepler sets a task's progress stage from its Git branches and pull requests (see [Status](/kepler/kepler-interface#status)). Sometimes Git and the pull requests do not show what you know. For example, a review was sent back, or the work was merged somewhere Kepler cannot see. In those cases, set the stage yourself.

You can set the stage in these ways:

- **The progress control.** Click the stage name on a task row, in the panel header, or in the task page header to open the **Progress** menu: **Automatic**, then each stage, **On hold**, and **Later**.
- **The task menus.** A task's **⋮** and right-click menus have the same choices under a **Progress** submenu, plus **Reopen** while the task is Done.
- **Drag a card.** In any grouping, on **List** or **Board**, drag a task's card or row. When grouped by **Progress**, drop it on another stage. On a touch screen, press and hold the card to pick it up. Press **Escape** to cancel the drag. If you drop the card in its own section, Kepler reorders it (see [Put tasks in your own order](#put-tasks-in-your-own-order)).
- **The Mark as bar.** While you drag, a **Mark as** bar appears over the toolbar with chips for what the card can become: **Read** or **Unread**, the stages, **On hold** and **Later**, **Reopen** for a Done task, and **Archive task**. For an archived task, it shows only **Restore**. Drop the card on a chip.
- **From the keyboard.** When a card has focus on the **Board** grouped by **Progress**, press **Cmd/Ctrl+Shift+←** or **Cmd/Ctrl+Shift+→** to move it 1 column. The card stops at **Exploration** and **Done**.

While you drag, each section that accepts the card has a dashed outline. Sections that do not accept it fade, and say why when you hover over them. On the **Board**, a folded column opens when you hold the card over it.

The control's tooltip says whether the stage *Updates as you work* or was *Set manually*.

**How a stage you set works with Git.** Kepler keeps a stage you set until Git and the pull requests catch up with it or change. Then Kepler sets the stage from them again:

- If you set a stage *ahead* of Git and the pull requests (**Done** before the merge, or **In Review** before the pull request), the stage stays until they reach it.
- If you set a stage *behind* them (**Reopen**, or a review sent back to **In Development**), the stage stays until they change in any way. A reopened task therefore still follows its next pull request.
- To return the task to automatic stages sooner, choose **Automatic**, or drop its card on the column that Git and the pull requests already show.

**Reopen** on a task you marked Done returns it to the stage that Git and the pull requests show. If Git and the pull requests show the task as finished, **Reopen** sets **In Development**, and the task's next pull request moves it forward again.

Dropping a card on **Archived** opens the archive confirmation. Dragging an archived card to another section restores the task first. An archived task's control reads **Archived** as a plain label, with no menu.

Agents can also set the stage, put a task on hold until a condition, or set it aside for later, through Kepler's workspace tools. If an agent lifts a hold you placed, it tells you.

### Hold a task, or set it aside for later

**On hold** and **Later** both put a task aside without changing its stage. Choosing any stage or **Automatic** lifts either one, and so does the task reaching **Done**.

- **On hold** is a pause. The task's agents keep running, and the hold can lift by itself when something happens.
- **Later** sets the task aside for longer. It stops the task's running agents but keeps their sessions, so you can resume them. **Later** never lifts by itself.

**Hold until something happens.** **On hold** in the **Progress** menu opens a submenu:

| Choice | The hold lifts |
|---|---|
| **Indefinitely** | Only when you lift it |
| **Until CI finishes** | When CI on the task's pull request finishes |
| **Until a review arrives** | When someone reviews the pull request |
| **Until the pull request merges or closes** | When the pull request is merged or closed |
| **Until another task is done** | When the task you pick reaches **Done** |
| **For 1 hour**, **For 3 hours** | After that long |
| **Until tomorrow**, **Until next week** | At 9:00 the next morning, or at 9:00 next Monday |
| **Until a custom date...** | At the date and time you choose, up to a year away |

The pull request rows need an open or draft pull request linked to the task. When the task has several, each pull request row opens a submenu: wait on **All running pull requests** for CI, or **Any pull request** for a review or a merge, or pick one pull request.

While a task waits, its row says what for, such as *On hold until CI finishes on #51*. When the hold lifts, the row says why, such as *Back from hold: CI passed*. A hold that lifts on bad news, such as failed CI, lists the task under **Needs attention**. Any other reason lists it under **Unread**.

***

## Filter

The **Filters** section at the end of the **View** menu has a submenu for each facet, such as **Progress** or **Provider**.

Each type of view has these facets:

| View | Facets |
|---|---|
| **Todo** | Needs my attention · Review requests · Your role · Type · Linked work · Status · Priority · Age · Provider, then one section per connection with its own Repository · Assignee · Author · Reviewer · Issue type · Label · Project · Milestone · Iteration or Sprint |
| **Tasks** | Progress · Activity · Repository · Agent · Session · Group · Linked work |

Facets with a fixed set of values, such as **Progress** or **Priority**, always list every value, even one that nothing matches. Other facets list only the values in your work, and Kepler hides a facet that has no values to choose from. For example, if you work in a single repository, the menu has no Repository facet.

GitHub Enterprise and GitLab Self-Hosted get sections of their own, apart from GitHub and GitLab. If you connect 2 servers of one provider, each section's heading names its host, such as *GitHub Enterprise · ghe.example.com*. **Milestone** appears for providers that have milestones, such as GitHub, GitLab, and Linear.

**Issue type**, **Label**, **Project**, and **Iteration** use your provider's own values (a Jira issue type, your team's labels, a board name), not Kepler's own names for them. Azure DevOps calls the last one **Iteration** and Jira calls it **Sprint**, so the facet uses each tracker's word.

**Linked work** filters by whether an item is connected to work in the other type of view:

- In Todo, it filters each pull request or issue by its task history: *Has an active task*, *Archived tasks only* (worked on before, but every task is archived), or *No tasks ever*.
- In Tasks, it offers *Has a PR or issue*.

**Activity** matches a task when *any* of its sessions is in that state, so a task with one running session and one unread session matches both **Running** and **Unread**.

**Session** offers *Has a session* and *Has a live session*. To find tasks *without* a pull request, issue, or session, exclude the value.

**Group** lists each of [your groups](#your-groups), including empty ones, and **Ungrouped** for tasks without a group. When the list is grouped by your groups, the facet also limits which group sections appear.

**Include or exclude any value.** Click a value to include it. To exclude a value instead, hover over it and click its minus button, or press **Shift+Enter** from the keyboard. An excluded value reads *not {value}*. On Todo, excluding a provider's value removes only that provider's items, so excluding a GitHub label never hides a Jira issue.

**Values you include in one facet are combined.** If you tick GitHub *and* GitLab under **Provider**, the list shows items from either provider. Excluded values remove items: Kepler hides an item that matches any of them. A facet with nothing chosen reads **Any** and does not narrow the list.

To find a value in a long facet, type in its **Search filters…** box. The filters you choose also show in the search box, and you can type them there instead. See [Filter from the search box](#filter-from-the-search-box). When a narrow window folds the search box into an icon, the **View** button counts the filters instead. Hover over the button to see them.

To fetch the current view from your providers again, click **Refresh**.

***

## Search

The search box finds items by **title, reference, or repository**, and finds tasks by their branch names too. Each word you type matches on its own, in any order, so *login kepler* finds a *Fix login* task in the kepler repository. Put a word or phrase in quotes to match whole words only: *"log"* leaves out *login*.

To find one task, paste its link (**Copy task link**) into the search box. A session's link (**Copy session link**) finds the task that holds the session.

The search box fills the free space in the toolbar. To have it grow only as you type, set **Search box** to **Grows as you type** in [Settings → Appearance → Dashboard](/kepler/settings-app#dashboard).

When a search or a filter narrows the list, pills at the right end of the search box show how many rows are left or hidden. Each pill clears only its own search or filters:

| Pill | What it counts | Clicking it |
|---|---|---|
| The search pill | The rows on screen out of every row: *{count} of {total}* | Clears the search |
| The filter pill | The rows your filters hide: *{count} hidden* | Clears the filters |

While a search is on, the filter pill counts only hidden rows that match the search. If a search seems to miss something, the filter pill shows whether your filters are hiding it. Todo loads in pages, so its counts read *40+* or *7+ hidden* until everything has loaded.

When nothing matches, the empty list offers a button that clears the search, the filters, or both.

Search covers only the work the view has already loaded. On a Todo view, that is the work its scope lists. See [Choose what a Todo view lists](#choose-what-a-todo-view-lists).

### Filter from the search box

The search box also takes the view's filters, written as qualifiers such as `activity:waiting` or `type:pr`, beside your search words. As you type, it suggests filters, then their values with their counts. A filter you set in the **View** menu appears in the box as a qualifier, and a qualifier you type sets the filter. When you type a qualifier:

- Put **-** before a qualifier to exclude its value, such as `-progress:done`.
- Put a name with spaces in quotes, such as `group:"Release work"`.
- On a Tasks view, `branch:` filters by branch name.

A qualifier that can match nothing is underlined. Hover over it to see why, such as a group name that does not exist.

***

## What Kepler remembers

Each view keeps its layout, grouping, sort, filters, search text, and, on Todo, its scope, in every window and across restarts. In each window, each view also remembers its open panels and their layout, its folded sections, and where you scrolled to. If you switch to another view and back, the panels you were reading are still open.

After a restart, each window reopens on the view it was showing, with that view's panels. The window's other views start with no panels open.

***

## Archive, restore, and clean up in bulk

**Archive task** puts a task away. The task moves from its current section to **Archived**, and Kepler stops its running agents. Its sessions and resources are kept, so you can resume them later. With **Also delete worktrees** ticked, archiving ends the task's agents instead, and closes the Kepler terminals open in those worktrees.

When a task meets all of these conditions, the preview header and the task page header suggest archiving it, with *Ready to archive?* and an **Archive** button:

- The task is at **Done**.
- None of its worktrees has unpushed work.
- No agent is working or waiting on you.
- No session is running background work, such as a dev server.

**Archive** opens the usual confirmation. The **X** dismisses the suggestion for that task in every window.

The confirmation offers the same options as deleting a task: **Also delete worktrees**, **Also delete branches** (after you tick **Also delete worktrees**), and **Also delete the branch on the remote** (after you tick **Also delete branches**). You can therefore remove a finished task's worktrees and branches from disk without deleting the task. With **Also delete worktrees** ticked, the dialog lists each worktree with what will happen to it, such as *2 uncommitted files*, and names the worktrees it keeps, such as the repository's main worktree. Kepler keeps a worktree that would lose work unless you tick the extra box that names what would be lost. To check before you decide, open the changes from the row of a worktree at risk.

With **Also delete the branch on the remote** ticked, Kepler also deletes each branch's remote copy, unless that would lose work, such as a branch with an open pull request or commits that are not on the remote. A message says which branches it kept, and why.

**Archived** takes priority over every other section, so an archived task stays in **Archived** even if a shell is still open on it.

**Restore task** replaces **Archive task** in an archived task's **⋮** menu, and also appears in the task page's header. It restores the task at once, without asking, even when another active task holds the same pull request (several tasks can share one). A restored task stays in its group, and if that group was archived, Kepler restores the group too.

To archive, restore or delete several tasks at once, click **Select** on a section header in a Tasks view. The header becomes a bar with a select-all box and the actions, and the section's rows show checkboxes. You can select in 1 section at a time, and while you select, clicking a row ticks it instead of opening its panel.

The bar has these buttons:

| Button | What it does |
|---|---|
| **Archive** | Archives every selected task that is not already archived |
| **Restore** | Replaces **Archive** when every selected task is already archived |
| **Delete** | Deletes the selected tasks permanently |
| **Cancel** | Ends selection and clears the selection |

**Archive** and **Delete** both ask you to confirm, with **Archive tasks** or **Delete tasks** as the confirm button. Both offer **Also delete worktrees**, **Also delete branches**, and **Also delete the branch on the remote**. Deleting cannot be undone, and the confirmation says so. The batch confirmation differs from the single-task dialog in 2 ways:

- The single-task dialog remembers what you ticked last time. The batch confirmation always starts with all 3 boxes unticked.
- The batch confirmation does not list what will happen to each worktree. Instead, Kepler keeps any worktree that would lose work, and a message afterwards says which ones and why. To see the list before you confirm, use the task's own **⋮** menu.

### Act on several tasks at once

The tasks you open with **Shift**-click or **Cmd/Ctrl**-click (see [Open a panel](/kepler/kepler-interface#open-a-panel)) are also a selection you can act on. While 2 or more tasks are selected, right-clicking or dragging any one of them acts on all of them. Right-clicking or dragging a task outside the selection acts on that task only. A row's **⋮** always acts on its own row.

Right-clicking inside the selection opens a selection menu instead of the task menu, and each item counts the tasks it acts on. With it you can set the progress of every selected task, mark them read or unread, star or unstar them, group or ungroup them, shut down their agents, and archive, restore or delete them. **Shut down agents** asks first while an agent is still working. The group and **Progress** items skip archived tasks. **Archive**, **Restore**, and **Delete** open the same batch confirmation as a section's **Select** bar. For the full menu, see [Task rows](/kepler/kepler-interface#task-rows).

Dragging a selected task drags the whole selection. Each drop target says how many of the tasks it accepts. After the drop, Kepler reports how many tasks moved and how many stayed where they were. Under the **Manual** sort, the tasks land together as one block.

To clean up worktrees and local branches instead of tasks, open **Settings → Repositories** and choose **Manage worktrees and branches**. The **Worktrees and branches** page lists every worktree, and every local branch that no worktree has checked out. You can filter the list by **Safe to delete**, **Needs update**, **Conflicts**, **Stale**, or **All**. On this page, you can:

- **Update** several worktrees at once, which brings each branch up to date with its base.
- Delete worktrees and branches, including their copies on the remote.

See [Settings](/kepler/settings-repositories#worktrees-and-branches).

---

---
# Actions
URL: https://help.gitkraken.com/kepler/actions/
product: Kepler
feature: Actions
content_type: how-to
audience: developer
plan_required: all
status: GA
last_verified: 2026-11

An **Action** is a named prompt you fire at a task, issue, or pull request to start agent work.

You can change every Action's wording and agent, and choose which Action each kind of work suggests as its one-click default. An [automation](/kepler/automations) can also run an Action for you, on a schedule or when new GitHub or Jira activity matches its query.

***

## The four built-in Actions

Kepler comes with 4 Actions, and you can edit each of them.

| Action | What it asks the agent to do | Available on |
|---|---|---|
| **Plan** | Research the code first, write out the proposed approach, change nothing, and wait for your confirmation | Tasks, Issues, Pull requests |
| **Implement** | Read enough surrounding code to be confident, then make the changes directly rather than describing them | Tasks, Issues, Pull requests |
| **Review** | Review the pull request if one is attached, otherwise the uncommitted work in the worktree | Tasks, Pull requests |
| **Address Feedback** | Triage the review comments, apply what's worth applying, and push back on the rest instead of applying every suggestion blindly | Pull requests |

**Address Feedback** never appears on a task with no pull request.

You can edit and reset built-in Actions, but you cannot delete them.

***

## Where the Action button appears

You fire Actions from a **split button**. The left half runs the Action suggested for that surface; the chevron opens the full list.

<div class="table-center" markdown="1">

| Surface | Suggested Action comes from |
|---|---|
| A row in **Todo** (an issue or pull request) | the row's own kind of item |
| The side panel, on the selected item | the selected item's kind |

</div>

Firing an Action from a Todo row is also how an issue or pull request that is not tracked yet **becomes** a task in Kepler.

On a narrow card, the button shrinks to a play icon. On a phone, a row has a single **⋮** menu instead that lists every Action.

In the list of Actions, hover a row, or move focus to it, to read that Action's prompt.

Inside a task, Actions are under the **chevron on the composer's send button**: type a refinement, then pick the Action to fire it with. In a composer that starts something new, such as the **New task** composer or a panel's draft, picking an Action does not fire it. It sets the main button to that Action, and the agent pill shows the Action's own agent, if it names one. See [Create a task](/kepler/create-task#from-the-new-task-composer).

Task rows do not carry an Action button. A task's own operations are in the **⋮** menu on its row.

***

## Firing an Action

An Action runs at once, unless Kepler needs you to choose where it runs.

### The left half: one click

The left half of the button runs the suggested Action straight away, in the current session if one exists. It stops to ask only when the task has **2 or more worktrees**.

The number of issues or pull requests attached to the task does not change what the Action does. Kepler sends the Action's prompt word for word, and every attached item reaches the agent as shared context. To have the agent look at one item first, say so in the prompt box or in the chat.

### The chevron: the deliberate path

An Action you pick from the chevron list asks where to run it whenever there is a choice, even between a new session and the current one.

At the bottom of the list, **Manage Actions…** opens **Settings → Actions**.

From the keyboard, the two halves are separate **Tab** stops, the Action first. **Down Arrow** or **Alt+Down** on the Action opens the list too, and closing the list puts focus back on the Action. Every split button in Kepler (**Send**, **Open in**, **Run**) works the same way.

### Choosing where it runs

The **Run in** view asks 2 separate questions.

**New session, or a current one?** A two-way toggle between **New session** and **Current session**. *Current session* lists every reusable session with its worktree, so clicking a row queues the Action into that exact session.

**Which worktree?** In *New session*, the rows are **All N worktrees**, **A new worktree**, and then one row per branch. In *Current session*, individual sessions replace branches that already have sessions.

Clicking any row **runs the Action** immediately, with no separate confirm step.

When an Action runs on several worktrees, Kepler takes you to the first one you picked. Under *Current session*, a worktree with no open session gets a new one, so **All N worktrees** always means all of them.

A task with no worktree runs the Action in a folder attached to it, or else in the task's own folder. With neither, Kepler tells you it has nowhere to start a session.

### Firing into a running session

Firing into a live session **queues** the prompt behind whatever the agent is currently doing. Nothing is dropped and nothing is canceled, and Kepler takes you to the session the prompt went into.

***

## Set your suggested Actions

To choose the Action each kind of item suggests, open **Settings → Actions → Suggested Actions**.

Each row sets the Action that the left half of the button runs for that kind of item.

<div class="table-center" markdown="1">

| Setting | Default |
|---|---|
| **Tasks** | Implement |
| **Issues** | Plan |
| **Pull requests I authored** | Address Feedback |
| **Pull requests from others** | Review |

</div>

Pull requests split by **who wrote them**, not by what you want to do with them. When you want the other Action, it is one click away in the chevron.

To show only the chevron on the button for a kind of item, set its slot to **None**.

**Suggest automatically**, below the pickers, is on by default. When you link an issue or pull request to a new task, the composer's button switches to that item's suggested Action, and anything you type is added to the Action's prompt. Turn it off to keep **Start**.

***

## Edit an Action

To edit an Action, go to **Settings → Actions** and click the Action's row under **All Actions**. The editor opens as its own page.

Each row shows what the Action does and where it is available. Once you have a custom Action, the list splits into **Built in** and **Custom**.

The editor has these fields:

| Field | What it does |
|---|---|
| **Title** | Required. The name shown on the button and in the chevron list |
| **Prompt** | Required. Sent to the agent word for word, and can be or start with one of your skills: type **/** (or **$** for Codex) to pick one |
| **Available on** | Where the Action is offered: **Tasks**, **Issues**, **Pull requests**, or several. Pick at least one |
| **Agent** | Which agent runs it. See below |

### Create your own

To create an Action, click **New Action** in **Settings → Actions**.

Custom Actions work exactly like the built-in ones. Make one for any prompt you would otherwise retype, such as backporting a fix, writing a migration, or auditing a dependency bump.

#### Example: Prepare for review

This Action asks the agent to gather the evidence a reviewer needs before you read the diff, so you start from what the agent did and what it did not check. To create it, click **New Action** in **Settings → Actions** and fill in the following fields:

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| **Title** | Prepare for review |
| **Available on** | **Tasks** |
| **Agent** | **Use default agent**, or a preset for a different agent from the one that wrote the code |

Use the following text for **Prompt**:

```text
Before I review this work, write a review summary in this session. Include:
- What the change is supposed to do, in one or two sentences
- Each file you changed, and why
- The commands you ran to test the change, and their results
- What you didn't test, and anything you're unsure about
Don't change any files.
```

The summary is the agent's own account. Check it against the diff in [Review Changes](/kepler/review-changes) before you commit.

#### Example: Open a pull request

Kepler has no "create pull request" button, so the agent or you open one. This Action has the agent open it, with a note in the description that an agent helped write the change. Fire it after you've reviewed and committed the work. To create it, click **New Action** in **Settings → Actions** and fill in the following fields:

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| **Title** | Open a pull request |
| **Available on** | **Tasks** |
| **Agent** | **Use default agent** |

Use the following text for **Prompt**:

```text
Push this worktree's branch and open a pull request against its base branch.
Write a title and a description that say what changed and why.
End the description with this line:
"An AI coding agent helped write this change, and a person reviewed it."
If the worktree has uncommitted changes, stop and tell me.
```

The agent opens the pull request with the tools it has, such as your Git host's command-line tool. When it publishes the pull request, Kepler attaches it to the task. See [Review Changes](/kepler/review-changes#opening-a-pull-request).

### Restore defaults

To undo your edits to one Action, click **Restore default** on its row. The row shows **Restore default** only after you edit the Action. To undo your edits to every Action at once, click **Restore all defaults** in the **All Actions** section header.

An Action you have never edited picks up new default wording when Kepler updates. **Restore default** discards your edit.

Deleting a custom Action that a suggested-Action slot points to sets that slot to **None**, so its rows show only the chevron. To pick a new suggested Action, go back to **Settings → Actions → Suggested Actions**.

You cannot delete an Action that an automation runs. Delete the automation first; see [Automations](/kepler/automations#manage-an-automation).

***

## Setting an Action's agent

By default an Action runs on your **default agent**, configured in **Settings → Tasks → New tasks → Default agent**. To change it, open the **Preset** list in the editor's **Agent** field and pick one of the following:

| Choice | What the Action runs on |
|---|---|
| **Use default agent** | Your default agent configuration |
| A preset, shown as **{preset} · {agent}** | That preset's agent, with its model, mode, and options. If that agent has more than 1 account, pick the account below the list |
| **Custom agent settings** | The agent, model, and mode you set for this Action alone |

You save agent presets in **Settings → Agents → Agent presets**; see [Settings](/kepler/settings-agents#agent-presets). For example, pick a cheap, fast preset for triage and review, and a heavier one for implementation. If an Action's preset no longer exists, the Action shows **Preset unavailable for this agent**.

An [automation](/kepler/automations) runs its Action unattended, on issue and pull request text that other people write. If an automation uses the Action, choose a mode that acts without asking only if you trust everyone who can open or comment on those items.

**Custom agent settings** is an **all-or-nothing override**: it pins the provider, account, model, mode, and options together, rather than changing one of them and inheriting the rest.

Three rules govern which agent actually runs:

- A model belongs to its provider, so a pinned model never runs on a different agent.
- If an Action names an agent you do not have installed, the override falls back **whole** to your default agent.
- **An agent you pick explicitly at the point of firing beats an Action's override.**

### Review with a different agent

You can have one agent write the code and a different agent review it. A reviewer that did not write the code is less likely to repeat the author's mistakes.

To give **Review** its own agent, take the following steps:

1. Go to **Settings → Actions**, and click **Review** under **All Actions**.
2. In the **Agent** field, pick a preset for a different agent from the one that writes your code, or choose **Custom agent settings** and pick that agent. **Implement** uses your default agent unless you've changed it.
3. Click **Save**.

**Review** now runs on that agent, whether you fire it at a task's uncommitted work or at an attached pull request, with the model and mode you chose for it.

To use a different reviewer just once, pick the agent when you fire **Review**. An agent you pick at that point beats the Action's override.

The review is a report, not an approval. You read it in the session and decide what to change before you commit.

---

---
# Tasks and Resources
URL: https://help.gitkraken.com/kepler/tasks-and-resources/
product: Kepler
feature: Tasks
content_type: concept
audience: developer
plan_required: all
status: GA
last_verified: 2026-11

A **task** is the unit of work in Kepler. It is one thing you want to get done, plus everything the agents working on it need: the repositories, the issue or pull request it came from, the branches, the notes, and every agent session you have run on it.

You can start a task with as much or as little as you have:

- Start a task from an issue in [the Kepler interface](/kepler/kepler-interface), and it opens with the repository and the issue body already attached.
- Start a task with nothing attached (no repository, no branch) to explore an idea, and attach the repositories and issues later.

***

## What a task holds

Everything attached to a task is a **resource**.

To see and change what a task holds, use one of these controls on the task page:

- **Manage resources**, at the bottom of the context panel or in the **Task actions** (**⋮**) menu, opens the **Resources** screen.
- The **+** on a group header in the context panel opens the same screen on that kind's tab.

The **Resources** screen has a tab for each kind of resource: **Repos & folders**, **Issues**, **Pull requests**, **Notes**, **Links** and **Files**. Each tab lists what the task already holds, above the way to add more. Everything you add goes onto the task at once.

A task can hold these kinds of resource:

| Resource | What it is |
|---|---|
| **Sessions** | Agent conversations that run on this task |
| **Terminals** | Shells opened in one of the task's working directories |
| **Worktrees** | Git working copies that the agents change. The context panel lists them under **Changes** |
| **Folders** | A directory that is not a Git repository, which the agent works on in place. If you later make it a Git repository, the task lists it under **Changes** |
| **Files** | A single file, when you need the file rather than its whole folder. A file is either linked from disk by its path or uploaded to the task as a copy |
| **Pull requests** | Pull requests from your connected Git hosts |
| **Issues** | Issues from your connected trackers |
| **Links** | Any URL you want to keep with the work |
| **Notes** | Text you write, such as standing instructions, decisions and reference material. The task's own **Prompt** is the first item in this group |

A task can hold **more than one** of each kind. For example, a task can span 3 repositories and link 2 issues.

To learn how the task page is laid out (the context panel, columns, split panes and tabs), see [the task page](/kepler/task-view).

### Picking issues and pull requests

The **Issues** and **Pull requests** tabs first list the items already on the task. To add more, click **Add issues** or **Add pull requests** to search the work on your connected providers.

The scope filter sets which items the list shows:

| Scope | What it lists |
|---|---|
| **Related to me** | Items you authored, are assigned, or were mentioned in or asked to review |
| **All in my repos** | Every open item in the repositories added to Kepler |
| **All visible** | Issues only: your GitHub and Azure organizations, or a Jira or Linear project or team you pick |

To add an item, select its row and click **Add**, press **Enter**, or double-click the row. **Remove** takes it off again.

To see more about an item before you add it, click **Show preview** in the screen's header, or press **Cmd/Ctrl+Alt+P**.

You can use the list from the keyboard:

| Key | What it does |
|---|---|
| **↓** from the search field | Moves into the list |
| **↑** / **↓**, **Home** / **End** | Moves between rows |
| **Enter** | Adds the focused row |

### Pasting an issue link

To add a link, click **Add link** on the **Links** tab, paste a URL, and press **Enter**. To change a web link's label later, click the pencil on its row, or press **F2**.

When you paste an issue's URL, Kepler looks up the issue and adds the link as that issue, under its title. To add it as a plain link anyway, click **Add as plain link**. If Kepler cannot find the issue, it adds a plain link instead.

### Files: linked or uploaded

The **Files** group holds 2 kinds of file. Kepler removes them differently, because it owns only the uploaded copy:

| Kind | Where it lives | Its row reads | Removing it |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Linked file** | Where it already was on disk. Kepler links to it by its path and never changes it | Its path | **Detach file…** leaves the file where it is |
| **Uploaded copy** | In the task's own folder. It belongs to this task only | **Task folder** | **Delete file…** deletes the copy |

To add a file, click **Add file** on the **Files** tab of the **Resources** screen and pick it. Kepler attaches it at once and opens its description, so you can tell agents what it is for. To edit a file's description later, or an uploaded copy's name, click the pencil on its row, or press **F2**.

Other ways files reach a task:

- When you attach a file to a prompt, Kepler copies it into the task when you send the prompt. That copy is an uploaded copy too.
- In a window connected to another machine, the **Files** tab also offers **Upload from this machine**, which copies files from the machine you are using.

To save either kind of file somewhere else, choose **Save as…** from its menu.

### Issues and pull requests attach themselves

You do not have to attach a task's pull request yourself. If a task holds no pull request yet, and one of its worktrees is on a branch that exactly matches an open pull request's head branch, Kepler attaches that pull request to the task. This works however the pull request was opened, including from a terminal, from GitKraken, or on the web.

Automatic attachment follows these rules:

- The branch names must match exactly. A similar name does not match.
- The pull request must be yours: one you opened, or one whose head is the branch your worktree pushes to. A teammate's pull request on a branch with the same name is not attached.
- Kepler attaches only open pull requests whose head branch is in the same repository. A pull request from a fork is never attached automatically.
- Kepler attaches a pull request even when another active task already holds it. Several tasks can share 1 pull request, and attaching it to one task never archives it or detaches it from the other.

**Issues attach the same way.** When an issue's branch matches one of the task's checkouts, Kepler attaches the issue. A task you start from a branch name therefore gets the issue behind that branch.

Automatic attachment only adds links. It never removes one. To remove a link you do not want on the task, detach it.

**Work item URLs attach as issues.** When you or an agent attaches one of the following URLs, Kepler records it as an issue rather than a plain link:

- A GitLab work item, such as `https://gitlab.com/{group}/{project}/-/work_items/{number}`
- An Azure DevOps work item, such as `https://dev.azure.com/{organization}/{project}/_workitems/edit/{id}`, or the organization-level `https://dev.azure.com/{organization}/_workitems/edit/{id}`

A GitLab work item that belongs to a group rather than a project stays a plain link.

### Keeping them current

Kepler refreshes a task's pull requests and issues when they could have changed, such as when an agent ends a turn or someone pushes one of the task's branches. A Jira or Linear issue that moves to a new key stays attached.

To refresh by hand, click the refresh button on the **Pull requests** or **Issues** group header, or choose **Refresh** in the task's **⋮** menu.

***

## Worktrees and working in place

A **worktree** is a private Git working copy for one task. Agents make their changes in the worktree, so nothing they do touches the checkout you work in, and several agents can run at once without changing each other's files. Use a worktree for most work.

To add a repository to a task, open the **Repos & folders** tab of the **Resources** screen, and click **Add repos or folders** if the task already holds some. Select a repository's row to open a confirm line under it. Its chip says how the task gets the repository, such as **New worktree from {base}**, and a button such as **Create worktree** adds it. A folder's row has an **Add** that adds it at once.

The chip's menu holds the **Isolated worktree** toggle, which sets whether the task gets a worktree, and the branch choice. The **New task** composer offers the same choice. See [Create a task](/kepler/create-task#configuring-a-repository).

| Setting | What it means |
|---|---|
| **On** | The task gets its own folder, and nothing else can switch its branch |
| **Off** | The task uses your repository folder, so anything that switches the branch there switches it for the task too |

If the branch you picked is already checked out somewhere, Git cannot check it out a second time. The toggle locks and says where the task will work instead.

> **With isolation off, the task has no branch of its own.** The task uses your repository folder exactly as it is. Kepler copies nothing and protects nothing. Turn isolation off only when you want an agent to work in your own checkout. Otherwise, leave it on.

Kepler always isolates a repository linked to a pull request, and locks the toggle.

When you attach the repository, you can also pick the branch:

- **Use this branch** works directly on an existing branch.
- **New branch** creates a branch from the repository's default branch.

Each option says where the work will happen. Kepler names a new branch for you unless you set a name. To fetch the latest branches from your remotes, click **Refresh branches**, beside **Find a branch…**.

**A new branch starts from the repository's remote default branch**, not from the branch you have checked out. To start from another branch, name a base yourself:

- A local base starts from its upstream.
- If the local base has commits you have not pushed, the new branch starts from your local tip instead, so it includes those commits.

With no remote default branch available, the new branch starts from your current commit.

**Starting a session brings an older worktree up to date.** When you start a session in an existing worktree whose branch has no changes or commits of its own and is not published, Kepler first moves the branch up to its merge target. Kepler never moves a branch that holds work.

Kepler suggests branch names from the task's own context. A suggested name starts with the issue identifier when the task has one, and sits under the `kepler/` prefix unless you configure another prefix. See [Create a task](/kepler/create-task#naming-the-branch).

**A task does not require a worktree, or even a repository.** Attach a plain folder, and the agent works on it in place. Attach nothing, and you have a space to explore an idea. You can attach repositories and other resources later, when you are ready to start the work.

### When a worktree goes missing

A worktree deleted outside Kepler **stays bound to its task**, so the task keeps its record of where the work was, even after a `git worktree prune`. The row is flagged **Gone from disk**, and the pane shows the details Kepler recorded: **Current branch**, **Base branch**, and **Recorded path**.

To bring the worktree back, click **Recreate worktree** on the pane, or choose it from the worktree's menu. Kepler recreates the worktree at the recorded path. If the branch was deleted too, Kepler restores the branch where it can, otherwise recreates it from its base, and tells you which.

An attached folder that was removed stays on the task the same way. If you start a new session in a worktree or folder that is gone, Kepler asks first, then rebuilds it before the session starts. A task with no repository or folder starts its sessions in the task's own folder.

### Make a new worktree ready to build

A new worktree is a clean checkout. It has no `node_modules`, no build output, and none of the files your setup script would normally create. An agent that starts there has to install dependencies first, or its first build fails.

To prepare new worktrees automatically, use **Commands**. Save a repository's setup steps once, such as `pnpm install` or a code generation step, and tick **Run on worktree creation**. Each time Kepler creates a worktree for that repository, it runs those commands in order in the new worktree's folder, before the agent starts. To run a command that is not set to run on creation, right-click a worktree in the context panel and choose **Run command here**.

**Copy ignored files such as `.env` into new worktrees.** A new worktree has none of the Git-ignored files in your checkout. List the ones a worktree needs in a `.worktreeinclude` file at the repository's root, in `.gitignore` syntax. Kepler copies the matching files from your checkout into each new worktree, before any **Run on worktree creation** command runs, and never overwrites a file that is already there. Lines that start with `!` are skipped.

The worktree's menu has the same entries wherever the worktree appears:

- **Run command here**, **New session here**, which opens a draft session in that worktree, and **New terminal here**.
- The **Branch** submenu, with **Rename branch**, the upstream, **Change merge target…**, and **Rebase onto {target}** or **Merge {target} into this branch**. For the upstream and updating the branch, see [Review Changes](/kepler/review-changes#publishing-and-syncing-the-branch).
- The copy actions, **Refresh**, **Detach worktree…** and **Delete worktree…**.

To set up commands, open **Settings → Repositories** and go to the repository's own page. See [Settings](/kepler/settings-repositories#per-repository-commands) for the fields, the **Variables** a command can use, and what happens when one fails.

### What a worktree does not separate

A worktree gives each task its own copy of the files, but nothing else. Tasks still share everything outside the worktree's folder:

- **Ports.** Two worktrees that start the same dev server on the same port collide, and the second server fails to start.
- **Databases and other local services.** Agents in different worktrees that point at the same database read and write the same data.
- **Caches and files outside the repository.** A global package cache or a file in your home folder is the same for every worktree.

To keep tasks apart, give each worktree its own settings when Kepler creates it. Add a per-repository command that runs on worktree creation and writes those settings, such as a port or a database name, into a local config file in the new worktree. The command runs in the new worktree's folder, and its **Variables** menu can insert the worktree's path. See [Settings](/kepler/settings-repositories#per-repository-commands).

***

## Shared context: how resources reach your agents

Kepler sends everything attached to a task to **every agent session in the task** as *shared context*: the task's prompt, the issue body, the pull request, your notes and the links. When a prompt refers to something *"described in the shared context above"*, it means these items.

Kepler sends each kind of item differently:

- **The task's prompt** goes in full, as background to the work rather than as an instruction. The agent acts on the messages you send it.
- **Each note** goes as a reference, with its title and size. The agent reads the note's text when it needs it.

**Launching a task saves its issues' descriptions as notes.** When you launch a task with linked issues, Kepler reads each issue again and saves its description as a note titled *Issue {identifier}: {title}*, with the issue's URL at the top. A long description is cut short, with a link to the issue.

In the conversation, shared context appears as a collapsible row with a count of the items included. The row reads **Task context added** the first time, and **Task context updated** each time the context changes. Expand the row to see exactly what the agent received.

You do not edit shared context directly. To change it, attach, detach, archive or edit resources. Each session receives the change with its next prompt.

### The task's prompt is context too

The text you wrote when you started the task is a context item of its own: the **Prompt**, at the top of the **Notes** group. Every session on the task works toward this prompt, so Kepler sends it with the rest of the shared context. When the goal changes, edit the prompt the same way you edit a note. Unlike a note, the prompt cannot be deleted.

### Starting a session without the task's context

Sometimes you want an agent that forms its own view, such as a reviewer that should not be influenced by the implementer's brief. To start a session without the task's prompt and notes, follow these steps:

1. Click **+** on the **Sessions** group in the context panel, or press **Cmd/Ctrl+T**. A draft session tab opens.
2. In the draft's composer footer, untick the **Task context** chip. The chip is on by default.
3. Type your prompt and click **Start**.

The new session does not receive the task's prompt or notes. It still gets the task's worktrees, folders, files and links, because it still needs to know where to work. The chip applies only to that draft, so turning it off does not change your other sessions. See [Starting a session](/kepler/task-view#starting-a-session).

### Notes are how you give standing instructions

Attach a **Note** for anything every agent on the task should follow, such as a style rule, a constraint, or a decision you do not want reopened. Write it once, and every session gets it, including sessions you start later. A session sees a note's title first and opens the note when it is relevant, so give each note a title that says what it covers. A note can be up to 1 MB.

To add a note, click **New note** on the **Notes** tab of the **Resources** screen, then type a title and the text, in Markdown. The note saves when you click away or click **Save note**.

To rename a note, click its name while you are in the note, press **F2** on the open note, or choose **Rename note** from its right-click menu. The name becomes a field. Press **Enter** to keep the new name, or **Escape** to restore the old one. A note with no name reads **Untitled note**. The task's **Prompt** cannot be renamed.

To edit an open note, click **Edit**, or press **Enter** on the focused note. The note opens in Kepler's code editor, with highlighted Markdown, line numbers, and find. To save, press **Cmd/Ctrl+S**. If the note changed while you were editing it, such as when an agent wrote to it, Kepler stops the save and asks first: **Save anyway** keeps your version, and the note's history keeps the version it replaces.

Beside **Edit**, **Copy** copies the note and **Save as…** saves it as a Markdown file. If you leave an edit unsaved, Kepler keeps it as a draft: the note reads **Unsaved draft**, and **Edit** becomes **Resume draft**.

A checklist item in a note, such as `- [ ] Add a test`, shows as a checkbox. Tick it in the open note, without opening the editor. Each tick saves a new version of the note.

To point someone, or an agent, at a note, choose **Copy link to note** from its menu. Hover a heading and click **Copy link to section** to copy a link that opens the note at that section. To ask an agent to change part of a note, comment on it. See [Comment on a note](/kepler/review-changes#comment-on-a-note).

**A note keeps its saved versions.** To see them, click **What changed** on the open note, or **See what changed** on the line that says who last edited it. The note shows what changed since your last edit. To compare other versions, pick them in **Changes after** … **up to** …. To bring a version back as the newest one, click **Restore version {version}**. **Back to note** returns to the note. A deleted note can be restored too: click **Deleted** on the **Notes** tab of the **Resources** screen, open the note, and restore a version from its history.

***

## Detaching and deleting

Removing a resource from a task leaves the resource itself intact, unless only the task holds it. The menu shows which action you are taking:

- **Detach** removes something that lives elsewhere, such as a folder or a pull request, from the task.
- **Delete** removes something that only the task holds, such as a note or an uploaded copy.
- **Archive**, on the **Resources** screen, sets a resource aside without removing it. See [Archiving a resource](#archiving-a-resource).

**From the context panel**, Kepler asks you to confirm each removal and says what it does:

| Resource | What removing it does |
|---|---|
| **Folder** or **linked file** | Removes it from the task and leaves it on disk |
| **Uploaded copy** | Deletes the copy in the task folder |
| **Pull request**, **issue**, or **link** | Removes it from the task |
| **Note** | Deletes the note |

The task's **Prompt** has no remove action.

**On the Resources screen, a removal can be undone.** When you remove a note, a file, or a web link there, Kepler asks you to confirm, then its row shows **Undo** for a short time. A folder, an issue, or a pull request goes at once, with no Undo, because you can add it back from the screen's lists.

To remove several resources at once, tick their checkboxes, or tick **Select all**, then use the buttons in the selection bar.

### Archiving a resource

To set a resource aside without removing it, open the **Resources** screen and choose **Archive** from its row's menu. An archived resource leaves the context panel and the task's shared context.

To see what is archived, click **Archived** in the tab's toolbar. Click **Restore** on a row to put it back on the task.

You cannot archive a worktree, the task's **Prompt**, or the task's own folder. To archive a folder a session works in, archive that session first.

A tab can also offer a one-click cleanup, such as **Archive {count} merged** for merged pull requests, or **Remove {count} missing** for files and folders that are gone from disk.

### Deleting a worktree

Deleting a worktree can lose work, so Kepler adds more checks before it deletes one.

The worktree's menu, in the context panel, in the worktree tab's header, or on its row on the **Repos & folders** tab of the **Resources** screen, has 2 separate entries:

- **Detach worktree…** removes the worktree from the task and leaves it on disk.
- **Delete worktree…** removes the worktree from disk, after you confirm in the **Delete worktree?** dialog. The repository's main worktree has no **Delete worktree…** entry.

The **Delete worktree?** dialog lists the worktree with what deleting it would cost, such as **No uncommitted changes** and **Branch kept**, under a verdict such as **Safe to delete**. To remove the branch along with the worktree, tick **Also delete branch**. You cannot delete a worktree that another task still uses. In that case, the dialog names the task that uses it and offers **Detach worktree** instead of **Delete worktree**.

You cannot detach or delete a worktree while a session is still running in it. The menu tells you how many sessions to archive first. If another program has the folder open, the delete fails. Close any editors, terminals, or file explorers that have the folder open, then try again.

The dialog's tags show what you could lose, such as uncommitted files, commits not on any remote, or commits on a detached HEAD. A branch whose commits are in a pull request, merged, or pushed loses nothing. The tags update when you tick **Also delete branch**. A branch merged through a rebase or squash merge counts as merged.

Kepler **keeps** a worktree that would lose work, unless you tick the extra box that names the worktree and what it would lose. Kepler never deletes uncommitted or unpushed work without your confirmation.

***

## Renaming, archiving, and deleting a task

To rename, archive or delete a task, open the **Task actions** (**⋮**) menu on the task's row or in the task page's header. The menu has these actions:

| Action | What it does |
|---|---|
| **Mark as read** / **Mark as unread** | **Mark as read** appears while any of the task's sessions is unread, and marks them all read. Otherwise the menu offers **Mark as unread** |
| **Rename task** | Turns the name into a field. **Auto-name** suggests a name from the task's prompt and resources |
| **Add to group** | Puts the task in one of [your groups](/kepler/arranging-your-work#your-groups) or a **New group…**, or takes it out with **Remove from group** |
| **Manage resources** | Opens the task's **Resources** screen. See [What a task holds](#what-a-task-holds) |
| **Copy task link** | Copies a Kepler link to the task. **Cmd/Ctrl+C** on a focused task row does the same |
| **Refresh** | Reads the task's worktrees and its pull requests and issues again |
| **Archive task** | Moves the task out of the active list and stops its running agents. Its sessions and resources are kept, and prompting it puts it back |
| **Restore task** | Replaces **Archive task** on an archived task, and returns it to the active list and its group |
| **Delete task** | Removes the task along with its sessions and resources. On the task page, **Cmd/Ctrl+Shift+Backspace** does the same |

**Kepler suggests archiving a finished task.** When a task meets all of these conditions, its header asks *Ready to archive?* with an **Archive** button:

- The task is at **Done**.
- Its worktrees have no unpushed work.
- No session is still working, waiting on you, or running background work.

If you dismiss the suggestion, Kepler stops suggesting it for that task.

**Archive** and **Delete** open the same dialog, with the same 3 checkboxes for the task's worktrees and branches. Each box stays unavailable until you tick the one above it, and Kepler remembers your choices for next time:

- **Also delete worktrees**
- **Also delete branches**
- **Also delete the branch on the remote**

Until you tick a box, worktrees and branches stay on disk. With **Also delete worktrees** ticked, every agent of the task ends, and Kepler closes the terminals open in those worktrees before it deletes them.

When you tick **Also delete worktrees**, Kepler lists every worktree with the same tags a single worktree delete shows, and says what will happen to each. It deletes a worktree that is safe to delete, and **keeps** one that would lose work unless you tick the box that names it and confirms the loss. A worktree it cannot delete, such as one another task uses, is listed with the reason.

When **Also delete the branch on the remote** is ticked, Kepler also deletes each branch's remote copy. It keeps the remote branch if deleting it could lose something, such as an open pull request or commits that are not on both sides, and tells you why.

**Restore task** appears in the task page's header as soon as you archive the task. On a row in the main list, it appears only after you filter **Activity** to **Archived**. See [Arranging Your Work](/kepler/arranging-your-work).

To archive or restore a single session, use the session's own menu in the context panel.

***

## What an agent can do with a task's resources

Agents work with tasks through Kepler's own MCP server, `kepler-workspace`. With its tools, an agent can keep the task's resources up to date for you, and can find and coordinate with the rest of your work.

<div class="note" markdown="1">

**Allow-listing the tools by name?** Each tool is named for what it acts on, then what it does, such as `task_get` or `worktree_create`. If an agent's settings allow-list `mcp__kepler-workspace__` tools by name, use the names below.

</div>

If you paste a Kepler link to a task or a session into the chat, the agent can use it to find that task or session. Wherever a tool takes a repository, the agent can also name the repository by one of its **Aliases**, which you set on the repository's page in **Settings → Repositories**. See [Settings](/kepler/settings-repositories#edit-a-repository).

**Reading tasks and notes**

| Tool | What it does |
|---|---|
| `task_get` | Read a task: its stage, group, places to work, notes, files, links, related tasks and sessions |
| `task_list` | Find tasks by name, prompt, notes or files, filtered by stage, hold, repository or [group](/kepler/arranging-your-work#your-groups) |
| `task_note_read` | Read one note's full text |
| `task_note_history` | List a note's saved versions, or the task's notes that have history |
| `task_comment_read` | Read the [review comments](/kepler/review-changes#review-comments) you sent on a task's code or notes, with their replies |

**Finding sessions, agents and places**

| Tool | What it does |
|---|---|
| `session_list` | Find agent sessions, with each one's state and what it is waiting on |
| `session_read` | Read another session's conversation, including one you link with **Copy session link** |
| `agent_list` | List the agents, accounts, models, modes and saved presets a new session can start with |
| `repo_list` | List the repositories and folders where work can happen |

**Notes, links and files**

| Tool | What it does |
|---|---|
| `task_note_write` | Create or edit a note. It never overwrites edits made since the agent read the note |
| `task_note_delete` | Delete a note |
| `task_note_restore` | Restore a saved version of a note as its newest version |
| `task_comment_reply` | Reply on a review comment you sent, and resolve it once the request is done |
| `task_link_update` | Attach or detach issues, pull requests and other links, such as the local URL of a dev server the agent started for you |
| `task_file_attach` | Attach files by path, or save a file the agent wrote as an uploaded copy, up to 200 MiB |
| `task_file_detach` | Detach files. An uploaded copy is deleted |
| `task_resource_archive` | [Archive](#archiving-a-resource) or restore a task's files, folders, links and notes |

**Worktrees**

| Tool | What it does |
|---|---|
| `worktree_create` | Create a worktree on a new branch and bind it to the task |
| `worktree_attach` | Bind an existing worktree or folder to the task |
| `worktree_detach` | Detach a worktree or folder from the task, leaving it on disk |
| `worktree_update` | Record a branch's new merge target, such as after a rebase onto another branch |
| `worktree_delete` | Delete a worktree from disk. An unmerged branch is kept unless the agent asks to delete it |

Where AI Sync and AI Compose are turned on, the `sync_*` and `compose_*` tools also let an agent update a branch from its base with a rebase or merge, and reorganize its commits. See [Review Changes](/kepler/review-changes#agent-tools-ai-sync-and-ai-compose).

**Progress and lifecycle**

| Tool | What it does |
|---|---|
| `task_create` | Create a *separate* task, linked back to this one as a sub-task, follow-up or related task. Nothing starts on it |
| `task_update` | Set the task's stage or hold, set it aside for **Later**, rename it, move it to a group, or restore it from the archive. A hold can lift by itself, such as when CI finishes on the task's pull request |
| `task_archive` | Archive a task and keep its sessions. It can also delete the task's worktrees and merged branches |

**Starting and coordinating work**

| Tool | What it does |
|---|---|
| `session_start` | Start an agent session on a task, such as a delegate or a reviewer, with a first message. It can start without the task's context |
| `session_send` | Send another session a prompt or a message, or stop its running turn |
| `session_update` | Rename a session |
| `session_archive` | Archive a session. A session cannot archive itself |
| `inbox_read` | Read this session's inbox, or wait for reports from the sessions it started |
| `approval_list` | List the requests waiting on your approval. It cannot approve or deny anything |
| `theme_get` / `theme_save` | Read Kepler's theme format, then check a theme file and install it into the themes folder |

### What runs at once, and what asks you

Every workspace tool is pre-approved, in Chat and in Terminal, so none of them shows the agent's own permission prompt. Instead, Kepler decides which requests can run at once.

An agent works freely within its own work. Its own work is its own task, plus the tasks and sessions it created or started sessions on. These requests run at once:

- Reads, anywhere.
- Creating a task, a note or a worktree.
- Changes inside the agent's own work, except changes that can lose something.

These requests wait for your approval:

- Sending a prompt to any session other than one the agent started itself, or a message to a session outside its own work
- Stopping or renaming a session outside its own work, or archiving any session other than one it started
- Changing a task outside its own work, such as its stage, hold, name, group, links or notes, detaching its files, or archiving its resources
- Changing a Kepler setting that affects your accounts, privacy, other tools, what runs, or where files go. Only [Ask Kepler](/kepler/ask-kepler) can change settings, and you approve each change on its own. See [Approval requests](/kepler/agent-sessions#approval-requests)
- Deleting any note
- Detaching an uploaded file, because Kepler deletes its saved copy
- Archiving a task outside its own work or with other live sessions, and any archive that also deletes worktrees
- Setting a task aside for later while its other sessions are working
- Deleting a worktree that has something to lose (uncommitted changes, unpushed commits on a branch being deleted, commits on a detached HEAD, a status Kepler cannot read), or that another task is bound to
- Starting a session in a more permissive mode than the agent's own, or on a task outside its own work
- Overwriting a theme file when there is no Trash to keep the old one
- The AI Sync and Compose tools that change a repository or rewrite its history

A session that an agent starts cannot run in a higher mode than the session that started it unless you approve.

The request appears as an approval card above the asking session's composer, with **Approve** and **Deny**. The **Approve** menu can approve every request of that kind from the session, or always. A rule you make with **Always approve** is listed under **Settings → Agents → Approvals**, where **Remove** deletes it. **Always approve** is not offered for actions that can lose work. See [Agent Sessions](/kepler/agent-sessions#when-the-agent-asks-you-something).

The agent does not wait for you to answer the card. Kepler tells the agent the request is awaiting your approval, the agent continues, and the outcome arrives in its inbox. Before an approved request runs, Kepler checks again. If the target changed in the meantime, such as a worktree that has new commits, nothing runs.

`worktree_delete` has the same protection as your own delete. It refuses while a live session is running in the worktree, including the agent's own session. A worktree it deletes stays on the task, marked as gone, until someone detaches it.

### Reports between sessions

Each session has an **inbox** for what other agents send it:

- Reports and messages
- Changes in the state of a session it started
- The outcomes of its approval requests

When an item arrives for an idle session, Kepler wakes the session to read it. A busy session reads it when its turn ends. In Terminal, Kepler can wake only some agents; see [Reports from other agents](/kepler/agent-sessions#reports-from-other-agents).

When a session has unread reports, the band above its composer says how many. To have the agent read them now, click **Have it read them**.

Agents that keep waking each other can loop. To stop a loop, after 20 turns started by agents rather than by you, reports stop waking the session. The band reads **Reports from other agents are paused**, and the session's tab and row show a reports badge with the count. To turn wakes back on, click **Resume reports**, or send the session a message of your own.

---

---
# The Task View
URL: https://help.gitkraken.com/kepler/task-view/
product: Kepler
feature: Tasks
content_type: how-to
audience: developer
plan_required: all
status: GA
last_verified: 2026-11

Each task has its own screen, the **task page**. The context panel lists everything attached to the task. Beside it, the content area shows the sessions, working copies, files, and details you open.

To open the task page, double-click a task's row in [the Kepler interface](/kepler/kepler-interface), or click **Open task page** in the task's side panel. For what a task is and what you can attach to one, see [Tasks and Resources](/kepler/tasks-and-resources).

***

## The header

The header holds these controls, from left to right:

- **Hide context panel** or **Show context panel**, which hides and shows the context panel. See [The context panel](#the-context-panel).
- **Back to dashboard**, a back chevron, which returns you to the Dashboard as you left it. With the views on the left side, it sits at the top of the views column instead.
- **The task switcher**, the task's name as a chip, which jumps to another task without going back first. Type to search it. Right-click the name for the same actions as the **⋮** menu, or double-click it to rename the task.
- **⋮ Task actions**, a menu of actions on the whole task. See [Task actions](#task-actions).
- **The Progress control**, which shows the task's stage, such as **In Development** or **Done**. Click it to set the stage yourself, to put the task on hold, or to set it back to **Automatic**. See [Arranging your work](/kepler/arranging-your-work).
- **Terminal**, at the right edge, which shows and hides the [terminal drawer](#the-terminal-drawer) and counts the terminals running in it.

When a task looks finished, the header shows a **Ready to archive?** prompt with **Archive** beside it, until you archive the task or dismiss the prompt.

### Task actions

The **⋮ Task actions** menu holds these items:

- The task's **Progress** submenu, with **Reopen** leading on a finished task.
- **Mark as read** while any of the task's sessions is unread, which marks them all read. Otherwise the menu offers **Mark as unread**.
- **Star** or **Unstar**.
- **Rename task** and **Add to group**.
- **Manage resources**, which opens the task's **Resources** screen. See [What a task holds](/kepler/tasks-and-resources#what-a-task-holds).
- **Refresh**, which reads the task's worktrees and its pull requests and issues again.
- **Copy task link**, which copies a Kepler link that opens this task, and **Copy task prompt**.
- **Shut down all agents**, while any are running. When an agent is still working, Kepler asks you to confirm first.
- **Archive task** and **Delete task**. On an already-archived task, **Restore task** replaces **Archive task**.

### Rename a task

To rename a task, do one of the following:

- Pick **Rename task** in the **⋮ Task actions** menu.
- Press **F2** anywhere on the page outside a text field.
- Double-click the task switcher.

The name turns into an editable field. **Auto-name** fills the field with a name suggested from the task's prompt and resources, which you can accept or edit. It never renames the task on its own. To save, press **Enter** or click the check mark. To cancel, press **Escape** or click **×**.

### On a phone

At phone width, for example in a phone browser connected through [Remote Access](/kepler/remote-environments#remote-access-reach-kepler-from-another-device), the task page replaces its header with a single bar:

- **Back**, on the left, which shows a dot when another task needs you.
- The task's name as a chip, which opens the task switcher. Swipe sideways on the name to go back to the previous task.
- A segment for each of **Sessions**, **Changes**, **Terminal**, and **Resources**.

Tap a segment to go to what needs you in that group, or else to the last session you had open. Each segment has a picker that lists that group's rows, where you can archive or close a row, or add one with **New session**, **New terminal**, or **Add resource**. On a phone, a terminal fills the whole column instead of a drawer.

Below the bar, a details row holds the Progress control and **Refresh**. Unfold it to see the checkout and its pull request and issue chips.

Pull down on the bar, or long-press a segment, to open **Everything in this task**. This sheet takes the place of the context panel: it lists every session, checkout, terminal, and resource, each with its own actions menu. Under **Resources**, each kind of resource has its own heading and count, in the same order as the context panel. The sheet also offers **New session**, **Add resource**, **New terminal**, and the archived sessions. A long press opens it on that segment's group only.

On a phone, the task switcher is a sheet that lists every task. Its header holds the current task's actions menu.

***

## The context panel

The context panel, on the left of the task page, lists everything attached to the task, grouped by kind:

**Sessions · Changes · Merged · Terminals · Pull requests · Issues · Notes · Links · Files · Folders · Related tasks**

The task's worktrees are listed under **Changes**. Each row shows the checkout's current state, and opening it opens the checkout's diff review.

**A planned worktree waits for the first session.** When an agent creates a task on a new branch, Kepler makes its worktree when the task's first session starts. Until then, **Changes** shows a row reading **Created when a session starts**. To drop the plan, right-click the row and pick **Remove planned worktree**.

**Merged** holds the worktrees whose branch has been merged, so they do not crowd the work still in progress. Each row says where it was merged. To delete all the merged worktrees at once, click **Delete all…** on the group header and confirm.

**Related tasks** lists the tasks linked to this one, each with its stage and its relation, such as **Sub-task** or **Follow-up**. Hover a row to see the reason for the link. Click the row to go to that task.

**Sessions** always appears, even on a task with no sessions, so you can always start the first one. Every other group appears only when it has something in it.

**The task's prompt has its own row.** **Prompt**, with its own icon, is the first row in the **Notes** group. Open it to read or edit the prompt the task started with. Your edit changes the task's prompt everywhere it appears. You cannot delete the **Prompt** row.

**Files** holds both files linked from disk and copies uploaded to the task. An uploaded copy shows **Task folder** under its name, where a linked file shows its path.

The context panel also has these controls and rows:

- **Manage resources**, at the bottom of the context panel, opens the task's **Resources** screen. See [What a task holds](/kepler/tasks-and-resources#what-a-task-holds).
- The **+** on a group header opens that kind's tab of the **Resources** screen, for example **Add issues** or **Add notes**. On **Changes**, the **+** is **Add worktree**. On **Sessions**, it's **New session**, which opens a draft session. See [Starting a session](#starting-a-session).
- A session you have not started yet shows as a **Draft** row in **Sessions**. Right-click it for **Discard draft**.
- Sessions that are not live, because they're archived or have ended, collect under a **{count} archived** fold below the live ones. Click an archived session to restore and open it in a single step, or pick **Restore** in its menu.

### Hide or show the context panel

To give the content area the full width, hide the context panel:

- Click **Hide context panel** in the header. **Show context panel** brings the panel back.
- Press **Cmd/Ctrl+B**. On Windows and Linux, a focused shell keeps **Ctrl+B** for itself.

While the context panel is hidden, the control shows the task's session status, so you can still see when a session needs you. Hover the control to peek at the context panel over the content, and press **Escape** to close it. To keep the context panel open, click the control while peeking. To resize the context panel, drag its edge.

When the window is too narrow for the context panel beside the open columns, Kepler hides the context panel, and you peek at it the same way. Widen the window to bring it back.

### What a row shows

Each row has 2 lines, cut off at the width of the context panel. Hover a row for a tip with its full name and the details the row has no room for, such as its path, repository, agent, or account.

Some kinds of row show more:

- A **pull request** or **issue** row shows the same live card as the Dashboard. A pull request row leads its subtitle with what needs attention, such as **CI failed**.
- A **file** row's card adds the file's size, type, and dates. An image file shows its own thumbnail as the row's icon.
- A **Changes** row's subtitle is a series of chips that show the checkout's state: uncommitted files, commits on the branch, commits behind or ahead of the upstream and the merge target, conflicts, and an unpublished branch. A checkout with nothing to report shows **Up to date**. When the task spans more than 1 repository, each row also names its repository.
- A checkout in an unusual state shows that state instead of the chips, such as a paused rebase or merge, **Detached** for a detached HEAD, or **Not trusted. Kepler runs no git here.** for a repository you have not trusted. A detached row is titled with the commit's short hash. See [Trust a repository](/kepler/settings-repositories#trust-a-repository).
- A **Changes** row's hover tip lists the branch, the repository and path, any unusual state, the pull request the branch owns, and how the branch compares with its upstream and merge target. With tabs on, a worktree's tab shows the same tip.
- A **session** row starts with its state. When an agent has more than 1 account configured, the row also shows which **Account** the session runs under.
