- A **session** row, and its tab, count the agent's replies to your review comments that you have not read. A **Changes** row counts the unread replies on comments in its changes. See [Replies and resolving](/kepler/review-changes#replies-and-resolving).

Some rows have controls at the end of the subtitle line, always visible:

| Row | Controls |
|---|---|
| **Folder** | **Open in…** |
| **Worktree** (on disk) | **Open in…** and the run-a-command control. To open a shell, use the row's menu or **Cmd/Ctrl+J** |
| **Session** | Show or hide the [Agent Graph](/kepler/agent-graph) for that session alone, and **Archive** |

The run-a-command control shows the newest command running in that worktree, with **Stop**. When nothing is running, it shows your default command.

The row whose item is on screen is highlighted. A ring marks the column that has focus.

### The row menu

Right-click any row for its menu. Every row menu starts with **Open**. When there's somewhere for the item to go, **Open to the side** (tabs off) or **Open beside** (tabs on) follows. See [Columns or tabs](#columns-or-tabs). A worktree row adds **Open changes**.

Each kind of row adds its own items to the menu:

| Row | Menu also holds |
|---|---|
| A worktree that's on disk | **Open changes**, **Open in**, the **Branch** submenu, **New session here**, **New terminal here**, **Run command here**, the copy actions, and **Refresh** |
| A folder | **New session here**, **New terminal here**, **Open in**, and **Copy path** |
| A file | **Open in default app**, a way to show it in your file manager, **Save as…**, and **Copy path** |
| A note | **Rename note**, **Copy note**, **Copy link to note**, and **Save as…**, which saves the note as a Markdown file |
| A session | **New session from this one**, **Rename session**, **Copy session link**, **Show Agent Graph**, the ways to continue it, **Restart agent**, and **Shut down agent** |
| A session started outside Kepler | **Open preview**, **Continue in this task**, **Create task**, and the copy actions |
| A pull request or issue | **Open**, which opens it in Kepler, **Open on {provider}**, the copy actions, **Refresh**, and **Go to worktree** when its branch is checked out |
| A plain link | **Open in browser** and the copy actions |
| A terminal that's closing | **Force close terminal** |

The worktree's **Branch** submenu holds the actions that change the branch itself: **Rename branch**, the upstream (**Set upstream**, **Change upstream**, **Unset upstream**, or **Publish as {remote}/{branch}…**), **Change merge target…**, **Rebase onto {target}**, **Merge {target} into this branch**, and the sync control. A stopped rebase or merge adds rows to continue or abort it.

**Run command here** lists the repository's commands, and so does the **Run a command** control on the row and on the worktree's own strip. Pick a command to run it in that worktree. Its terminal appears in the drawer without taking your focus. Picking a running command stops it.

- **Create command…**, at the end of the menu, adds a command without leaving the task.
- **Manage commands…** opens the repository's page in **Settings → Repositories**, and brings you back to the task when you leave it.

**Open in** lists your editors, with your default editor at the top. On a worktree, the list ends with **Open on {provider}**, which opens the branch on its Git host. To set the editor Kepler uses everywhere, use **Open files and folders in** under **Settings → General**.

**Picking an editor or a command does not make it your default.** To make one your default, use the set/unset toggle at the end of its row.

**Rename branch** opens a dialog for the new name. Tick **Also rename remote branch** to rename it on its remote too. **Change merge target…** opens a picker of remote branches; see [Review Changes](/kepler/review-changes).

**Rename session** lets you name a Chat session yourself. Automatic titles never overwrite a name you chose.

**Copy session link** copies a Kepler link that opens the session. When the window is connected to a remote machine, the link names that machine, so it opens there. With the row focused, **Cmd/Ctrl+C** copies the same link. See [Agent Sessions](/kepler/agent-sessions#pointing-an-agent-at-another-session).

**Continue as** moves the conversation to another signed-in account of the same agent. The agent restarts under that account and keeps the conversation. **Continue in Terminal** and **Continue in Chat** move the conversation between the 2 ways a session runs. When the session is still running, Kepler asks first, and warns when queued messages would be discarded. **Stop and switch** stops the session and moves it. See [Moving a session to another account](/kepler/agent-sessions#moving-a-session-to-another-account) and [How a session runs](/kepler/agent-sessions#how-a-session-runs).

**Use another copy…** appears when Kepler has more than 1 saved copy of the conversation. It lists each copy, with **In use** on the current one. Pick the one to continue when you resume. See [Agent Sessions](/kepler/agent-sessions).

**Option/Alt-click** a resource row to open it in your browser instead of in Kepler.

The last item in a row menu removes the row from the task. It depends on the kind of row:

- **Detach worktree…**, **Detach folder…**, **Detach file…**, **Detach pull request…**, or **Detach issue…** for something that stays on disk or at its provider
- **Delete file…**, **Delete note…**, or **Delete link…** for something Kepler holds itself
- **Archive session** for a session
- **Close terminal** for a terminal

A worktree menu also ends with **Delete worktree…**, except on the repository's main worktree. **Detach worktree…**, **Delete worktree…**, and **Detach folder…** are unavailable while a session of this task still runs there. Archive that session first.

***

## Columns or tabs

The content area shows what you open in either columns or tabs. To choose, turn **Show tabs on the task page** on or off in **Settings → Tasks → Task page**:

| Setting | What the content area does |
|---|---|
| **Off** (the default) | Fixed **columns**, one per kind of thing, each showing one thing at a time |
| **On** | Free-form **tabs** you can pin, drag between groups, and arrange side by side |

In both layouts, terminals open in the [drawer](#the-terminal-drawer) below the content area, never in a column or a tab. Closing a column or a tab only changes the view. It does not detach anything or stop a session, and the context panel still lists everything.

### The columns

With tabs off, the kind of row you open decides its column:

| Column | What opens here |
|---|---|
| **Sessions** | Agent conversations, whether they run in Chat or in a terminal, and draft sessions you have not started yet |
| **Changes** | A worktree: a strip of actions over its changed files. See [Review Changes](/kepler/review-changes) |
| **Resources** | Folders, files, pull requests, issues, links, notes |

To resize columns, drag the divider between them. Kepler keeps the sizes you set.

**Clicking a row toggles it.** Click a row to open it in its column. Click the row that's already on screen to close it again. A column with nothing open disappears, and the other columns take its space.

When the window is too narrow for the open columns side by side, the page shows one column at a time: the one with focus. Clicking a row in the context panel shows its column. Widen the window to see every column again.

When you open the task page, it shows a conversation and the checkout that conversation works in.

To close a column, click **Close panel** (**X**) on its strip.

**Split a column to see 2 items of the same kind.** Cmd-click a row in the context panel (Ctrl-click on Windows and Linux), or pick **Open to the side** in its menu. The item opens beside what that column already shows. While a column is split, a plain click replaces only the focused pane and leaves the others alone.

**Shift-click to open a range of rows.** Use a range to watch several agents at once. Click one session, then shift-click another, and every session from the first to the second opens side by side in the Sessions column.

The close control on a session's strip depends on the session:

- On one of Kepler's own sessions, it's **Archive session**, which stops the agent, saves the conversation, and moves the session under the archived fold in **Sessions**.
- On an external session or a preview, it's **Close tab**, which only hides it.

### Tabs and groups

With tabs on, anything you open from the context panel, including sessions, worktrees, files, and every other resource, opens as a tab. Tabs sit in **groups** that you arrange freely, like editor tabs in VS Code.

- **Drag a tab** to reorder it, onto another group to move it there, or to a group's edge to split off a new group there. Drag the divider between groups to resize them.
- **A single click opens a preview.** A resource opened with one click shows in an italic preview tab that the next single click replaces. Double-click a row, or start editing in the tab, to keep it open. A session always opens as a tab you keep. Turn **Preview tabs** off in **Settings → Tasks → Task page** to have every click keep its tab.
- **Cmd-click a row** in the context panel (Ctrl-click on Windows and Linux), or pick **Open beside** in its menu, to open it in a new group beside the one you're reading.
- **Shift-click opens a range** of rows, each as its own tab.
- Clicking the row of something already open just brings its tab forward. Close a tab from the tab itself.

To open a tab's menu, right-click the tab, or press **Shift+F10** or the Menu key on a focused tab. The menu starts with the tab's own actions, such as **Keep open** on a preview, **Pin tab**, **Close others**, and **Close all**, followed by everything the item's row menu offers. A pinned tab shrinks to its icon at the front of its group and has no close control; unpin it to close it.

A draft session's tab shows **(draft)** after its name when the tab strip has room. With tabs off, right-click a draft tab for **Discard draft**. With tabs on, close a draft with **Close tab** in its menu. Closing a draft that has text in it asks you to confirm first, because your draft prompt and attachments are removed.

A session tab swaps its close control for the session's status dot while the session has something unread or needs you, so you can see which conversation needs attention.

Closing a tab only hides it. You can close a tab in any of these ways:

- Click its **×** (**Close tab**). The active tab always shows its **×**; another tab shows it when you point at the tab.
- Middle-click the tab.
- Press **Cmd/Ctrl+W**, or **Ctrl+F4** on Windows and Linux.
- Press **Delete** on a focused tab.

**Backspace** does not close a tab, except on a Mac keyboard, whose delete key sends Backspace. A closed session keeps running and stays in the context panel. To archive a session, use **Archive** on its row. **Cmd/Ctrl+Shift+T** reopens the last tab you closed.

When every tab is closed, the content area offers **New session**, so you can start something right away.

To bring in an agent conversation you started outside Kepler, start a new session, then click **Open an external session** under its composer. The card shows only while Kepler lists [sessions started outside Kepler](/kepler/agent-sessions#sessions-started-outside-kepler). Each conversation you open gets its own tab. **Back to the new session** returns to the composer.

The list shows the agent conversations Kepler found outside it, under **Live now** and **Past sessions**, with the folder each ran in and when it was last active. **Show past sessions** and **Show sessions from every folder** widen the list. For each agent, the list says how many days back it goes.

### Keyboard

The task page has these keyboard shortcuts:

| Keys | What they do |
|---|---|
| **Ctrl+Tab** / **Ctrl+Shift+Tab** | Switch between the task's sessions, most recently used first |
| **F6** / **Shift+F6** | Move focus to the next or previous region of the page |
| **Cmd/Ctrl+1**, **2**, **3** | Focus the Sessions, Changes, or Resources column (tabs off) |
| **Cmd/Ctrl+Shift+[** and **Cmd/Ctrl+Shift+]** | Previous and next tab. Also **Ctrl+PageUp** and **Ctrl+PageDown** on Windows and Linux |
| **Alt+1** to **Alt+9** | Jump to a tab in the focused group (tabs on) |
| **Cmd/Ctrl+Alt+[** and **Cmd/Ctrl+Alt+]** | Move the focused tab left or right. Also **Ctrl+Shift+PageUp** and **Ctrl+Shift+PageDown** on Windows and Linux |
| **Cmd/Ctrl+W** | Close the focused tab or panel. Also **Ctrl+F4** on Windows and Linux |
| **Delete** | Close the focused tab, the way its **×** does |
| **Cmd/Ctrl+Shift+T** | Reopen the last closed tab (tabs on) |
| **Cmd/Ctrl+T** | New session, which opens a draft tab |
| **Cmd/Ctrl+B** | Show or hide the context panel |
| **Cmd/Ctrl+J** | Show or hide the terminal drawer |
| **Cmd/Ctrl+Shift+J** | Maximize the terminal drawer, opening it first if it's hidden |
| **Cmd/Ctrl+O** / **Cmd/Ctrl+P** | **Open File…** / **Go to File…**. See [Opening a file](#opening-a-file) |
| **Cmd/Ctrl+Shift+O** | **Open Folder…** |
| **Cmd/Ctrl+Shift+P** or **F1** | **Go to task**. See [Go to a task or file](#go-to-a-task-or-file) |
| **Cmd/Ctrl+F** | Find in the focused file or diff. See [Finding text in a file](#finding-text-in-a-file) |
| **F2** | Rename the task, or the note whose pane or tab has focus |
| **Cmd/Ctrl+Shift+Backspace** | Delete the task, after you confirm |
| **Cmd/Ctrl+C** | Copy what the focused row names, such as a session's link or a file's path |
| **Cmd/Ctrl+Shift+W** | Close the window |
| **Tab** to a divider, then the arrow keys | Move the divider between panes, columns, or tab groups. Hold **Shift** for bigger steps |

With tabs off, a tab's menu in a column strip also holds **Move left** and **Move right**.

***

## Starting a session

Every new session starts as a draft in its own tab, marked **(draft)** when the tab strip has room. In the draft's prompt composer, you choose where the agent works and how it runs before anything starts.

To start a session, follow these steps:

1. Click **+** on the **Sessions** group in the context panel, or press **Cmd/Ctrl+T**. A draft tab opens, and a **Draft** row appears in **Sessions**.
2. Choose where the agent works from the place chip at the bottom of the composer. The chip names the place, then its branch, then whether the session gets a new worktree.
3. Open **Agent settings** to choose the **Agent**, **Start in**, and the agent's own options, such as **Permission mode**.
4. Type your prompt.
5. Press **Start**.

The place chip has 3 segments. The first segment opens a menu of places in these groups, with a **Search places** field when the list is long:

| Group | What it lists |
|---|---|
| **Attached to this task** | The task's worktrees, by branch, and its folders, led by **All worktrees and folders**. That row runs the session in the task folder with access to every worktree and folder, and reads **Task folder** while nothing is attached |
| **Repositories** | The repositories the task has worktrees of |
| **Add a repository or folder** | A picker over all your repositories and folders. A folder you pick joins the task right away; a repository joins it when the session starts |

The second segment picks the branch the session works on. The third is a checkbox: tick it to start on a new branch in a new worktree of the session's own, or leave it clear to work in the place as it is.

If the place is a worktree that's gone from disk, **Start** recreates it, after Kepler asks you to confirm. On a task with no place to run, click **Add worktree or folder** first. On a task with a [planned worktree](#the-context-panel), a new draft starts on the planned branch. On a task with more than 1 worktree or folder, a new draft starts on **All worktrees and folders**, unless only 1 of them is a folder or an unmerged worktree, which it then starts on. To narrow the session to one place, pick it from the place chip.

**Task context** is a checkbox chip in the composer's footer, beside the place chip. It's on by default and gives the agent the task's prompt and notes, and later changes to them reach the agent with your next message. Turn it off when you want the session to form its own view without them. See [Starting a session without the task's context](/kepler/tasks-and-resources#starting-a-session-without-the-tasks-context).

**Which agent a draft starts with is a setting.** By default, each session starts on the agent you used last. **New sessions start with**, in **Settings → Tasks → New tasks**, sets the agent for your first session, and for every session once you untick **Start each session on the agent you used last** under it. See [Settings](/kepler/settings-tasks#default-agent).

If no agent is set up, the agent control reads **Set up an agent**, and **Start** opens a panel where you can install an agent or tell Kepler where yours is. See [Agent Integrations](/kepler/agent-integrations). If the agent is signed out, sign in to it before you start.

**Start a draft in a specific checkout.** Right-click a worktree or folder row and pick **New session here**. A draft opens with that checkout already chosen as its place, ready for your prompt.

**When a session cannot start.** If the agent fails after launch, the task page shows **{agent} was unable to start** with the agent's message. Press **Retry** to launch it again, or **Open agent settings** to fix the problem.

**Start from an existing session.** **New session from this one**, on a session's row or tab menu, picks an agent and starts a session in the same working directory that can read the source conversation. **New session from here**, on a message in a conversation, does the same but cuts the source off at that message. The new session shows a **Continues from** divider naming its source; **Open source session** in its menu takes you back.

To run an Action instead of typing a prompt, open the chevron beside the session composer's **Send** button and pick an Action. Kepler adds anything you typed to the Action's prompt as a refinement. See [Actions](/kepler/actions).

***

## Opening a file

The task's own files and folders open on the task page, in Kepler's file viewer: as a tab with tabs on, or in the **Resources** column with tabs off. To see a worktree file alongside its changes instead, pick **Open in Changes** in its tab's menu, which opens it in the Changes overlay on File view. Any other file opens in an overlay. See [Files that open in an overlay](#files-that-open-in-an-overlay).

You can open a file in these ways:

| How to open one | What you get |
|---|---|
| **File › Open File…** (**Cmd/Ctrl+O**) | A file picker for the machine the window is connected to |
| **File › Open Folder…** (**Cmd/Ctrl+Shift+O**) | A folder picker. The folder opens with its file tree |
| **File › Go to File…** (**Cmd/Ctrl+P**) | The Go to palette on its **Files** tab. See [Go to a task or file](#go-to-a-task-or-file) |
| **View › Command Palette…** (**Cmd/Ctrl+Shift+P** or **F1**) | The Go to palette on its **Tasks** tab |
| A row in the context panel's **Files** group | That file |
| A file path an agent writes in the conversation | The file, at the line the agent named. A click or Cmd/Ctrl+click opens it in Kepler, and Cmd/Ctrl+Shift+click opens it in your default editor. |
| A file path in a terminal | The file, at its line. See [File paths are links](#file-paths-are-links) |

**All file links work the same way.** A click, a Cmd/Ctrl+click, or a middle-click opens the file in Kepler. Cmd/Ctrl+Shift+click opens it in your default editor at its line.

A path that's already one of the task's files opens that file's own tab rather than a second copy, however the path was spelled.

### Go to a task or file

**Go to File…** and **Command Palette…** open the same palette, on its **Files** tab or its **Tasks** tab. While it's open, press the other shortcut to switch tabs. The palette also has a **Todo** tab for your pull requests and issues, and a **Commands** tab: in an empty search field, type **#** or **>** to switch to them. For the other tabs, see [Go to a task or file](/kepler/kepler-interface#go-to-a-task-or-file).

On the task page, **Files** starts on this task's files, shown as a pill in the search field. Before you type, it lists **Changed in this task** and **Recent in this task**. To search every task's files, click the pill's **×** or press **Backspace** in the empty field. You can also type a full path. A path that names a folder offers **Open** and opens the folder.

### What the file viewer shows

The file viewer shows each kind of file in its own way:

- **Code and text**, with syntax highlighting, scrolled to the line you opened it at, with that line marked. **Wrap lines** turns soft wrapping on and off.
- **Markdown**, rendered, with a **Preview** / **Source** toggle. A Markdown file opened at a line, such as from a path an agent wrote, opens in **Source** so you see the line.
- **Images and SVG**, fitted to the pane, with **Fit** and **100%**.
- Anything else gets a **No preview for this file** card with the options available in this window: **Open in default app**, **Show in Finder** (macOS), **Show in Explorer** (Windows) or **Show in file manager** (Linux), and **Copy path**.

**An open file stays in sync with the file on disk.** When the file changes, the viewer updates in place and says **Updated just now**, naming the session that changed it when Kepler knows. **Show changes** shows what changed since the file was first shown; **Back to file** returns. A deleted file keeps showing the last version Kepler read, and says so.

A very large file shows its start first, with **Load the rest**.

**Review comments work in the file viewer too.** Hover a line and click the gutter's **+** to leave a comment, the same way you do in the Changes overlay, then click **Send comments** in the tab's actions. From the keyboard, move to a line with **↑** and **↓**, hold **Shift** to select a range, and press **C** to comment. To send comments on a file outside the task's worktrees, open it from the conversation. See [Review comments](/kepler/review-changes#review-comments).

**Open in** on the viewer's header opens the file in your pinned editor, or else the one you used last. Its chevron lists the rest, including your computer's **Default app**, and any of them can be pinned with **Set as default**.

### Finding text in a file

Every code view, the file viewer and the diffs in the Changes overlay alike, has its own find bar. Press **Cmd/Ctrl+F** in the view to open it at the top right. It counts matches as *{current} of {total}*, or **No results**, and offers the following:

| Control | Keys |
|---|---|
| Next and previous match | **F3** and **Shift+F3**. Also **Cmd+G** and **Cmd+Shift+G** on macOS |
| **Match case** | **Alt+C**, or **Cmd+Option+C** on macOS |
| **Match whole word** | **Alt+W**, or **Cmd+Option+W** on macOS |
| **Use regular expression** | **Alt+R**, or **Cmd+Option+R** on macOS |

**Escape** closes the bar. In a diff, the search runs across every file in the stack but skips the unchanged lines that are folded away.

Selecting text works across the whole file, not only the lines on screen, so select all and copy gets the whole file.

### Files that open in an overlay

A file that is not one of the task's files or folders opens in an overlay rather than a tab. So does any file opened away from the task page, such as from the Dashboard or a conversation link outside a task:

- A file or folder inside a worktree opens in the Changes overlay on File view. A changed file opens on **Working changes**. Any other file opens in the **Files** view, the worktree's whole tree. A folder opens the **Files** view with its changed files selected.
- Any other file opens in the file overlay, beside a file tree rooted at the attached folder or worktree that holds it, or else at the file's own folder.

In the file overlay:

- **Show file tree** and **Hide file tree** toggle the tree, and the tree's edge resizes it. On a narrow window, widen the window to show the tree.
- **Filter files** narrows the tree. Right-click a tree row for the ways to open it and copy its path.
- Each folder in the breadcrumb lists its folders and files, and can open the folder in your file manager.
- **Add to task**, in **More file actions**, attaches the file to the task.
- Drag either edge of the overlay to widen it, or use **Maximize**.

***

## The terminal drawer

Terminals open in a drawer below the content area. Drag its divider to resize it. The **Terminal** control at the right edge of the header shows and hides the drawer, and counts the terminals running in it.

To show the drawer or open a terminal, use one of these:

| How to open one | What you get |
|---|---|
| **Cmd/Ctrl+J**, or the header's **Terminal** | Shows and hides the drawer |
| **New terminal here**, on a worktree or folder row | A shell in that checkout |
| **Run command here**, on a worktree row | The command you pick, running in that checkout, revealed without taking your focus |
| The strip's **+** | A shell. With several checkouts it becomes **New terminal in…**, listing them by branch |

Every terminal also has a row in the context panel's **Terminals** group. Click the row to open the drawer on that terminal. Click the row of the terminal already showing to hide the drawer. Drag the drawer's tabs to reorder them.

**Maximize terminal pane**, or **Cmd/Ctrl+Shift+J**, takes the whole height; **Restore terminal pane** brings it back.

On a phone, a terminal takes the whole column, with a row of the keys a phone keyboard lacks beneath it, and you select text with a long press. See [Remote Access](/kepler/remote-environments#remote-access-reach-kepler-from-another-device).

### When a terminal reconnects

A terminal reattaches to its running shell rather than starting a new one:

- While it reconnects, the last screen stays readable. If it cannot reconnect, the shell is still running: click **Retry** to load its output again.
- What you type while it reconnects is sent once the terminal is back. If the program printed something in the meantime, Kepler drops your typing and tells you to type it again.
- Only 1 view can type in a terminal at a time. When another window or a Remote Access device is driving it, click **Take control** to type here.
- When a terminal prints faster than the connection can show, Kepler shows the latest output and skips older lines.

### Reading a tab

Each tab shows **a single icon** that tells you both what kind of terminal it is and how it ended, so a clean finish and a crash look different:

| Kind | What it is |
|---|---|
| **Shell** | A plain terminal you opened |
| **Agent** | A session running an agent in Terminal mode. See [Agent Sessions](/kepler/agent-sessions#how-a-session-runs) |
| **Command run** | One of the repository's commands |

When the program in a shell tab reports a status, the tab shows it: **Running**, **Needs you**, **Done**, or **Failed**. Hover the tab for the program's message and progress. An agent tab keeps its own icon, because its session reports the status.

**A shell tab is named after what runs in it**, such as `pnpm dev`. Back at the prompt, the tab returns to its own label, such as **Terminal 2**. Command runs and agent tabs keep their names.

When a shell's program needs you or finishes, Kepler sends a notification that names the terminal and its task, unless that terminal is on screen in the focused window. These notifications follow the same settings as agent sessions, in **Settings → Notifications**.

A finished command run shows a **result bar** rather than leaving you to read the scrollback: **Exited with code {code}**, **Exited by signal {signal}**, or **Stopped**, with **Run again** and **Close** beside it. A still-running one offers **Stop**.

### File paths are links

File paths printed in a terminal are links, including relative paths, paths with a line suffix such as `src/app.ts:42`, and paths wrapped across lines. Cmd-click one (Ctrl-click on Windows and Linux) to open the file [on the task page](#opening-a-file) at its line, and Cmd/Ctrl+Shift+click to open it in your default editor.

Right-click a path for more: **Open file**, your default editor (opening at the line), **Open in** for the rest of your editors and your computer's **Default app**, **Save as…**, and **Copy path**. Any of those targets can be your default, with **Set as default**.

Kepler task and session links in a terminal are links too. Cmd/Ctrl-click one to open it in Kepler, or right-click it for **Open in Kepler** and **Copy link**.

On a phone, long-press a path or link instead, then pick **Open** from the small menu over the selection, which also offers **Copy**, **Paste**, and **Select all**. See [Remote Access](/kepler/remote-environments#remote-access-reach-kepler-from-another-device).

### Closing a busy terminal

Closing a terminal with something running in it asks you to confirm first, naming the job that would stop. Click **Close terminal** to go ahead. A terminal that is already closing offers **Force close**.

Shell tabs survive a Kepler update and come back after a restart. With **Keep agents and terminals running across restarts and updates** on, in **Settings → General**, command runs do too. A plain **Quit** ends them. When you quit Kepler with busy terminals or sessions, it asks first.

***

## What each resource pane shows

Each kind of resource opens in its own pane:

| Resource | Details |
|---|---|
| **Worktree**, on disk | A strip of actions (the branch, the sync control, **Open in**, **Run a command**) over its changed files, which lead into the Changes overlay, plus a **Comments** view that lists the task's review comments with how many are open and unread. See [Review Changes](/kepler/review-changes) |
| **Worktree**, missing | Its branch, base branch, and recorded path, with a way to recreate it. See [When a worktree goes missing](/kepler/tasks-and-resources#when-a-worktree-goes-missing) |
| **Folder** | The folder's name and its **Path** |
| **File** | The file itself, in the [file viewer](#opening-a-file), with its description, where it came from, and its size on the viewer's toolbar. An uploaded copy says it's a copy in the task folder, and has **Rename** in **File actions** |
| **Pull request** / **Issue** | Status, who it involves, the item's description and its labels. An issue adds its comments |
| **Link** | Every plain link (one that is not a pull request or issue) shares one **Links** pane, scrolled to the link you picked |
| **Note** | The note itself, with **Copy**, **Save as…**, **What changed**, and **Edit**. The **Prompt** note edits the task's prompt |

**The worktree strip.** The **⋮** beside the branch, and a right-click on the branch, both open the worktree's full [row menu](#the-row-menu). With more than 1 worktree, the branch name also switches between the task's worktrees. **Detach worktree…** leaves the worktree on disk, and **Delete worktree…** removes it from disk.

**Files.** A description you edit saves as you type, and **Done** closes the field. **Rename** on an uploaded copy renames its file on disk. A linked file has no **Rename**.

**Pull requests and issues.** You can select and copy the description text. When Kepler cannot read a description or the provider, the pane says so and points you to the item on its provider.

A pull request's **People** section shows its author, its **Assignees**, and each reviewer with their review state. An issue shows its **Assignee**.

An issue from GitHub, GitHub Enterprise, GitLab, GitLab Self-Hosted, Jira, or Jira Server also shows its latest comments under **Comments · {count}**. **Show earlier comments** pages back, and **Refresh comments** reads them again. Kepler shows the comments for you to read. It does not pass them to the agent.

**Links.** The **Links** pane lists every plain link on the task with its title and URL, an **Open in browser** button, and **Link actions**, scrolled to the link you clicked.

**Notes.** In a note's pane:

- To rename the note, click its name while you are in the note, press **F2** with the note focused, or pick **Rename note** from its row menu. **Enter** saves the name and **Escape** puts it back. You cannot rename the **Prompt** note.
- To edit the note, click **Edit** or press **Enter** on the focused note. The note opens in Kepler's code editor, and **Cmd/Ctrl+S** saves it. A note with unsaved edits says **Unsaved draft**, and **Edit** reads **Resume draft**.
- To see the note's earlier versions in its place, click **What changed**, or **See what changed** on the line that says who last edited the note.
- **Save as…** saves the note as a Markdown file.

See [Notes are how you give standing instructions](/kepler/tasks-and-resources#notes-are-how-you-give-standing-instructions).

---

---
# The Agent Graph
URL: https://help.gitkraken.com/kepler/agent-graph/
product: Kepler
feature: Agent Graph
content_type: how-to
audience: developer
plan_required: all
status: GA
last_verified: 2026-11

When several agents run at once, use the **Agent Graph** to see what each one is doing. The graph shows every task, the sessions in each task, each turn, every tool call, every subagent, and the files the agents touch. It updates live, and new nodes appear as the agents work. The Agent Graph shows agent work the way the Commit Graph in GitKraken Desktop shows a repository's history.

***

## Open the Agent Graph

You can open the Agent Graph for all your agents or for a single session. It has no page of its own:

| To see | Do this |
|---|---|
| **All your agents** | Select the **Agent Graph** view on the Dashboard. To show any **Tasks** view as a graph, choose **Graph** in its **View** menu |
| **One session** | On the task page, open the menu of the session's row in the context panel and choose **Show Agent Graph**. The session's graph opens beside its transcript, and **Hide Agent Graph** closes it |

To learn about the Dashboard's views and their **List**, **Board** and **Graph** layouts, see [Arranging Your Work](/kepler/arranging-your-work).

A graph view shows the tasks that its search and filters let through. A session's graph opens fully expanded, top to bottom, and grows as the agent works.

The graph is for viewing, not for working. To work in a session, open the session from its task. The node details in the graph link directly to it. To watch several agents at once and answer them, **Shift**-click sessions to open them side by side. See [the task page](/kepler/task-view).

***

## How to read the graph

The graph has layers. Each layer is one level further from the root:

| Layer | What it is |
|---|---|
| **Task** | The root, 1 for each task. See [Tasks and Resources](/kepler/tasks-and-resources) |
| **Session** | Each agent session in that task, with its agent and model |
| **Turn** | One exchange: **Turn 1**, **Turn 2**, and so on |
| **Tool call** | What the agent did in that turn |
| **Subagent** | A subagent the agent started, with its own tool calls beneath it |
| **File** | The files a call touched. This is the bottom layer, where you can see when 2 sessions work on the same file |

The graph shows only sessions that belong to a task, so an external session that no task owns does not appear.

### Past turns start folded

In a Dashboard graph view, each session shows its latest turn and folds the earlier ones. A folded card shows a chevron and the number of nodes beneath it. To fold or unfold any card with children, such as a session, a turn or a subagent, double-click it. A session's own graph starts with every turn unfolded.

Look out for 2 kinds of node, because the agent cannot continue until you respond: **Permission needed** and **Question for you**.

### What a node's state means

| State | What is happening |
|---|---|
| **Running a tool** | Working now |
| **Waiting on the model** | Thinking |
| **Blocked** | Waiting on you |
| **Finished — unread** | Done, and you have not looked at it yet |
| **Done** | Finished, and you have looked at it |
| **Stopped** | You interrupted it |
| **Failed** | It ended with an error |
| **Idle** | Doing nothing |

For 3 states that need your attention, the card shows a word instead of a color: **New**, **Needs you**, and **Error**.

### Tool calls are colored by what they do

Each tool call has a color for its kind:

**Read · Edit · Delete · Move · Search · Execute · Think · Fetch · Switch mode · Other**

The colors are the quickest way to see what an agent is doing. A task with only **Read** calls is still exploring the code. Many **Edit** calls mean the agent has chosen an approach and is making changes.

Repeated calls of the same kind fold into one node marked **Group**. The node keeps the kind as its name and shows the number of calls and how many different files they touch. For example, a **Read** node that reads *9 calls · 4 files* did not read the same file 9 times. To unfold a group, double-click it. Double-click it again to fold it. A single click only selects a node, so selecting a group never rearranges the graph.

***

## Click any node for detail

When you select a node, its details open beside the graph. The details depend on the kind of node:

- **Session**: the agent, state, model, mode, context used, cost, where it is running, and its stop reason.
- **Tool call**: the tool, the exact input, the files and paths it touched, how long it took (some calls show no duration), and how many calls failed.
- **Subagent**: its type, its prompt, and its own calls.
- **Task**: its status (**Active**, **On hold**, **Later**, or **Archived**), its sessions, and its resources.
- **File**: a preview of the file. For a large file, the preview reads only its beginning.

For a node with children, the details header also has a fold button, **Collapse what is under this node** or **Expand what is under this node**. It does the same as double-clicking the card. The stats column still counts the whole graph, including folded nodes.

From the details, click **Open task** or **Open session** to go to the work, or **Copy** to copy any input or prompt.

***

## The stats column

The stats column, on the right side of the graph, shows numbers about all your agents' work. Read it from top to bottom.

On the Dashboard, the stats column hides while a panel is open.

### The counters

The top of the stats column has 6 tiles, 2 across:

| Counter | What it counts |
|---|---|
| **Working** | Sessions in a turn, with a tool running |
| **Blocked** | Sessions that cannot continue without you |
| **Thinking** | Sessions in a turn with no tool running, waiting on the model |
| **Unread** | Sessions that finished a turn you have not looked at |
| **Subagents** | Subagents running now |
| **Failed calls** | Tool calls that ended with an error, across the graph shown |

**Blocked** and **Unread** are the counters that tell you to act.

### Needs attention

The **Needs attention** list appears under the counters when something needs you. It lists everything that is waiting for you, most urgent first, tagged **Needs you**, **Error**, or **New**. Click a row to go to its node. In a graph with 300 nodes, this list is the reliable way to find the nodes that need you.

### Throughput

The **Throughput** section shows a trace of your agents' activity over time, with these readings under it:

| Reading | What it tells you |
|---|---|
| **Tasks** / **Sessions** | How many the graph shows |
| **Tools** | Tool calls running now |
| **Files touched** | How many different files the calls in the graph have touched |
| **Context** | How much context window your sessions have used, as a total and a percentage. Only sessions that report usage count, and the row does not appear when none do |
| **Cost** | What the work has cost so far, in the currency your sessions report. The row does not appear when sessions report no cost, or report it in several currencies |

### Tool spectrum

The **Tool spectrum** section shows the calls by kind, with a bar and a count for each kind. It shows whether your agents are mostly reading, editing or running commands. Kinds with no calls do not appear, and until there are calls, the section reads **No tool activity yet**.

### Usage windows

The **Usage windows** section shows your agent subscription windows, with 1 bar for each window of each agent, and the share of the window you have used. The section appears when it has something to show:

- With **Check plan usage with each agent's provider** on (the default, in **Settings → Agents → Usage limits**), Kepler asks each agent's provider for your usage.
- With it off, the section shows only readings that your agents report themselves, dimmed when they are out of date. The section stays hidden until an agent reports a reading.

See [Settings](/kepler/settings-agents#usage-limits).

These bars show only how much of each window you have used. To see whether you are on pace for a window, and when it runs out at your current rate, check a session's usage meter. See [Usage indicators](/kepler/agent-sessions#usage-indicators).

### What was folded away

At the bottom of the stats column, a note counts what Kepler left out of the graph to keep it readable:

- Tool calls grouped.
- Sessions filtered out.
- Sessions Kepler can see but not trace.
- Tasks with no session.

***

## Finding things in a busy graph

In a Dashboard graph view, use the Dashboard's search box and the view's **View** menu. In a session's own graph, use the search box, **Options** menu and depth slider in the graph's header. The zoom buttons and the replay bar float over the bottom of the graph:

| Control | What it does |
|---|---|
| **Detail depth** | How many layers deep the graph goes: up to 5, and 4 by default |
| **Direction** | Draws the tree **Left to right** or **Top to bottom** |
| **Zoom to selection** | Zooms to the selected node and its tree. The **While zoomed** settings below it set when the view moves again |
| **Group repeated tool calls** | On by default. When off, every call is its own node |
| **Compact stats** | Shows the stats column in less space, for a smaller window |
| **Sessions** | On the Dashboard, under **Filters**. **Active**, the default, hides sessions that have ended |
| **Only active sessions** | In a session's own graph, hides sessions that have ended. Off by default |
| **Agent** / **Repo** | In a session's own graph, narrows it to 1 agent or repository |
| **Zoom in** / **Zoom out** / **Fit to view** | Moves the view. You can also drag to pan, and press **Escape** to clear a selection |

Each graph view keeps its own settings.

### Pause and replay the graph

A live graph changes while you read it. To hold the picture still, or to look back at what just happened, use the replay bar over the bottom of the graph:

| Control | What it does |
|---|---|
| Play/pause button | From live, holds the picture on screen. While you hold a frame, plays the recording forward from it, or pauses it again |
| **Previous frame** / **Next frame** | Steps back or forward 1 frame. From live, **Previous frame** shows the moment just before the latest one |
| Scrubber | Moves to any point in the recording. Drag it, click it, or use the arrow keys |
| Readout | While you hold a frame, how far behind live the picture is, such as *-12s*. While the graph is live, how much history you can move back through |
| **Live** / **Back to live** | Reads **Live** while the graph follows your agents, and **Back to live** while you hold a frame. Click **Back to live** to return to live |

To see the time of the last update, hover over **Live**.

Your agents keep working while you hold a frame, so the readout shows the picture falling further behind. Kepler records only while an agent is working, so while every agent is idle, the replay bar's controls are unavailable.

***

## What the graph does not show

The graph does not show everything about your agents' work:

- **No token counts per turn.** The graph shows how full the context window is, and the cost, instead.
- **No durations for some calls.** See [Click any node for detail](#click-any-node-for-detail).
- **No cost or time per subagent.**
- **No activity for external and terminal sessions.** The graph shows each one as a single node with a badge, instead of showing it as idle.
- **No history after Kepler restarts.** After a restart, the nodes beneath a session are empty, though the session node remains.

When nothing is running, the graph reads **Nothing running yet**, with the hint *Start an agent session and its activity appears here in real time.* When sessions exist but your filters exclude all of them, the hint changes to *No sessions match the current filters.*

***

## Send feedback

The Agent Graph is new, and it will change. To tell the Kepler team whether it helps you, click **Feedback** in the top bar to open **Send feedback**, then follow these steps:

1. Pick a **Type**: **Feature request**, **Bug report**, or **General feedback**.
2. Write a **Message**.
3. Send it.

You can also post feedback on the public issue board at [github.com/gitkraken/gk-ade/issues](https://github.com/gitkraken/gk-ade/issues).

---

---
# Create a task
URL: https://help.gitkraken.com/kepler/create-task/
product: Kepler
feature: Tasks
content_type: how-to
audience: developer
plan_required: all
status: GA
last_verified: 2026-11

You can start a task in 5 ways. The shortest starts from work that is already assigned to you:

| Start from | How |
|---|---|
| **Work assigned to you** | Run an Action on an issue or pull request in the **Todo** view of [the Kepler interface](/kepler/kepler-interface). One click starts the task with its context attached |
| **Something you're describing yourself** | **New task** opens the **New task** composer, where you write the prompt and attach what it needs |
| **A conversation you already started** | **Open an external session**, under the **New task** composer, wraps a task around an agent session you began in your own terminal |
| **Workspaces in another agent app** | **Import from another app** brings workspaces from Conductor, Orca, herdr, or Vibe Kanban in as tasks, with their branches and chats |
| **Another GitKraken app** | A link from GitLens or GitKraken Desktop opens Kepler on the work you were looking at |

***

## From an issue or pull request

Starting from an issue or pull request is the shortest path. Find the item in **Todo** and click its **Action** button. Kepler then does the following:

1. Creates the task.
2. Attaches the repository and the item.
3. Sets up a worktree.
4. Starts an agent with the context in place.

The default Action depends on the item:

- **Plan** for an issue.
- **Address Feedback** for a pull request you authored.
- **Review** for someone else's pull request.

You can edit all of these Actions. To read an Action's prompt, open the list under the button's chevron and hover the Action. See [Actions](/kepler/actions).

The button stays an outline until you hover or select its row. On a narrow card, it shrinks to a play icon. On a phone, it becomes a single **⋮** menu that lists every Action.

Kepler names tasks automatically from what you started them with. To rename a task, use **Rename task** in the **⋮** menu, whose field also has an **Auto-name** button that suggests a name from the task's prompt and resources. See [Tasks and Resources](/kepler/tasks-and-resources).

<div class="note" markdown="1">

**Nothing in Todo?** Set up your [issue tracker](/kepler/issue-tracker-integrations) and [pull request](/kepler/pull-request-integrations) integrations in **Settings** first. **Todo** shows work only from connected accounts.

</div>

***

## From the New task composer

Click **New task** or press **Cmd/Ctrl+N**. To start one without switching to Kepler first, press **Shift+Alt+N** to open the quick launcher from anywhere, including when Kepler is not the focused window.

The **New task** composer is a prompt box above a row of 4 buttons:

| Control | What it attaches |
|---|---|
| **Add repo or folder** | A repository to work in, or a plain folder |
| **Add issue** → **Issues** | Issues from your connected trackers. With only Linear in the list, a team picker and a **Project** picker show every open issue in the team or Linear project you pick, not just yours |
| **Add PR** → **PRs** | Pull requests from your connected hosts |
| **Add context** | Files and links the agent can read. A folder to work in goes through **Add repo or folder** |

Each picker lists what you have already attached of its kind, where you can also remove it.

**Paste a link to attach it.** Paste a pull request or issue URL into the prompt, from a connected host or from Jira or Linear, and it becomes a chip naming the item. The chip attaches the item the same way **Add issue** or **Add PR** would, along with its repository, so a pull request from another repository launches in that repository, on its branch. If the repository is not in Kepler yet, Kepler clones it when the task starts.

A repository you pick yourself takes precedence over the link's. If Kepler cannot read a link, the composer says so and tries again when you press **Start**. A link that still cannot be read does not stop the task: the task starts with whatever was staged, and the agent gets the link to continue from. If the link staged nothing, the task does not start.

In a window connected to another machine, picking a file through **Add context** also offers **Upload from this machine**. Uploads are saved into the task's own folder when it starts.

**Repositories and folders share 1 list**, with the places you use most at the top. Picking a folder that is one of a repository's existing worktrees attaches that worktree itself, and the chip reads **Worktree *branch***.

You can attach as much or as little context as you want. To create a task from the composer, follow these steps:

1. Write the prompt: *Describe a task or ask a question…*
2. Attach what the prompt needs. You can also attach nothing.
3. If you attached a repository, configure it. See [Configuring a repository](#configuring-a-repository).
4. Click the primary button, such as **Start**.

**The composer remembers the repositories you last started a task with** and stages them again the next time you open it. The branch and worktree settings reset to their defaults.

**The composer also remembers an unsent draft.** If you close the dialog with a prompt half written, the prompt is still there when you reopen it. Kepler asks before it discards a draft.

**Kepler also remembers which repository you pick for a tracker project.** When you pick a Jira, Linear, or Azure issue, its **Repository** chip holds the repository you used for that project before. To use another repository, or **No repository**, choose it from the chip's menu.

The primary button runs the Action that matches what you've attached, exactly as it would from a Todo row. A linked pull request resolves to **Address Feedback** or **Review**, depending on who wrote it; a linked issue resolves to **Plan**. With nothing attached, the button reads **Start** and starts the task with your prompt as written.

To keep **Start** when you link an issue or pull request, turn the switching off: click **Turn off** in the note the composer shows the first time it switches, or turn off **Suggest automatically** in [Settings → Actions](/kepler/settings-actions).

The chevron beside the primary button lists the other choices: **Prepare**, which creates the session without starting work yet, and every Action that applies to what you've attached. Picking one there does not run it. Instead, it relabels the primary button, and an Action that names its own agent puts that agent in the agent pill. You can then check or change what will run before you press the button. To pick an Action and run it at once, hold Cmd/Ctrl as you click it. The Action sends its prompt, with anything you typed added as a refinement.

**Shift+Tab** in the prompt cycles the primary button through the same list.

A task that has its prompt but no session yet, such as one an agent created for you, opens a draft session tab. To send the task's prompt as written, press **Start** on the empty box.

The task appears in the list as soon as you press **Start**, with a **Preparing** pill until setup finishes. The task's panel and the task page show each launch step. **Cancel** stops a launch while Kepler is reading a link or cloning a repository.

If setup fails, the row's pill reads **Failed** and the panel shows the error. To change the task and try again, click **Edit and retry**, or **Dismiss** to clear it. If it failed because a repository or folder is not trusted, the panel says so: click **Trust and retry**. A task that starts without some of its repositories warns you which ones it left out. When they were left out because they are not trusted, the warning offers **Trust**. See [Trust a repository](/kepler/settings-repositories#trust-a-repository).

If the task starts but its agent session does not, the task page and the Dashboard panel say that the agent was unable to start, with **Retry**. See [Agent Sessions](/kepler/agent-sessions#when-a-session-drops).

### Configuring a repository

Each attached repository gets a chip with 3 segments:

- **Base branch**: by default, the task gets a new branch from **the repository's remote default branch**. Open the segment to branch off a different branch, to work directly on an existing one, or to take the repository's **current** branch in place.
- **Branch name**: the new branch's name, suggested from your prompt as you type. Click it to edit it. See [Naming the branch](#naming-the-branch).
- **Isolated worktree**: an on/off toggle, on by default, that gives the task its own working copy. Turn it off to have the task share your repository folder, so a branch switch there moves your checkout. See [Tasks and Resources](/kepler/tasks-and-resources#worktrees-and-working-in-place).

**What a newly attached repository starts on is a setting.** The 3 segments start from **Settings → Tasks → New tasks → Where new tasks make changes**: **Isolated worktree** (the default), **New branch**, or **Current branch**. The setting changes only the starting point. You can still change every segment for each repository in each task. See [Settings](/kepler/settings-tasks#where-new-tasks-make-changes).

Picking **New branch** or **Current branch** means the task runs in the repository's own checkout rather than an isolated one, so only 1 task can use that checkout at a time. If another task already has it, the chip says **Another task is working here** and names it. Click **Create a worktree for this task** to put this repository in an isolated worktree instead.

### Naming the branch

Kepler names a task's branch from what the task is about, rather than from the task's name alone:

- **The name is suggested from your prompt** and appears on the chip as you type. Click it to edit it: **Enter** keeps your name, and **Esc** restores the suggestion.
- **An issue identifier leads the name** when the task came from one, such as `KEP-421-fix-the-import-path`.
- **Automatic names are namespaced under `kepler/`.**
- **A name you type is yours verbatim.** The prefix applies to automatic names only.
- **Kepler applies your repository's own branch-naming policy** where the host publishes one.

You can set the prefix in 2 places: **Settings → Tasks → New tasks → Branch prefix** for the app, and per repository in **Settings → Repositories**, on the repository's own page. The repository's page offers **Default (*prefix*)**, **None**, or **Custom**, and shows an example branch name. Leave the app setting empty for no prefix at all. If a repository already has a branch named `kepler`, Kepler tells you the prefix cannot be used there.

A repository linked to a pull request always opens in its own isolated working copy, and the toggle is locked. If the pull request's branch already exists on this machine with commits that are not on the pull request, Kepler keeps your local branch and starts the task on a new branch that tracks the pull request. A pull request from a fork never takes over your own branch of the same name, unless that branch already tracks the fork.

When the task starts, Kepler clones a repository you have not cloned yet into your **Repositories folder**. Until then, you cannot pick its branch.

Attaching the same repository twice gives the task 2 independent worktrees on it, for example to compare 2 approaches. Two chips that would end up in the *same* worktree are marked **Duplicate worktree**, and Kepler creates only 1 of them.

***

## From a session you already started

If you started work with an agent in your own terminal, you can track that conversation in a task. Under the **New task** composer, and on an empty tasks list, **Open an external session** switches the composer to a list of every agent conversation Kepler can see. **Start a new task** switches back. **Open an external session** appears only while external session detection is on.

| Part | What it does |
|---|---|
| **Live now** | Sessions live in a terminal right now |
| **Past sessions** | Conversations found on disk, from any time |
| **Find an external session…** | Searches across both groups |

When the list is capped, or Kepler could not read one agent's sessions, the list says so.

Pick a conversation to continue it in a new task:

- A past conversation resumes.
- A live conversation opens read-only in its task, so you can follow it while it keeps running in your terminal. Once the conversation is idle, close it in your terminal, then click **Continue here** in the session to continue it in Kepler.

### When a task already covers that folder

When the conversation's folder already belongs to a task, Kepler asks under the list. **Add it to that task** adds the conversation to that task, and **Make a new task** creates a new one anyway.

Starting a task from an external session anywhere else, such as from a Kepler link, asks the same question in the **Add to existing task?** dialog. **Add to task** adds the conversation to the task you pick, and **Create a new task** creates a new one anyway. When several tasks include the folder, the dialog marks the **closest**.

For what happens to the conversation once it's on a task, including forking, continuing, and what Kepler will and will not answer on its behalf, see [Agent Sessions](/kepler/agent-sessions#sessions-started-outside-kepler).

***

## From another agent app

If you work in Conductor, Orca, herdr, or Vibe Kanban, you can bring its workspaces into Kepler as tasks. Each workspace becomes a task in the same folder, on the same branch, and its chats continue as the task's sessions.

To import workspaces, take the following steps:

1. Choose **File → Import from Another App…**. On an empty tasks list, you can also click the card that names the apps Kepler found, such as **Import from Orca**.
2. If Kepler finds more than 1 of these apps, pick the one to import from.
3. Tick the workspaces you want. A workspace you already imported is marked **Already a task**.
4. Click **Import *N* workspaces**.

Continue each chat in one app only: both apps write to the same chat history.

***

## From a folder, or from nothing at all

**A task does not need a repository.** Attach a plain folder from **Add repo or folder**, and the agent works on it in place, with no branch, no worktree, and no Git at all. A folder of notes or a scratch directory works as a normal task.

When you browse for a folder in a window connected to another machine, Kepler opens its own folder picker. To use this picker everywhere, turn on **Always use the custom folder picker** in **Settings → General**. When you type a path into it, Kepler checks the path and, for a path close to an existing folder, offers **Did you mean** with the closest folder.

You can also attach nothing at all: no repository, no folder, and no issue. Use a task like this to ask a question or explore an idea, and attach the real work later, once it's worth tracking. See [The Task View](/kepler/task-view).

***

## From another GitKraken app

You can open Kepler from other GitKraken products, such as GitLens and GitKraken Desktop. A link from one of them can do the following:

- Open the **New task** composer already filled in with the issue, pull request, or repository you were looking at.
- Open a task or session you already have.
- Put a prompt and an Action in the composer.
- Start a new session on a task you already have.
- Start right away rather than waiting for you to press **Start**.

For an item that a task already holds, Kepler offers **Open task** instead. If the repository is not on this machine, Kepler clones it when the task starts. A link that Kepler cannot fully resolve still opens, with a warning about what Kepler could not use.

### Which window a link opens in

Kepler sends each link to the window that can use it:

- A link for a task opens in the window already showing that task.
- A link that names a saved remote machine opens in a window on that machine. If none is open, Kepler opens one.
- Any other link goes to the window you used last.

If a link cannot open on the machine it names, it opens on this computer instead, a notice says so, and nothing it asked to start runs on its own. In a window on a remote machine, a link for something that is not there offers **Open on this computer**.

***

## After the task starts

The task appears in the **Tasks** view right away, with the **Preparing** pill until its setup finishes. Click it to open its side panel, or double-click it to open [the task page](/kepler/task-view).

From there you can add more sessions, attach more resources, and review what the agent changed. See [Agent Sessions](/kepler/agent-sessions) and [Review Changes](/kepler/review-changes).

### Context: what gets handed to the agent

Starting from **Todo** and starting from the **New task** composer send the same Action prompt, but they attach different amounts of detail:

| Started from | What the agent receives |
|---|---|
| **A row in Todo** | The full issue or pull request body, attached as shared context |
| **The New task composer** | A reference (identifier, title, and URL) which the agent fetches the detail from itself |

Either way, Kepler saves each linked issue's description as a note titled with the issue's identifier and title; long descriptions are shortened with a link to the issue. Kepler does not save pull request descriptions this way.

---

---
# Agent Sessions
URL: https://help.gitkraken.com/kepler/agent-sessions/
product: Kepler
feature: Agent Sessions
content_type: how-to
audience: developer
plan_required: all
status: GA
last_verified: 2026-11

An **agent session** is one running conversation with a coding agent, anchored to one working directory. Learn how to start a session, direct it with prompts, answer its questions, and manage it from start to archive.

A task can hold several sessions. For example, 2 agents can share one worktree, each agent can have its own worktree, or a session can run in the task folder itself. A task lists all of its sessions under its **Sessions** group. See [The Task View](/kepler/task-view).

Sessions vary in 2 ways:

| Property | Values | Details |
|---|---|---|
| **How it runs** | **Chat** or **Terminal** | [How a session runs](#how-a-session-runs) |
| **Where it started** | In Kepler, or outside Kepler and found by it | [Sessions started outside Kepler](#sessions-started-outside-kepler) |

Prompts, steering, permissions, status, and the session lifecycle work the same way for every session.

To read the changes an agent made, see [Review Changes](/kepler/review-changes).

***

## Starting a session

You can start a session from any of the following places:

| From | How |
|---|---|
| A row in **Todo** | Fire an Action. See [Actions](/kepler/actions) |
| The task page's context panel | **New session** on the **Sessions** group, or **New session here** on a worktree or folder row |
| An open session strip | **+** (**New session**), or **Cmd/Ctrl+T** |
| An existing session | **New session from this one** on its row menu |
| A message in a conversation | **New session from here** on the message's right-click menu |

For a quick question that does not belong to a task, use **Ask Kepler**, the chat in the top bar's side panel. Any agent that runs in **Chat** can answer there. To move the chat into a task, click **Continue in a new task**. On that task's session, **Open source session** reopens the chat in the panel. See [Ask Kepler](/kepler/ask-kepler).

### Draft session tabs

**New session** opens a draft tab, not a menu. Nothing starts until you send the first message, so you can write the prompt, attach files, and pick the agent first. The tab takes its name from the first line of your prompt. When the tab strip has room, the tab is marked **(draft)**. In the context panel, the same row reads **Draft**.

To choose where the session runs, open the draft's target picker. It offers the following:

| Part | What it does |
|---|---|
| **Search branches and folders** | Filters the list as you type |
| **Attached to this task** | The worktrees and folders already attached to the task, including **All worktrees and folders**: *Runs in the task folder and has access to all worktrees and folders* |
| **Branches** | Other branches of the task's repositories. Pick one to start the session on that branch |
| **New branch from this** | Starts the session on a new branch based on the branch you picked |

Every session sees the task's attached resources wherever it runs. **All worktrees and folders** changes only the session's working directory.

A session receives the task's shared context by default. To start a session that forms its own view of the work, untick the **Task context** chip in the draft composer's footer, beside **Attach a file** and the microphone. The task context is the task's prompt and notes, and later changes to it reach the agent with your next message.

Right-click a draft tab or its row in the context panel for these actions:

- **Discard draft**: removes the draft. If the draft holds text or attachments, Kepler asks first: **Discard new session?**
- **Move left** or **Move right**: moves the draft among the other tabs.

If **Show tabs on the task page** is on, the draft has a regular tab menu instead: **Pin tab** or **Unpin tab**, **Keep open** while the tab is a preview, and **Close tab**, the only way to close it. See [Task View](/kepler/task-view#tabs-and-groups).

### Branching and renaming a session

**New session from this one** starts a sibling session in the same task, worktree, agent, and account. The new agent can read the source conversation.

**New session from here** does the same, but the new agent reads the source only up to and including the message you picked. The command is available once that message has finished streaming, and not on a terminal or external session.

To go back to the original, choose **Open source session** on the new session's menu.

To give a session your own name, choose **Rename session** on its row menu. Agents can also name and rename the Chat sessions they start, through Kepler's workspace tools.

***

## Agent, model, mode, and effort

To choose the agent, model, mode, and effort, use the **Agent settings** pill on the composer, when you start a session or while it runs.

An **agent preset** is a saved set of one agent's model, mode, effort, and options. To save the current settings as a preset, click **Save preset** at the bottom of the menu. To create or edit presets, click **Manage presets** in the **Preset** list. See [Settings](/kepler/settings-agents#agent-presets).

| Choice | Changeable mid-session | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| **Agent** | No | Fixed once the session exists. To use another agent, start a new session |
| **Preset** | Yes | **No preset**, or one of this agent's presets, once it has any. A preset you change reads **{name} (unsaved)** |
| **Start in** | No | **Chat** or **Terminal**, for an agent that offers both. To use the other mode, start a new session; see [How a session runs](#how-a-session-runs) |
| **Model** | Yes | Models are per provider, so each agent has its own catalog and a model never moves to another agent. At the default, the row reads **Default · {model}**, naming the model the default resolves to |
| **Mode** | Yes | The agent's own permission modes |
| **Effort** | Yes | Reasoning or thinking depth, for agents that offer it |
| **Options** | Some | The agent's on/off options, such as **Artifacts**, ticked in one menu |
| Startup options | No | Set when you launch the session. A Terminal launch offers the CLI's own options; see [How a session runs](#how-a-session-runs) |

A change applies from your next message. It never interrupts the turn in progress.

The menu also shows its state:

- An option row reads **Agent default** until you pick a value.
- **{name} settings changed** appears when a session's preset was edited after the session started. Click **Apply** to use the new settings.

If a session's model changes, for example because the default now resolves to a different model, the conversation shows *Model changed from {from} to {to}.*

The model and mode lists update on their own, so a newly released model appears without restarting Kepler.

The same menu lists the MCP servers the agent loads for this repository. To change them, click **Manage**. See [MCP Servers](/kepler/mcp-servers).

When the menu cannot offer the usual choices, it shows one of these messages:

| The menu reads | When |
|---|---|
| **Loading your last agent choice…** | Kepler is restoring the agent you used last |
| **Set up a coding agent** | No agent is set up. See below |
| **Sign in to {agent} to start a session** | The chosen agent is installed but signed out |
| **{agent} didn't share its options** | Kepler could not read the agent's models and modes. You can still start a session on the agent's own model and mode, or click **Retry** |

To set one up from **Set up a coding agent**, click **Install or locate {name}** for an agent. If you installed an agent yourself, click **Rescan**. If your agents are on another machine, click **Choose** to open **Settings → Remote environments**.

If you have more than one account, the **Agent** list groups accounts under their agent. The list ends with **Add another account** and **Install another agent**.

By default, a new task, the Dashboard composer, and a new draft tab start with the agent, model, and mode you last picked. To always start with one agent instead, open **Settings → Tasks → New tasks**, pick the agent and its settings in **New sessions start with**, and clear **Start each session on the agent you used last**. To start one session with other settings, change them in the draft's **Agent settings**. See [Settings](/kepler/settings-tasks#default-agent).

### Which agents are available

Kepler supports Claude Code, Codex, GitHub Copilot, Cursor, Auggie, OpenCode, Grok Build, Pi, and Google Antigravity, plus any custom agent you add. Kepler offers only the agents you have installed. See [Agent Integrations](/kepler/agent-integrations).

***

## Several accounts for one agent

Claude Code, Codex, GitHub Copilot, Auggie, and Grok Build can each have more than one signed-in account. To manage an agent's accounts, open **Settings → Agents**, expand the agent, and find **Accounts**:

Each account keeps its own credentials but shares your skills, agents, commands, and settings. An account keeps its own conversation history unless it shares history with the CLI, which Claude Code, Codex, and GitHub Copilot accounts can do. A Copilot account shares history unless you choose otherwise.

| Control | What it does |
|---|---|
| First row, badged **Default** | The agent's own login, in its normal config directory |
| **Add account** | Adds an account with its own credentials. For Claude Code, Codex, and GitHub Copilot, you choose **Keep separate** or **Share with the CLI** for its history |
| **Account name** | Rename a row in place. The name is what you pick from later |
| **Sign in** / **Sign out** | Authenticates or clears that account alone |
| **Check usage** | Reads that account's plan usage. Grayed out only when **Check plan usage with each agent's provider** is turned off in **Settings → Agents → Usage limits** |
| **Switch account…** | On a signed-in Claude Code account's row menu. Signs that account in with a different Claude login, after a confirmation that counts the running sessions using it |
| **Remove account** | Signs the account out and deletes its local data, but leaves your shared skills, agents, and settings alone. Sessions whose conversations are stored only in that account are deleted with it; see below |
| Color swatch | At the left of each added account's row: pick a color, or **No color**. The default account's ⊘ **No color** mark means it stays uncolored, not that it is off |

An account's color tints the agent icon on session tabs, in the context panel, and on the terminal status bar. You can tell sessions on different accounts apart by their color.

**Switch account…** opens the same sign-in as **Add account**. If your browser is already signed in, choose a different account on the sign-in page. On the default row, the switch also changes the account the `claude` command uses in your own terminals, and the confirmation says so.

**An added account can stop sharing your configuration.** An added account links to your own configuration instead of copying it. That configuration includes your settings, instructions, skills, agents, commands, plugins, rules, and hooks. If the agent saves a change to one of these while signed in to that account, the account gets its own copy and stops following yours. Kepler then shows **This account stopped sharing your {items}** under the account's row.

Expand the warning to see which file the account copied, with the paths of **This account's copy** and **Your {item}**. Then choose one of the following:

- **Ask Kepler to resolve**: opens a new Ask Kepler chat with a prompt that asks the agent to compare the 2 copies and copy what matters into your shared copy. Nothing is sent until you send it. See [Ask Kepler](/kepler/ask-kepler).
- **Share your {item} again**: links the account back to your file, after a confirmation. Kepler saves the account's own copy as a backup next to it, so nothing is lost.
- **Keep its own {item}**: keeps the account's copy. **Share your {item} again** then moves to the account's row menu.

**Removing an account tells you what it will remove.** The **Remove {name}?** dialog counts the running sessions it will stop and the sessions it will permanently delete, because their conversations are stored only in this account. To keep those sessions, first click **Move to CLI account** under **Keep these conversations**. The sessions stay in their tasks, and removing the account then deletes nothing. If you do not move them, **Continue to remove** asks you to confirm the deletion once more.

**How many accounts you can add depends on your GitKraken plan.** Pro and higher plans have no limit. If your plan stops covering an account that a running session uses, the session tells you, so you can switch it to another account or upgrade.

### Choosing an account for a session

If 2 or more accounts are signed in, the **Agent** list shows one row per account, labeled with the account name. You pick the agent and the account in one click, in the **New task** composer or in a draft session tab.

With one account, the agent keeps a single row, with that account shown beside its name.

A session starts on the account you picked. Later, you can move it to another signed-in account of the same agent and keep the conversation. When more than one account exists, session tabs name the account. If a tab's account has since been removed, the tab reads **(account missing)**.

Kepler reads usage figures from the account the session runs on, not from the first account in the list.

#### Moving a session to another account

To move a session to another account, use any of these:

- **Continue as** on the session's row or tab menu.
- The **Account** row in the composer's **Agent settings**: **Restart conversation as** on a live session, or **Resume as** on a dormant one.
- The agent and account part of a Terminal session's status bar.
- **Continue as {login}** on the usage-limit banner. See [When you hit a usage limit](#when-you-hit-a-usage-limit).
- The **Resume** or **Restart** split button on a dormant session, when another account could take the conversation.

Each list shows the agent's other accounts with their login, color, and usage, and checks the current one. When you pick an account, Kepler restarts the agent with this conversation as that account and confirms **Continued as {login}**.

Some accounts look different in the list:

- An account that keeps its own history is grayed out as **Separate history**, because it cannot read this conversation. To change that, open **Settings → Agents**.
- A signed-out account offers **Sign in…**.
- An account signed in with an API key or a token has no login name. It reads **Signed in**, and you can pick it like any other.

If the session is busy, with a turn running or work still going in the background, Kepler asks first: **Stop this session and continue as {login}?** **Stop and switch** stops the session and resumes the conversation on the new account. If the session is still restarting, Kepler asks you to try again in a moment.

***

## Signing in through your browser

Claude Code and Codex both sign in through your browser, without a terminal. To sign in, open **Settings → Agents**, click **Sign in**, and pick a method under **Choose how you want to authenticate.**

| Connection | Claude Code | Codex |
|---|---|---|
| Local | Kepler runs the sign-in, your browser opens, and Kepler shows a status line instead of a terminal | Browser sign-in with your ChatGPT account |
| Remote or SSH | **Sign in with browser**: sign in in your local browser, then paste the code it returns | **ChatGPT (device code)**: sign in with a one-time code in your browser |

A local sign-in offers these controls:

- **Open sign-in in browser**: opens the sign-in page if the browser did not open on its own.
- **Sign-in link**, with **Copy link**: the same address, so you can open it in another browser or profile.
- **Paste the code from your browser**, with **Paste from clipboard** and **Submit code**: appears if the callback cannot complete. If Kepler rejects the code, copy the full code and try again.

On a remote, the same button and **Sign-in link** field sit above the code. Codex shows a **One-time code** to enter there, and Claude Code shows a field for the code your browser returns. If your ChatGPT workspace turns off device sign-in, use **Import local Codex login** or an API key instead.

Auggie signs in the same way locally. On a remote target, Auggie asks you to paste the JSON it returns. GitHub Copilot uses a device code: click **Sign in with GitHub**, then enter a one-time code at `github.com/login/device`.

On a remote Codex target you can also **Import local Codex login** to copy your local Codex sign-in to that target. See [Remote Environments](/kepler/remote-environments).

Before a login expires, Kepler warns you how many days are left. To renew it, sign in again.

***

## How a session runs
