# Task Settings
URL: https://help.gitkraken.com/kepler/settings-tasks/
product: Kepler
feature: Settings
content_type: reference
audience: developer
plan_required: all
status: GA
last_verified: 2026-11

Use **Settings → Tasks** to choose how new tasks start and how a task's page looks, and to manage your task groups. A task is one piece of work: its prompt, the agent sessions working on it, and the worktree or folder they work in.

## New tasks

**New tasks** sets what Kepler preselects for every new task: the agent, where the task makes changes, where its panel opens on the Dashboard, how branches and folders are named, and whether Kepler names the task for you. These values belong to the environment you are working on, so in a remote window they are the remote machine's.

### Default agent

**New sessions start with** sets the agent that the **New task** composer, the Dashboard's composer, and a new draft session start with. It is the same agent-settings pill as in the composer: pick the agent and account, and optionally an [agent preset](/kepler/settings-agents#agent-presets), a model, and other options. Kepler saves each pick as you make it.

**Start each session on the agent you used last**, below the pill, is on by default. With it, your first session uses the pill's agent, and each later session starts with the agent, model, and mode you last picked. To start every session on the pill's agent and settings, clear it. A task that an agent created and that has no session yet starts with the agent that created it. Kepler does not remember an Action's own agent as your last pick.

If no agent is installed, Kepler hides the control. If you later uninstall the agent you saved, the row warns you to pick another. This setting does not apply to Ask Kepler, which has its own default in [Settings → Agents](/kepler/settings-agents).

An [Action](/kepler/actions) inherits this configuration unless it names an agent of its own.

### Where new tasks make changes

**Where new tasks make changes** sets what a repository starts on when you attach it to a new task in the **New task** composer. It has these options:

| Option | What it does |
|---|---|
| **Isolated worktree** | The default. Creates a new branch in its own worktree, so agents can work in parallel |
| **New branch** | Creates a new branch in the repository's own checkout, with no worktree |
| **Current branch** | Works on whichever branch the repository's own checkout has |

This setting is only the default. For a single task, the repository chip's own **Base branch** and **Isolated worktree** controls override it. See [Create a task](/kepler/create-task#configuring-a-repository).

**With New branch and Current branch, commits land on whichever branch is checked out at the time**, because both work in the repository's own checkout. If another task is already working in that checkout, Kepler says so and offers to switch that repository to an isolated worktree instead.

You can edit **Branch prefix**, **Worktrees folder**, and **Tasks folder** whichever option you choose, because a single task can still ask for a new branch or a worktree.

### Where a new task opens on the Dashboard

**Where a new task opens on the Dashboard** sets where the panel of a task you start, or open from a notification, appears among the Dashboard's open panels:

| Option | What it does |
|---|---|
| **Beside the focused panel** | The default. Opens the panel next to the one you are reading, or at the end once the panels fill more than one row |
| **At the end** | Always opens the panel after every open panel |

### Branch prefix

The following setting starts the name of every branch Kepler creates:

| Setting | What it controls | Default |
|---|---|---|
| **Branch prefix** | *Starts the name of every branch Kepler creates. A repo can set its own in its settings.* | `kepler/` |

The prefix applies to **automatic** names only. Kepler uses a branch name you type exactly as you typed it, so a repository with an enforced `feat/` or `fix/` push rule still works. If your prefix does not end in a separator, Kepler adds a `/`, so `team` becomes `team/`, while `ea-` stays as you typed it.

To override the prefix for one repository, use its [Edit repo](/kepler/settings-repositories#edit-a-repository) page under **Settings → Repositories**.

### Folder locations

Kepler uses 3 folder settings to decide where to put things:

| Setting | Where it is | What it controls | Default |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Worktrees folder** | Tasks → New tasks | *Where Kepler creates the worktree for each new task.* | `~/kepler/worktrees` |
| **Tasks folder** | Tasks → New tasks | *Each task gets a folder here for its attachments and files.* | `~/kepler/tasks` |
| **Repositories folder** | [Repositories](/kepler/settings-repositories#repositories-folder) | Where Kepler clones repositories, and where it looks for repositories to add | `~/kepler/repositories` |

Type a path, or click **Choose a folder** beside the field to browse. An edit saves when you leave the field.

The fields also warn you about paths that do not work the way you might expect:

- If a **Worktrees folder** has text before `<REPOSITORY_PATH>`, Kepler adds each repository's full path after that text, and the field suggests 2 patterns that work: worktrees next to each repository, or a subfolder per repository. On Windows, Kepler does not save such a path.
- If the **Repositories folder** does not exist yet, the field tells you that Kepler creates it when you clone.

### The Variables menu

A folder field that takes variables has a **Variables** menu beside it. Pick a variable, such as **REPOSITORY PATH**, to insert it at the cursor. Kepler fills it in when it creates the folder, so one pattern works for every repository. Each field offers only the variables it can fill in:

| Field | Variables offered |
|---|---|
| **Worktrees folder** | `<REPOSITORY_PATH>` (*Main repo folder*), `<REPOSITORY_NAME>` (*Repo name*) |
| **Repositories folder** | `<REPOSITORY_NAME>` |
| **Tasks folder** | None |

For example, `<REPOSITORY_PATH>/.worktrees/<REPOSITORY_NAME>` nests each worktree inside the repository it belongs to.

Per-repository commands have a **Variables** menu of their own, with 2 more variables. See [Per-repository commands](/kepler/settings-repositories#per-repository-commands).

### Automatically name new tasks

The following setting names new tasks for you:

| Setting | What it controls | Default |
|---|---|---|
| **Automatically name new tasks** | *Names a new task with AI from its prompt and attached resources. A task created from a single issue or PR keeps that item's name.* | On |

You need a paid GitKraken subscription to turn this setting on. Without one, a lock replaces the checkbox while the setting is off, but you can always turn it off. A change takes effect on the next task you create.

## Task page

**Task page** sets how a task's page looks in this window. Kepler saves these settings on this machine:

| Setting | What it controls | Default |
|---|---|---|
| **Show tabs on the task page** | Keeps sessions, worktrees, and resources open as tabs you can pin, drag between groups, and arrange side by side | Off |
| **Preview tabs** | *A single click opens a preview that the next click replaces. Double-click, or edit, to keep it open.* | On |

With **Show tabs on the task page** off, each column of a task shows one thing at a time, and you switch between them from the list on the left. **Preview tabs** works only with it turned on. Sessions always open as permanent tabs. See [The task view](/kepler/task-view).

## Groups

**Groups** lists all your task groups, including archived ones. To open it from the Dashboard, choose **Manage groups…** in a group header's menu.

- To add a group, click **New group** in the section header.
- To edit a group's name or color, click its name.
- To reorder groups, drag a row by its grip.
- To archive or delete a group, use its **⋮** menu. You can archive a group once all its tasks are archived.

Archived groups are listed under **Archived**, where their menu has **Restore group**. Deleting a group never deletes its tasks; they stay, ungrouped. See [Your groups](/kepler/arranging-your-work#your-groups).

***

---

---
# Repository Settings
URL: https://help.gitkraken.com/kepler/settings-repositories/
product: Kepler
feature: Settings
content_type: reference
audience: developer
plan_required: all
status: GA
last_verified: 2026-11

Use **Settings → Repositories** to choose where Kepler clones repositories, add and edit the repositories and folders Kepler tracks, update and clean up worktrees and branches, and group repositories into projects.

## Repositories folder

To choose where Kepler clones repositories, use this setting:

| Setting | What it controls | Default |
|---|---|---|
| **Repositories folder** | Where Kepler clones repositories, and where it looks for repositories to add | `~/kepler/repositories` |

To add every repository already in that folder, click **Scan for repositories** beside the field. Kepler scans only when you change the setting or click the button. A scan skips any repository you removed; to bring one back, add it yourself with **Add repo**. Repositories a scan adds start untrusted. See [Trust a repository](#trust-a-repository).

After a scan that added repositories, **Undo** removes them again, except any you have used or changed since the scan. To scan, the setting needs a full folder path before any variable in it.

If the folder does not exist yet, Kepler creates it when you clone. The field takes the `<REPOSITORY_NAME>` variable. See [The Variables menu](/kepler/settings-tasks#the-variables-menu).

## Your repos and folders

**Your repos and folders** lists every repository Kepler tracks and every folder you have attached to a task. Each row shows its name, its path on disk, and how many commands it has. A repository or folder you have not trusted shows an **Untrusted** badge. The section has these controls:

| Control | What it does |
|---|---|
| **Filter repos and folders** | Narrows the list by name |
| A row | Click it to open the repository's **Edit repo** page, or the folder's page |
| **Add repo** | Opens the **Add repo** page. See below |
| **Add folder…** | Adds a plain folder |
| Trash icon | Stops tracking the repository or folder, and leaves the folder on disk |

If a folder you added later becomes a Git repository, for example after `git init`, Kepler treats it as a repository from then on.

Removing a repository deletes its sessions, terminals, and configured commands, and ends any live agent and terminal sessions tied to it. Kepler asks you to confirm first.

### Add a repository

To add a repository, follow these steps:

1. Click **Add repo**.
2. In **Folder or URL**, paste a URL to clone, or pick a folder that already holds a repository. You can also drop a folder onto the page, or click **Create a new repo instead**.
3. Kepler shows what it found as a card, and says what it will do, such as clone into a new folder or add an existing clone as it is. It also tells you when the repository is already in Kepler, or the folder is not a Git repository. Edit the name, description, and branch prefix on the card if you need to.
4. Click **Add repo**, or **Clone** for a URL.

You can leave the page while a clone runs; the clone continues, and a notification tells you when it finishes or why it failed.

### Edit a repository

Click a repository's row to open its **Edit repo** page. The page shows the repository's path, its remote, and its branches. When Kepler knows the remote's host, click the remote's provider line to open the repository there (**Open on {provider}**). The page has these parts:

| Part | What it holds |
|---|---|
| **Name** | How this repo is listed in Kepler. Leave it empty to use the folder name |
| **Aliases** | Short names for this repo when talking to agents, separated by commas, such as `api, backend` |
| **Description** | What this repo is for. Agents working in it read this |
| **Trusted** | Lets Kepler run git in this repo. See [Trust a repository](#trust-a-repository) |
| **Branch prefix** | Overrides the prefix from **Settings → Tasks** for this repository only. See below |
| **Branch synchronization** | How this repo's branches update by default (**Rebase** or **Merge**), and whether to push after an update. See [Update worktrees](#update-worktrees) |
| **Commands** | Shell commands for this repository. See [Per-repository commands](#per-repository-commands) |
| **MCP servers** | Extra tools your agents get in this repo, on top of their own lists. See [MCP Servers](/kepler/mcp-servers) |

**Name**, **Aliases**, and **Description** are optional. The page has no **Save** button: each field saves on its own and shows its save status. Some fields have more rules:

- A repository you name keeps that name exactly.
- An alias cannot contain a colon, or repeat another repository's alias or name.
- Agents working in this repo read the description, so write a full sentence.

#### Branch prefix, per repository

The **Branch prefix** control has 3 options:

| Option | What it does |
|---|---|
| **Default ({value})** | Uses the prefix from **Settings → Tasks** |
| **None** | Creates task branches with no prefix |
| **Custom** | A prefix for this repository only |

**New task branches will look like** shows an example branch name for your choice.

Kepler does not save a prefix that the repository already uses as a local branch name. Rename that branch, or choose another prefix.

#### Trust a repository

Kepler runs no git in a repository or folder you have not trusted, because a repository's own settings can run programs. Until you trust it, its status, branches, and changes stay empty.

To trust a repository or folder, turn on **Trusted** on its page. You can also click **Trust** where Kepler asks, such as in a task's Changes view. While **Trusted** is on, agent sessions in it also skip the agent's own trust question.

### Per-repository commands

Use commands to run your dev server, tests, or build from a task's worktree in one click. A command can also run when Kepler creates a new worktree, for example to install dependencies. Commands are shell commands for one repository.

To add a command, click **Add command** in the **Commands** section of the Edit repo page. Each command row has 3 fields:

| Field | What it does |
|---|---|
| Name | A label, for example *Install deps*. You pick the command by this name from the **Run** menu |
| Command | The shell command, for example `pnpm install`. Its **Variables** menu inserts any of the variables below |
| **Run on worktree creation** | Runs the command each time Kepler creates a worktree for this repository. Off by default |

To save a row, click **Add command** (or **Save** on a stored command), or press **⌘ Enter** (**Ctrl + Enter** on Windows and Linux). Each command saves on its own.

Commands accept 4 variables, which Kepler fills in when the command runs:

| Variable | Resolves to |
|---|---|
| `<REPOSITORY_PATH>` | Main repo folder |
| `<REPOSITORY_NAME>` | Repo name |
| `<SOURCE_PATH>` | Where files come from (the main repo, or the source worktree when forking) |
| `<WORKTREE_PATH>` | The new worktree folder |

To reorder commands, drag a row by its handle, or move it from the keyboard with **Alt + ↑** and **Alt + ↓**. A new order saves at once. The order sets the order of the **Run** menu, and the order in which commands set to run on worktree creation run.

A row needs both a name and a command before you can save it. A closed row that is not saved yet shows **Not saved**. **Remove command** deletes a saved command, and the notification that follows offers **Undo**.

Commands set to run on worktree creation run one at a time, in list order. If one fails, Kepler skips the rest. Each command runs in the new worktree's folder through your login shell, so tools set up in your shell profile, such as `nvm`, are available. Each command has a 10-minute timeout.

A failed command does not undo the worktree. The worktree exists but may not be usable. To fix it:

1. Read the command output in the task.
2. Correct the command here.
3. Run it again from the **Run** menu.

To run a command from the task view, right-click a worktree row in the task's context panel and use **Run command here**. It lists that repository's commands and runs the one you pick in that worktree, in a terminal. For a repository with no commands yet, **Create command…** opens the Edit repo page. To stop a running command, use the run button or its menu.

### Copy ignored files into new worktrees

A new worktree starts without your repository's git-ignored files, such as `.env`. To copy some of them, list them in a `.worktreeinclude` file at the repository's root, in the same format as `.gitignore`. Kepler copies them before any command set to run on worktree creation starts. It copies only files that git also ignores in the new worktree, so a copied secret cannot be committed by mistake, and it never overwrites a file already there.

## Worktrees and branches

To update, clean up, or delete worktrees and local branches across your repositories, click **Manage worktrees and branches** on the Repositories page. The **Worktrees and branches** sub-page opens.

On the sub-page, you can see which worktrees and local branches are stale, update the ones that are behind, and delete what is done. It lists every worktree, and every local branch that no worktree holds, grouped by repository, and a summary says how many look safe to delete. Kepler deletes nothing until you ask, and never deletes the base branch, which has a **Base** badge.

The sub-page has these controls:

| Control | What it does |
|---|---|
| **Search branch, path or repo** | Narrows the list. Every word you type must match the branch, the path, or the repository name |
| **Show worktrees and branches** | Filters by status: **Safe to delete**, **Needs update**, **Conflicts**, **Stale**, or **All** |
| **Show worktrees, branches or both** | Shows **All**, **Worktrees only**, or **Branches only** |
| **Stale after** *n* **days** | Sets how many days without activity make a row stale. Defaults to 14 |
| **Re-check** | Fetches every repository's remotes and checks the list again |
| **Select all** | Selects the rows in the current view |
| Selection bar | Has **Clear**, **Create task**, **Update**, and **Delete**. **Update** and **Delete** act only on selected rows you can see |

**Create task** opens the **New task** composer with the selected worktrees and branches already added: each worktree as it is, and each branch without a worktree as a branch to work on. Kepler creates nothing until you start or prepare the task. See [Create a task](/kepler/create-task).

Each row shows the following:

- Where it stands with its upstream: commits to push (↑) and pull (↓), **No upstream**, or **Upstream gone**.
- How it compares with its base, such as **3 behind main**, and how many files are uncommitted.
- How long since it was last touched, and why it may be finished, such as being merged into its base.
- The tasks, sessions, and pull request tied to it. An **External** count shows sessions started outside Kepler.

With a Jira or Jira Server account connected, a row whose branch name references a Jira issue shows a chip for that issue. To open the issue in your browser, click the chip. See [Issue Tracker Integrations](/kepler/issue-tracker-integrations).

A row counts as one or more of the following:

- **Safe to delete**: its work has landed (merged into the base, or its pull request merged or closed with the upstream gone), and nothing is uncommitted, unpushed, or in use.
- **Needs update**: behind the base branch with no known conflict, so an update can bring it up to date.
- **Conflicts**: behind the base branch, and merging the base in would conflict, so you have to update it by hand.
- **Stale**: no activity for longer than the stale threshold, but nothing proves the work landed. Deleting it can lose uncommitted or unpushed work.

**Needs update** and **Conflicts** leave out rows that are safe to delete.

### Delete worktrees and branches

Select rows, then click **Delete**. The confirmation says what is lost:

- For worktrees, their folders are removed from disk with anything the dialog lists. **Also delete the branches** deletes each worktree's branch too.
- For local branches, commits that exist only on them are lost. The dialog marks each branch that is not merged as **not merged**. **Force delete branches that are not merged** deletes those too, and **Also delete the branches on the remote** deletes the remote branches.

Kepler keeps any branch it cannot delete safely and says why, for example when a worktree still has it checked out. A local branch with commits that are not merged is kept too, and the result offers **Force delete** for it, which deletes the branch with those commits.

Kepler never deletes a repository's main checkout. It keeps any worktree that still has uncommitted or unpushed work, other tasks, running agent sessions, or a lock from another tool, and says why for each one. Where forcing can help, the result offers **Force delete**, which discards the listed work and ends the agent sessions running there.

### Update worktrees

To bring several worktrees and local branches up to date with their base branch at once:

1. On the Worktrees and branches sub-page, select the worktrees and branches.
2. Click **Update**. The **Update worktrees** dialog opens. Nothing changes until you confirm.
3. Under **How to update**, keep **Default** to use each repository's own setting (see [Edit a repository](#edit-a-repository)), or choose **Rebase** or **Merge** for this update.
4. Under **Push after update**, keep **Default**, or choose **Don't push**, **Push**, or **Push + Publish**. **Push** pushes only branches that already have a remote branch; **Push + Publish** also publishes the ones that do not.
5. Review the plan. Each row says how the branch will update and where it will be pushed, or **Skipped** with the reason, such as uncommitted changes or a conflict.
6. Click **Update**.

A branch with no worktree is updated in place; it is skipped if a worktree holds it or the main checkout has uncommitted changes. If Kepler prepared an update but could not apply it automatically, Kepler keeps it for you to review instead of discarding it.

When the update finishes, you can undo one row with **Roll back**, or every row with **Roll back all**. If you did not push during the update, **Push** and **Push all** push the updated branches that have an upstream. Kepler does not push a branch that moved since the update. The finished report stays in every window until you click **Dismiss**.

## Projects

Use **Projects** to group repositories that belong together under one name, such as a frontend and a backend you change together. A project's repositories act as a unit. The section has these controls:

| Control | What it does |
|---|---|
| A row | Opens the project's page |
| **New project** | Opens a page where you name a project and pick its repositories. **Add from folder** adds a repository without leaving the page |

To create the project, give it a name and click **Create**. After that, its page has no **Save** button: its name and each repository you tick or untick save as you change them. A folder's page saves its name and description the same way.

To delete a project, click **Delete project** on its page. Its repositories stay in your repository list.

***

---

# Integration Settings
URL: https://help.gitkraken.com/kepler/settings-integrations/
product: Kepler
feature: Settings
content_type: reference
audience: developer
plan_required: all
status: GA
last_verified: 2026-11

Use **Settings → Integrations** to connect the issue trackers and Git hosts you start tasks from, and to follow agent sessions you run in your own terminal.

## Issues and pull requests

Connect your issue and pull request providers to see their issues and pull requests in the **New task** composer and in [the Kepler interface](/kepler/kepler-interface). Kepler lists every supported provider, with the connected ones first: Azure DevOps, Azure DevOps Server, Bitbucket, Bitbucket Data Center, GitHub, GitHub Enterprise, GitLab, GitLab Self-Hosted, Jira, Jira Server / Data Center, Linear, Trello, and Asana.

Each provider row shows these controls and states:

| Control | What it does |
|---|---|
| **Connect** | Connects a provider you have not connected |
| **Connected** | Marks a working connection |
| **Reconnect** | Refreshes a token on a row marked **Sign-in expired** |
| **Cannot connect to server** | The server did not answer; the integration stays connected and the state clears on its own |
| **Unexpected response** | Kepler could not read the provider's answer, so some items may be missing; reconnecting does not fix it |
| **Disconnect** | Disconnects the account from every GitKraken product that uses it; other accounts stay connected |
| **Refresh** | Checks every provider's connection again, from the section header |

If a row shows **Cannot connect to server**, check that the server is reachable from your network or VPN. If **Unexpected response** stays, check for a proxy or gateway between Kepler and the provider.

Providers connect through your GitKraken account, so you sign in to GitKraken before you can manage them.

### Self-hosted providers

A self-hosted provider, such as GitHub Enterprise, Azure DevOps Server, Bitbucket Data Center, or Jira Server / Data Center, connects with a personal access token. Click **Connect**, enter the **Server URL** and **Personal access token**, then click **Save connection**. Kepler checks the token against your server and adds the connection to your GitKraken account. Until it finishes, the row shows **Cloud sync pending**.

A connected self-hosted provider lists each server on its own row. Each server keeps its own repositories and issues:

- To connect another server, click **Add connection** on the provider's row. Connecting more than 1 server needs an active GitKraken plan or trial.
- To renew an expired or rejected token, click **Replace token** on that server's row.
- To make a server the provider's default connection, click **Set as primary**.

### Choose what's visible

To hide organizations, repositories, or tracker projects you do not want in Kepler, click **Choose what's visible…** under the provider's row, then untick the items to hide. Every connected provider except Trello and Asana has it. Hidden items leave the dashboard, the launcher, and pickers, and tasks and branches already linked to them keep working. The choice is saved on your GitKraken account.

### Accounts and organizations

When a provider has more than 1 account, an **Accounts** block lists them. **Set as primary** chooses which account Kepler acts as, and **Read from this account** chooses which account Kepler reads issues and pull requests from. These can be different accounts, but agents' GitKraken MCP server always acts as the primary account. See [MCP servers](/kepler/settings-agents#mcp-servers).

When an organization refuses a working connection, because it blocks third-party OAuth apps or has not approved GitKraken, the row names the organization and says that its items are not shown. The row links to a fix, such as **Request access on GitHub**.

For per-provider setup, see [Issue Tracker Integrations](/kepler/issue-tracker-integrations) and [Pull Request Integrations](/kepler/pull-request-integrations).

## Your terminal

To follow agent sessions you start in your own terminal, use this setting:

| Setting | What it controls | Default |
|---|---|---|
| **Show sessions started outside Kepler** | Lists sessions you start in your own terminal, so you can follow and continue them in Kepler | On |

The setting covers every agent Kepler can follow this way. See [Agent Sessions](/kepler/agent-sessions#sessions-started-outside-kepler).

If a running agent session stops reporting to Kepler, every window shows *Agent sessions aren't reporting to Kepler*, with a **Repair** button. **Repair** reinstalls the reporting configuration. Restart any session that still does not report. For another computer's sessions, repair from that computer.

***

# Action Settings
URL: https://help.gitkraken.com/kepler/settings-actions/
product: Kepler
feature: Settings
content_type: reference
audience: developer
plan_required: all
status: GA
last_verified: 2026-11

Use **Settings → Actions** to save the prompts you use often and run them on a task, issue, or pull request without typing them again. An **Action** is an editable named prompt. The page has these sections:

| Section | What it holds |
|---|---|
| **Suggested Actions** | The Action that the button on each kind of item suggests: **Tasks**, **Issues**, **Pull requests I authored**, and **Pull requests from others** |
| **All Actions** | The built-in Actions under **Built in** and yours under **Custom**, each with what it does and where it is available |

Under **Suggested Actions**:

- Set a picker to **None** to leave only the menu on that kind of item.
- **Suggest automatically** switches a new task's button to the suggested Action when you link an issue or pull request to it. Turn it off to keep **Start**.

Under **All Actions**, click a row to edit it, use **Restore default** on a row you have edited, or use **Delete** on a custom row. To delete an Action that an [automation](/kepler/automations) runs, delete the automation first.

An Action can run with one of your [agent presets](/kepler/settings-agents#agent-presets), and the preset picks the agent. If the Action's preset no longer exists, its row shows **Preset unavailable for this agent** and the Action runs without it. To fix it, choose another preset in the Action's editor.

To create an Action, click **New Action** in the **All Actions** section header. **Restore all defaults**, beside it, discards every edit. An Action you create or edit opens as a sub-page.

Kepler has 4 built-in Actions, and each one is the default suggested Action for one kind of item:

- **Tasks** default to **Implement**.
- **Issues** default to **Plan**.
- Pull requests you authored default to **Address Feedback**.
- Pull requests from others default to **Review**.

For what the built-in Actions ask an agent to do, how the editor's **Title**, **Prompt**, **Available on**, and **Agent** fields behave, and how an Action picks the agent it runs on, see [Actions](/kepler/actions).

***

---

---
# App Settings
URL: https://help.gitkraken.com/kepler/settings-app/
product: Kepler
feature: Settings
content_type: reference
audience: developer
plan_required: all
status: GA
last_verified: 2026-11

Use these Settings pages to change how Kepler itself looks and behaves:

- [General](#general): language, the chat's send key, the default editor, windows and dialogs, keeping agents running, and usage insights
- [Notifications](#notifications): which agent events notify you, on the desktop and in Kepler
- [Appearance](#appearance): light or dark appearance and themes, the Dashboard's views, the chat, the terminal font, and the code font and diff layout
- [Voice](#voice): dictation, with its models and learned words, and read aloud
- [Keyboard shortcuts](#keyboard-shortcuts): look up and change Kepler's keyboard shortcuts

***

## General

Use **General** to choose Kepler's language, which key sends a chat message, which editor opens your files, how its windows open, whether agents keep running when your machine would sleep or Kepler restarts, and whether Kepler keeps usage statistics on your computer.

### Language

**Language** has 1 setting:

| Setting | What it controls | Default | Options |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Language** | The display language for Kepler's interface | English | English, Español |

The language also applies to native dialogs, not only to the in-app interface.

### Chat

**Send messages with** chooses the key that sends a message from the chat box: **Enter**, the default, or **⌘ Enter** (**Ctrl + Enter** on Windows and Linux). With **Enter**, **Shift + Enter** starts a new line. With **⌘ Enter**, **Enter** starts a new line. In the browser on a phone or tablet, **Enter** always starts a new line.

### Default editor

**Default editor** has 1 setting:

| Setting | What it controls | Default |
|---|---|---|
| **Open files and folders in** | The app that **Open in** and **⌘ ⇧**-click (**Ctrl + Shift**-click on Windows and Linux) on a file link use. The options are **Last used app**, each editor Kepler finds on this machine, and your system's default app | Last used app |

With your system's default app, files open without line numbers, and folders open in Finder, Explorer, or your file manager. If Kepler cannot open any editor from the window you are in, the setting says so.

### Windows and dialogs

These settings set how windows and folder dialogs work on this machine:

| Setting | What it controls | Default |
|---|---|---|
| **Restore windows on launch** | *Reopens the windows you had open, with their size, page and connection. Turn off to start with one window.* | On |
| **Always use the custom folder picker** | Local windows open your system's folder dialog, and windows connected to another machine use Kepler's own folder picker, which can browse that machine. Turn this on to use Kepler's picker in every window | Off |

A change to **Restore windows on launch** takes effect the next time you start Kepler.

### Keep agents running

These settings keep agent work running when the machine would otherwise stop it. They apply to the machine the agents run on, so in a window connected to a remote machine, they apply to that machine:

| Setting | What it controls | Default |
|---|---|---|
| **Keep this machine awake while agents work** | Blocks sleep while an agent session is starting, running, or waiting for your input, and while Remote Access is connected | On |
| **Keep agents and terminals running across restarts and updates** | *Agent sessions and terminals stay alive while Kepler restarts or updates, and reconnect afterwards. Experimental.* | On |
| **Put idle agents to sleep** | How long a chat agent can sit idle before Kepler stops it, from **After 5 minutes** to **After 1 hour**, or **Never** | After 15 minutes |

**Keep this machine awake while agents work** also counts Claude Code sessions running outside Kepler. The screen can still turn off. If Kepler cannot keep the machine awake, the setting says why under the switch.

**Keep agents and terminals running across restarts and updates** applies from the next session you start.

**Put idle agents to sleep** stops chat sessions you have left alone, and their status reads **Asleep**. Your next message wakes a session, and the conversation carries on. Agents that are working or waiting on you stay awake. See [Session status](/kepler/agent-sessions#session-status).

### Insights

**Insights** has 1 setting:

| Setting | What it controls | Default |
|---|---|---|
| **Collect usage insights** | *Keep local statistics about your sessions and tasks on this computer. Nothing leaves it.* | On |

***

## Notifications

Use **Notifications** to choose which agent events Kepler tells you about, and where. **Desktop** notifications show while Kepler is in the background, and **In Kepler** alerts show while you are using it. Sessions started outside Kepler notify you only once they are on a task. Kepler saves these settings on this machine.

### What to notify you about

**What to notify you about** has a **Desktop** and an **In Kepler** box for each event. The following table lists the events and their defaults in the desktop app:

| Event | When it fires | Desktop | In Kepler |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Replies** | *An agent finished replying and it's your turn.* | Off | Off |
| **Questions** | *An agent asks you something and waits for your answer.* Also fires when a plan is ready for your review | On | On |
| **Permission requests** | *An agent wants permission to do something.* | On | On |
| **Approval requests** | *An agent asks to do something in Kepler only you can approve, like deleting a worktree or rewriting a branch.* See [Approvals](/kepler/settings-agents#approvals) | On | On |
| **Errors** | *A session stops because something went wrong.* | On | On |

In a browser connected to Kepler, every **Desktop** box starts off. Until you set **Approval requests** yourself, it follows **Permission requests**. When you turn on the first **Desktop** box, Kepler sends a sample notification so your OS asks for permission.

These settings appear under the grid:

| Setting | What it controls | Default |
|---|---|---|
| **Play a sound with desktop notifications** | Whether a desktop notification makes the OS notification sound | On |
| **Notify even for the task you're looking at** | *Otherwise Kepler stays quiet about the task open in the window you're using.* | Off |

To silence desktop notifications from one remote machine only, use **Mute notifications from {host}** on that machine in [Remote environments](/kepler/settings-environment#remote-environments).

***

## Appearance

Use **Appearance** to choose light or dark and a theme, and to set up the Dashboard's views, the chat, the terminal, code text, and diffs. Kepler saves these settings on this machine.

### Theme

The **Theme** section has 2 parts: **Appearance**, which picks whether Kepler looks light or dark, and **Theme**, which picks the colors for each. Themes color the whole app, including code views, diffs, syntax, chat code blocks, and terminals.

**Appearance** has 3 options:

| Option | What it does |
|---|---|
| **System** | *Follows your system.* Kepler uses your dark theme when your OS is dark and your light theme when it's light, and switches when the OS does. **The default** |
| **Light** | *Always uses a light theme* |
| **Dark** | *Always uses a dark theme* |

Under **Theme**, each theme is a tile. The **Kepler** group holds the built-in themes:

- **Kepler**, which has a dark and a light version. It's the theme a fresh install uses for both.
- **Midnight**, a near-black theme that has only a dark version.

How you pick a tile depends on **Appearance**:

- On **System**, each tile has a moon and a sun. Click the moon to *Use {name} when your system is dark*, or the sun to *Use {name} when your system is light*. Click the tile itself to *Use {name} for both dark and light*.
- On **Light** or **Dark**, click a tile to use it for that appearance.

The tile in use reads **In use now**.

Terminals follow the theme too. Agent CLIs and other terminal programs that support it match your theme.

#### Your themes

**Your themes** lists the themes you have added, with 2 more tiles, **Browse gallery** and **Create a theme**. **Open themes folder**, beside the heading, opens the folder that holds your themes, `~/.kepler/themes`.

A theme file follows these rules:

- It is a `.json` or `.jsonc` file, so comments are allowed.
- A single file can hold a family of up to 8 themes, such as a dark and a light version.
- Each theme has an id and a name, and `extends` one of Kepler's base themes: `midnight`, `dark`, or `light`. The theme then overrides that base's colors, and can add code colors and a `terminal` block.
- The `terminal` block sets the terminal's background, foreground, cursor, selection, and 16 ANSI colors.

Kepler reads up to 64 theme files, and reloads a file each time you save it.

If Kepler cannot fully read a theme's file, its tile shows **Has problems** or **Has warnings**. To see what is wrong, click the badge. Each problem gives its line and column, or names the setting it is in, such as *themes.1.extends*.

A file with warnings still works. Kepler leaves out a theme that has errors, and still loads the other themes in its file. To fix a file, use one of these options below the list of problems:

- **Create a task to fix it** gives the file to an agent.
- In the desktop app, **Open file** opens the file in your editor, at the error's line when there is one. Changes apply when you save.

A tile's **More actions for {name}** menu has **Show in folder** and **Move to Trash** (**Move to Recycle Bin** on Windows).

#### Theme gallery

**Browse gallery** opens the **Theme gallery** of community themes, each checked for contrast, which you can try before you install. The gallery needs an internet connection. It has the following controls:

- **Search themes**, which matches a theme's name, author, tags, or description.
- **Show**, which filters to **All**, **Dark**, or **Light** themes.
- **Sort:**, with **Featured**, **Newest**, or **Name**.

Click a theme to see its details card, with its author, its dark and light variants, its version and license, and any contrast warnings. Then choose one of the following:

- **Install** adds the theme to **Your themes** without changing the theme on screen. The button then reads **Use**.
- **Try it** closes the gallery and paints the whole window in the theme, so you can open a diff or a terminal to judge it. In the bar at the bottom, click **Use {name}**, or **Done** to return to the gallery.

If a theme you already have uses the same id, Kepler asks before it replaces that file, and moves the old file to the Trash. A gallery theme you installed and have not edited offers **Update to {version}** on its tile when a newer version is published. The gallery's themes come from `gitkraken/kepler-themes` on GitHub, where you can also publish your own.

#### Create a theme

**Create a theme** opens the **New task** composer with a prompt already written for an agent, ending in *The theme I want:* for you to describe it. You do not need to attach the themes folder: the agent checks the theme's format and contrast, then saves it to **Your themes**. **Create a task to fix it**, on a broken theme file, starts the same kind of task with that file's problems listed.

#### Themes in a remote window

Themes belong to this computer, as your choice of theme does. Every window, including one connected to a remote environment, lists and installs themes in this computer's themes folder and gallery.

In a window connected to another machine, the picker adds an **On {host}** group with that machine's themes:

- A theme you do not have offers **Install {name} on this computer**.
- A theme that differs from your copy offers to update or replace your copy, and is marked **Update to {version}**, **Older than yours**, or **Differs from yours**.

Kepler asks before it updates or replaces your copy, and moves your copy to the Trash (the Recycle Bin on Windows). It never replaces your copy on its own.

### Dashboard

These settings set where the Dashboard's views sit and how they look:

| Setting | What it controls | Default | Options |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Views** | Where the Dashboard's views sit in the window | Below the title bar | In the title bar, Below the title bar, Along the left side |
| **View style** | How views in or below the title bar look | Tabs | Tabs, Pills |
| **Size** | How big views along the left side are | Default | Default, Compact |
| **Counts on views** | Shows how many tasks match each view's filters | On | On, Off |
| **Search box** | How wide the Dashboard's search box is | Full width | Grows as you type, Full width |

With **Along the left side**, the **Settings** button moves to the bottom of the views.

### Chat

These settings set how wide a session's conversation grows and how it scrolls:

| Setting | What it controls | Default |
|---|---|---|
| **Conversation width** | How wide the conversation grows in a wide pane: **Narrow**, **Wide**, or **Full width** | Narrow |
| **Scrolling** › **While an agent replies** | **Follow new output** keeps the newest output in view until you scroll up. **Stay on my message** keeps your message in view | Follow new output |
| **Scrolling** › **Return to where I left off when I reopen a session** | Whether a session reopens where you left it | On |

### Terminal

These settings control Kepler's embedded terminals:

| Setting | What it controls | Default |
|---|---|---|
| **Font** › **Family** | *Separate fonts with commas. The terminal uses the first one installed on this machine.* | Empty, which uses your platform's standard monospace fonts |
| **Font** › **Size** | Terminal font size in pixels, from 8 to 32 | 13 |
| **Font** › **Line height** | Spacing between lines, from 1 to 2 | 1.2 |
| **Show the message box under terminal sessions** | Adds Kepler's message box, for attachments and voice, under an agent's terminal | Off |

The grayed text in **Family** is an example, not the value in effect. If Kepler cannot find a font you name, the field says so, and the terminal uses the next name in your list. **Family** and **Size** save when you press **Enter** or leave the field. Code views use this family too, unless you set one under [Code](#code).

#### Embedded terminals

Each Kepler terminal belongs to a worktree. Opening a terminal starts a shell in that worktree's folder, so you do not need to `cd` into it, and the shell loads your profile the same way an interactive login shell would. Use **⌘ J** to show and hide the terminal panel, **New terminal** to open another terminal, and **Close terminal** to end one.

Use terminals for work next to an agent session: running tests while the agent writes code, checking Git state, or reproducing something the session did not show. A terminal starts in one worktree and stays there, so for work that spans several repositories, use a standalone terminal.

### Code

These settings set how diffs and code look:

| Setting | What it controls | Default |
|---|---|---|
| **Diff layout** | The layout diffs open in: **Stacked** or **Split** | Stacked |
| **Font** › **Family** | The font for diffs, file views, and code in chat. Leave it empty to use the terminal's font | Empty |
| **Font** › **Size** | Text size in diffs and file views, from 10 to 24 | 13 |

To switch a single diff without changing the default, use the layout button on the file's header in the Changes overlay. See [Review changes](/kepler/review-changes).

***

## Voice

Use **Voice** to talk to your agents instead of typing, and to have their replies read aloud. Both run on this machine, so nothing you say or hear leaves it. Kepler saves these settings on this machine.

### Dictation

Dictation is the microphone in the chat prompt. It has no on/off switch: it is on once a model is downloaded.

#### Model

**Model** lists 3 models, each with its download size and its own **Download** button:

| Model | What it's best at |
|---|---|
| **Qwen3-ASR 1.7B** | *The most accurate, especially with developer terms and mixed languages. Needs a recent graphics card.* |
| **Qwen3-ASR 0.6B** | *Better than Whisper with technical terms, and lighter on memory. For graphics cards with less memory.* |
| **Whisper** | *Works on any machine, including without a compatible graphics card. Less accurate with technical terms.* |

Both Qwen3-ASR models need a graphics card with WebGPU. Without one, a single row says so. Kepler marks the Qwen3-ASR size that suits this graphics card **Recommended**. Whisper's row has a **Quality** select, **Fast**, **Balanced**, **Accurate**, or **Most accurate**, with the best fit for this machine marked *suggested*.

Your first download turns dictation on. With more than 1 model downloaded, pick the one dictation uses. A download keeps going while you work elsewhere in Kepler, and Kepler notifies you when the model is ready. Until a newly chosen model is downloaded, dictation keeps using the installed one.

A downloaded model's row offers **Remove…**, which deletes the model after you confirm. Removing the model that dictates turns the chat microphone off until another is downloaded and picked. When a newer version of a downloaded Qwen3-ASR model is released, its row offers **Update**, and Kepler tells you once in a notification. Dictation keeps using the installed model until you update.

#### Listening

| Setting | What it controls | Default |
|---|---|---|
| **Dictation language** | With a Qwen3-ASR model, the language you speak. **Auto-detect** picks among your system's preferred languages and the app language. Whisper ignores this setting | Auto-detect |
| **When you stop talking** | **Insert the text so you can edit it**, **Send the prompt**, or **Keep listening, transcribing each phrase as you pause** | Insert the text so you can edit it |

#### Learned words

**Learned words** works with Qwen models only. Qwen3-ASR learns how to spell words that you fix in dictated text before you send it, 1 word at a time. When you fix the same word in 2 sends, Kepler suggests it, and dictation uses it once you approve it. Kepler stores only the words, on this device only, and keeps them after you sign out.

When a fix becomes a suggestion, a notification offers **Review**, which opens **Learned words**. It has 2 lists:

- **Suggested words**: fixes you made in 2 sends, each with what dictation heard, **Approve**, and **Dismiss**. Kepler never suggests a dismissed fix again.
- **Words**: the words dictation uses, each with a remove button. To add a word yourself, type it in **Add a word** and click **Add**.

**Forget learned words…** removes every word Qwen3-ASR learned or suggested, and every word you added, on this device, after you confirm.

Kepler downloads each model from the internet once. Transcription then runs entirely on your device, and your audio is never uploaded. See [Dictation and Read Aloud](/kepler/voice-input).

### Read aloud

**Read aloud** reads agent replies to you from the chat, the terminal, or the title bar. See [Read aloud](/kepler/voice-input#read-aloud).

| Setting | What it controls | Default |
|---|---|---|
| **Voice engine** | **System voices**, built into this machine, or **Kokoro**, natural English voices that need a graphics card with WebGPU and their own **Download** | System voices |
| **Voice** | The voice that reads. Choosing a voice plays a short sample | System default |
| **Speed** | How fast Kepler reads. **Reset to 1x** returns to normal speed | 1x |

Until Kokoro is downloaded, and for text that is not English, the system voice reads. Once Kokoro is downloaded, **Remove…** deletes it after you confirm.

***

## Keyboard shortcuts

Use **Keyboard shortcuts** to look up Kepler's shortcuts and choose your own keys. The page lists every command in 6 groups: **General**, **Navigation**, **Dashboard**, **Task page**, **Chat**, and **Changes and code views**. A command without a key shows **None**. Menu items and button tooltips show each command's keys, including the ones you set. For a few tab shortcuts that Settings does not list, such as reopening a closed tab and jumping to a tab by position, see [Task View](/kepler/task-view#keyboard).

### Change a shortcut

1. Find the command, or type its name in **Search shortcuts**.
2. Click the pencil (**Change shortcut**) on its row. If the command already has a key, a menu opens: choose **Change shortcut**, **Add another shortcut**, or **Remove** followed by the key.
3. Press the new keys. **Escape** cancels, and **Backspace** removes the shortcut.

If the keys already belong to another command, Kepler names it, and **Replace** moves the keys to this command. Kepler refuses keys it needs elsewhere, such as the key that sends chat messages, and says why.

A changed row offers **Reset to default**. **Changed only** lists only the shortcuts you changed, and **Reset all shortcuts** puts every shortcut back to its default after you confirm. A row with a lock, such as **Copy the selection or the focused item** or **Dismiss / Cancel**, cannot be changed.

### Default shortcuts

The tables list the default keys, Mac symbols first. On Windows and Linux, **⌘** is **Ctrl** and **⌥** is **Alt**, and **⌃** is **Ctrl** on every platform.

#### General shortcuts

The **General** group holds app-wide shortcuts:

| Action | Mac | Windows / Linux |
|---|---|---|
| Open settings | ⌘ , | Ctrl + , |
| Toggle Ask Kepler chat | ⌘ L or ⌘ K | Ctrl + L or Ctrl + K |
| Toggle Ask Kepler terminal | ⌃ ` | Ctrl + ` |
| New Ask Kepler chat | ⌘ ⇧ K or ⌘ ⇧ L | Ctrl + Shift + K or Ctrl + Shift + L |
| New task | ⌘ N | Ctrl + N |
| Open quick launcher (global) | ⇧ ⌥ N | Shift + Alt + N |
| New window | ⌘ ⇧ N | Ctrl + Shift + N |
| Quit | ⌘ Q | Ctrl + Q |
| Zoom in | ⌘ = | Ctrl + = |
| Zoom out | ⌘ - | Ctrl + - |
| Reset zoom | ⌘ 0 | Ctrl + 0 |
| Toggle full screen | ⌘ ⌃ F | F11 |
| Minimize | ⌘ M | Ctrl + M |
| Reload | ⌘ R | Ctrl + R |
| Hide Kepler | ⌘ H | macOS only |
| Hide others | ⌘ ⌥ H | macOS only |
| Copy the selection or the focused item | ⌘ C | Ctrl + C |
| Close window | ⌘ ⇧ W | Ctrl + Shift + W |
| Toggle terminal | ⌘ J | Ctrl + J |
| New session | ⌘ T | Ctrl + T |
| Rename task | F2 | F2 |
| Delete task | ⌘ ⇧ Backspace | Ctrl + Shift + Backspace |
| Manage remote environments | ⌘ ⇧ R | Ctrl + Shift + R |
| Toggle side panel | ⌘ B | Ctrl + B |
| Open file | ⌘ O | Ctrl + O |
| Open folder | ⌘ ⇧ O | Ctrl + Shift + O |
| Go to file | ⌘ P | Ctrl + P |
| Go to task | ⌘ ⇧ P or F1 | Ctrl + Shift + P or F1 |
| Dismiss / Cancel | Escape | Escape |

**Go to task** and **Open folder** are also in the app menu, as **View › Command Palette…** and **File › Open Folder…**.

#### Navigation shortcuts

The **Navigation** group moves you between tasks, tabs, and regions:

| Action | Mac | Windows / Linux |
|---|---|---|
| Go to next task needing attention | None | None |
| Go to next unread task | None | None |
| Go to next task needing attention or unread | None | None |
| Previous tab | ⌘ ⇧ [ | Ctrl + Shift + [ or Ctrl + PageUp |
| Next tab | ⌘ ⇧ ] | Ctrl + Shift + ] or Ctrl + PageDown |
| Move tab left | ⌘ ⌥ [ | Ctrl + Alt + [ or Ctrl + Shift + PageUp |
| Move tab right | ⌘ ⌥ ] | Ctrl + Alt + ] or Ctrl + Shift + PageDown |
| Focus next region | F6 | F6 |
| Focus previous region | ⇧ F6 | Shift + F6 |
| Close tab or panel | ⌘ W | Ctrl + W or Ctrl + F4 |
| Go back | ⌘ [ | Alt + ← |
| Go forward | ⌘ ] | Alt + → |

The 3 **Go to next task** commands open the next task that needs you, the next task with an unread reply, or the next of either.

#### Dashboard shortcuts

The **Dashboard** group works on the Dashboard's tasks and detail panels:

| Action | Mac | Windows / Linux |
|---|---|---|
| Move panel left | ⌘ ⌥ ⇧ ← | Ctrl + Alt + Shift + ← |
| Move panel right | ⌘ ⌥ ⇧ → | Ctrl + Alt + Shift + → |
| Move panel up | ⌘ ⌥ ⇧ ↑ | Ctrl + Alt + Shift + ↑ |
| Move panel down | ⌘ ⌥ ⇧ ↓ | Ctrl + Alt + Shift + ↓ |
| Move task to the previous Progress stage | ⌘ ⇧ ← | Ctrl + Shift + ← |
| Move task to the next Progress stage | ⌘ ⇧ → | Ctrl + Shift + → |
| Focus detail panel 1 to 8 | ⌘ 1 to ⌘ 8 | Ctrl + 1 to Ctrl + 8 |
| Focus last detail panel | ⌘ 9 | Ctrl + 9 |
| Previous item in list | ⌥ ⇧ ↑ | Alt + Shift + ↑ |
| Next item in list | ⌥ ⇧ ↓ | Alt + Shift + ↓ |
| Switch to older panel | ⌃ ⇧ Tab | Ctrl + Shift + Tab |
| Switch to newer panel | ⌃ Tab | Ctrl + Tab |
| Solo detail panel | ⌘ ⇧ M | Ctrl + Shift + M |
| Maximize panel terminals | ⌘ ⇧ J | Ctrl + Shift + J |
| Toggle changes pane | ⌘ ⇧ G | Ctrl + Shift + G |
| Toggle task list peek | ⌘ ⇧ B | Ctrl + Shift + B |
| Toggle resources pane | ⌘ ⇧ E | Ctrl + Shift + E |
| Find in dashboard | ⌘ F | Ctrl + F |

#### Task page shortcuts

The **Task page** group works on a task's page:

| Action | Mac | Windows / Linux |
|---|---|---|
| Focus chat | ⌘ 1 | Ctrl + 1 |
| Focus changes | ⌘ 2 | Ctrl + 2 |
| Focus resources | ⌘ 3 | Ctrl + 3 |
| Switch sessions | ⌃ Tab | Ctrl + Tab |
| Switch sessions, oldest first | ⌃ ⇧ Tab | Ctrl + Shift + Tab |
| Maximize terminal drawer | ⌘ ⇧ J | Ctrl + Shift + J |
| Show or hide the preview in Add resources | ⌘ ⌥ P | Ctrl + Alt + P |

#### Chat shortcuts

The **Chat** group works in a session's conversation:

| Action | Mac | Windows / Linux |
|---|---|---|
| Find in conversation | ⌘ F | Ctrl + F |
| Previous message | ⌘ ⌥ ↑ | Ctrl + Alt + ↑ |
| Next message | ⌘ ⌥ ↓ | Ctrl + Alt + ↓ |
| Interrupt & send | ⌘ ⇧ Enter | Ctrl + Shift + Enter |

#### Changes and code view shortcuts

This group has 2 lists. The **Changes** list works in the Changes view:

| Action | Mac | Windows / Linux |
|---|---|---|
| Filter changed files | ⌘ P | Ctrl + P |
| Previous file | ⌥ ↑ | Alt + ↑ |
| Next file | ⌥ ↓ | Alt + ↓ |
| Next change | F7 | F7 |
| Previous change | ⇧ F7 | Shift + F7 |
| Toggle changes sidebar | ⌘ B | Ctrl + B |
| Open all changes | ⌘ ⇧ A | Ctrl + Shift + A |
| Comment on selection | ⌘ ⇧ C | Ctrl + Shift + C |
| Edit working copy | ⌘ E | Ctrl + E |

The **Code views** list works in any code view, such as a diff or a file you have opened:

| Action | Mac | Windows / Linux |
|---|---|---|
| Find in file or diff | ⌘ F | Ctrl + F |
| Next match | F3 or ⌘ G | F3 |
| Previous match | ⇧ F3 or ⌘ ⇧ G | Shift + F3 |
| Match case | ⌘ ⌥ C | Alt + C |
| Match whole word | ⌘ ⌥ W | Alt + W |
| Use regular expression | ⌘ ⌥ R | Alt + R |

### Shortcuts that depend on where you are

Some keys do different things depending on where you are:

- **⌘ 1**, **⌘ 2**, and **⌘ 3** focus a detail panel on the Dashboard but a column on the task page.
- **⌃ Tab** switches detail panels on the Dashboard and sessions on the task page.
- **⌘ ⇧ [** and **⌘ ⇧ ]** step through the Dashboard's views on the Dashboard, and through a panel's tabs when the panel or the task page has focus. **⌘ ⌥ [** and **⌘ ⌥ ]** move the current view or tab.
- **⌘ ⇧ J** maximizes the panel's terminals on the Dashboard and the terminal drawer on the task page.
- **⌘ B** shows or hides the changes panel in the Changes view, docks or hides the task list on the Dashboard, and docks or hides the context panel on the task page.
- **⌘ P** filters changed files in the Changes view and opens **Go to file** elsewhere.
- **⌘ F** finds in the Dashboard from its list or header, finds in a file or diff in a code view, and finds in the conversation elsewhere.
- **⌘ ⇧ G** shows or hides changes in a Dashboard detail panel, and, on macOS, moves to the previous match in a code view.
- **⌘ C** on a focused row, chip, or link copies what it names, such as a task's Kepler link, a pull request or issue link, a file path, or a commit hash. In a text field, a terminal, or a text selection, it copies as usual.

**Previous item in list** and **Next item in list** work even while you type in the open panel's chat.

**Open quick launcher** works while Kepler is in the background. Its row has a **Global** badge. **Close tab or panel**, **Toggle full screen**, **Minimize**, and **Reload** work only in the desktop app.

On Windows and Linux, a focused terminal passes **Ctrl + W**, **Ctrl + L**, and **Ctrl + B** to the shell. To toggle the Ask Kepler chat from a terminal, press **Ctrl + K**: the shell does not keep that key. **Ctrl + `** always toggles the Ask Kepler terminal, even from a terminal.

Hold the **Go back** or **Go forward** key to keep moving through your history.

**Send feedback**, **Show release notes**, **Show About Kepler**, **Check for updates**, and **Clean up worktrees** have no default key, nor do commands such as **Open documentation**, **Appearance: Dark**, and **Dashboard layout: Board**. To use one from the keyboard, give it a key on this page.

***

---

---
# Environment Settings
URL: https://help.gitkraken.com/kepler/settings-environment/
product: Kepler
feature: Settings
content_type: reference
audience: developer
plan_required: all
status: GA
last_verified: 2026-11

Use **Settings → Remote environments** to save the machines your agents can run on over SSH or WSL, and to choose how remote windows load. Use **Settings → Remote Access** to open this computer's Kepler from a browser or your phone. To learn how to work in a remote environment day to day, see [Remote Environments](/kepler/remote-environments).

***

## Remote environments

*Run your agents on another machine, like a dev server or cloud VM, while you work from here. Kepler installs itself over SSH, so there's nothing to set up on that machine first.* On Windows, you can also use a WSL distro, with nothing extra to install.

To open this page from anywhere, press **⌘ ⇧ R**, or click **Manage remote environments…** in the remote chip's popover. Kepler saves the machine list on this computer, whichever machine a window is connected to.

The Remote environments page has 3 sections:

| Section | What it holds |
|---|---|
| **Your machines** | Your saved machines. Each row shows whether the machine is connected and how many windows have it open |
| **Found on this machine** | *Machines from your SSH config and WSL that you haven't added yet.* The section appears only while Kepler finds one |
| **Remote windows** | How a window connected to another machine loads its interface. See [Remote windows](#remote-windows) |

In **Your machines**, you can do the following:

- To open a machine in this window, click **Connect**. To open it in a new window, click the button next to **Connect** (*Connect to {name} in a new window*).
- To add a machine by hand, click **Add machine**. On Windows, choose **SSH** or **WSL** in **Machine type**. A WSL machine takes a **Distro** and an optional **Name**.

In **Found on this machine**, you can do the following:

- To save a machine, click **Add**.
- To move a machine out of the list, click **Hide**. Hidden machines appear under **Show hidden ({count})**.

If your plan does not include remote environments, **Add** reads **Try free and add** when a trial is available. Otherwise it reads **Upgrade to add**, which opens the plan page and saves nothing.

To open a saved machine's page, click the machine:

| Control | What it does |
|---|---|
| Name | Rename the machine. You can rename a machine only from a local window |
| **Latency**, **Live sessions** | The connection's current state |
| **Color** | Tints the machine's chip, its popover, and a connected window's top strip, so you can tell machines apart. **None** removes the tint |
| **Mute notifications from {host}** | *Kepler won't show desktop notifications for sessions on {host}. Alerts still appear inside its windows.* |
| **Connection** | Edit the SSH or WSL address. If you enter a new SSH address, Kepler asks you to trust its host key with **Trust and save** |
| **Remove {name}…** | Deletes the saved machine |

To edit the connection of a machine you are connected to, disconnect from it first.

In a window connected to an SSH machine, a **Ports** list shows the ports forwarded from that machine to this computer. You can do the following:

- To forward another port, enter its number.
- To stop forwarding a port, click **Stop**.
- To stop every forwarded port, click **Stop all**. This button appears when more than one port is forwarded.

A window connected to a machine shows the other machines read-only, with the message *To add, edit, or remove machines, open Remote environments in a local window.* To make changes, click **Open in a local window**.

If a window cannot reconnect to its machine, it shows a full-screen recovery screen instead of this page. See [The recovery screen](/kepler/remote-environments#the-recovery-screen).

### Remote windows

When another machine runs a different version of Kepler, a window connected to it uses that machine's interface. The following setting, in the desktop app only, changes that:

| Setting | What it controls | Default |
|---|---|---|
| **Always use this app's interface** | Offers to update the server or this app instead of showing the server's interface. An outdated server then updates when you connect, even while other devices use it | Off |

To learn how to connect, forward ports, and how sessions behave on a machine, see [Remote environments](/kepler/remote-environments).

***

## Remote Access

*Use this machine from any browser or your phone, through a secure GitKraken relay.* You do not need to open a port or set up a tunnel. Remote Access requires a paid GitKraken plan and is not available on the Community plan.

Under **How it works**, the page lists 3 steps:

1. Turn it on and name this machine.
2. Scan the QR code or open the link that appears here, on your phone or any browser.
3. Sign in with your GitKraken account, and this machine's tasks and sessions are there.

### Turning Remote Access on and off

To turn on Remote Access, do the following:

1. Click **Turn on Remote Access**.
2. Enter a name in **Name this machine**.

A status badge shows the connection state: **Connecting…**, **Active**, **Reconnecting…**, **Waiting to reconnect**, **Error**, or **Inactive**. While Remote Access is on, the page shows a QR code (*Scan with your phone camera to open*) and **Copy URL**. The page also shows *This machine stays awake while Remote Access is on.*, with **Change in General**, which opens [Keep agents running](/kepler/settings-app#keep-agents-running).

Remote Access stays on until you turn it off, sign out, or another account signs in.

To turn off Remote Access, click the switch. Kepler asks **Turn off Remote Access?** first, because *Every paired device is disconnected.*

### Reconnecting after a dropped connection

If Remote Access loses the connection, Kepler first retries quickly. It then shows **Waiting to reconnect** and the reason, under **Unable to connect**, with *Kepler retries every 5 minutes.* To retry at once, click **Retry now**. Paired devices stay paired.

These 2 reasons tell you how to fix them:

- *Waiting for a GitKraken sign-in. Remote Access connects as soon as one is available.*
- *Your account has reached its limit of machines with Remote Access on. Remove one you no longer use, then retry.* This message has a **Manage machines on gitkraken.dev** button.

### Managing machines and devices

**Machines on your account** shows *See every machine on your account with Remote Access on, and remove the ones you no longer use.* Its **Manage machines on gitkraken.dev** button appears even while Remote Access is off.

**Connected devices** lists each device that has connected. It marks **This device** and shows when each device was **Last seen**. You can do the following:

- To disconnect one device, click **Revoke**.
- To reload the list, click **Refresh**.

The section notes: *Only you can connect, signed in to your GitKraken account. Turning Remote Access off disconnects every device, and you can revoke any single device under Connected devices.*

A pairing link works once and expires after 5 minutes. A used link shows *This pairing link no longer works*. To pair again, open a new link from the computer running Kepler. If you open a saved address, such as a bookmark, after its browser session has ended, Kepler takes you to gitkraken.dev to sign in again. To learn about prerequisites, pairing, and managing sessions from gitkraken.dev, see [Remote environments](/kepler/remote-environments).

***

---

---
# Update and Help Settings
URL: https://help.gitkraken.com/kepler/settings-updates-help/
product: Kepler
feature: Settings
content_type: reference
audience: developer
plan_required: all
status: GA
last_verified: 2026-11

Use **Updates** to see which version of Kepler you have and to install a new one. Use **Help** to open the docs and release notes, see dismissed tips again, and save Kepler's logs when you need to report a problem.

## Updates

The **Updates** page has these rows:

| Row | What it does |
|---|---|
| **Current version** | The installed version, with **Release notes** beside it to open what's new in that release |
| **Check for updates** | Checks for a newer release and downloads it in the background. Reads **Up to date** when there is nothing newer, and becomes **Check again** |
| Download progress | While a release downloads: **Downloading**, with its progress and the time left. A **Verifying** step follows, and on Windows a **Preparing** step |
| **New version** | Appears once a release is ready, with **Restart to update** beside it, and how many running agents a restart would stop |

When an update is ready, a chip also appears in the top bar on every screen. Its popover reads **Update ready to install** and says what a restart does to running work. If agents are in the middle of a tool call when you restart, Kepler waits up to 30 seconds for them to finish. To skip the wait, click **Restart now**, which may interrupt tool calls that are still running.

**Check for updates** in the app menu shows its result where you are, without opening Settings. The top bar shows **Checking…**, then **Up to date** or the download. On the welcome screen, click the version in the corner to check. If that check fails, it reads **Unable to check for updates** with **Try again**.

After an update, the release notes open in Kepler by themselves, once any guided start has ended. A release can start with a highlights card, *Three things in {version} to try first:*, and each item opens its part of the notes.

The update controls appear only in the desktop app. In a browser window connected to Kepler, the **Updates** page has nothing to update.

***

## Help

Use **Help** to find the docs and release notes, see tips again, and save logs when something goes wrong.

### Help

The **Help** section links to the docs and release notes, and shows again any tip you dismissed:

| Control | What it does |
|---|---|
| **Kepler documentation** | *Guides, keyboard shortcuts, and agent setup.* **Open docs** opens the Kepler docs site in your browser |
| **Release notes** | *See what changed in each version.* **Show release notes** opens them in Kepler, starting with the release's highlights when it has them. See [Updates](#updates) |
| **Show tips and guides again** | A disclosure, closed by default: *Kepler points out a few controls the first time they matter. Show any of those tips again here.* |

Inside the disclosure, each tip has a row that reads **Seen and dismissed** or **Not shown yet**, with its own **Show again** button. A tip that Kepler showed but you never dismissed still reads **Not shown yet**. The tips are the following:

- **Actions callout**
- **Todo pointer**
- **Task page callout**
- **Panel layout callout**

To show every tip again at once, instead of 1 row at a time, click **Reset all onboarding and show everything again** at the bottom of the disclosure.

### Logs

To report a problem, save the logs and attach the file. The **Logs** section has these controls:

| Control | What it does |
|---|---|
| **Copy path** | Copies the current log's path to your clipboard |
| **Show in Finder** | Opens the log's folder in your file manager (**Show in Explorer** on Windows, **Show in file manager** on Linux). Hidden where the machine cannot open a file manager |
| **Save logs…** | Saves Kepler's logs as a single zip file |
| **Clear log…** | Deletes the current and rotated log files, after a confirmation |

In a window connected to a remote environment, the section shows the remote machine's logs: *These are the logs on {machine}.* Saving them from there includes this machine's logs too. To open your local logs, click **Show this machine's logs**.

To find this computer's log without opening Settings, use **Help → Show Logs in Finder** (**Show Logs in Explorer**, **Show Logs in File Manager**) in the app menu.
