# Remote Environments
URL: https://help.gitkraken.com/kepler/remote-environments/
product: Kepler
feature: Remote Environments
content_type: how-to
audience: developer
plan_required: all
status: GA
last_verified: 2026-11

A **remote environment** runs your agents, worktrees, and terminals on another machine: a dev server, a cloud VM, or a WSL (Windows Subsystem for Linux) instance on Windows, while you work from this window. Kepler installs itself on the host over SSH (Secure Shell), so you do not need to pre-install anything there.

***

## Two remote features

Kepler has 2 remote features, and they work in opposite directions:

| Feature | Direction | Where it lives |
|---|---|---|
| **Remote environments** | Kepler on your desktop reaches **out** to another machine, and your work runs there | The title-bar chip, and **Settings → Remote environments** |
| **Remote Access** | Another device reaches **in** to this Kepler, and your work stays here | The **Remote Access** button in the title bar, and **Settings → Remote Access** |

Both sit at the right end of the title bar. The **Remote Access** button shows a monitor-and-phone icon.

To let another device reach this Kepler, rather than connecting *to* another machine, see [Remote Access](#remote-access-reach-kepler-from-another-device).

<div class="note" markdown="1">

**Remote environments need a paid plan.** Every paid plan except Student includes them, with no limit on how many environments you can add. On other plans, a banner offers a free trial when one is available. If another organization you belong to includes remote environments, the banner names that organization and offers **Switch to organization**. If you have just upgraded, click **Check again** under **Already upgraded?** to reload your plan.

</div>

***

## Switching environments from the title bar

Each window works on one environment at a time, and the title-bar chip shows which one. The chip leads with the environment's type icon, and a green dot on that icon means connected.

| Chip | What it means |
|---|---|
| **Local** | This window works on this machine |
| **Connecting to *machine*…**, or the current stage | This window is connecting, or its server is restarting or updating |
| **Reconnecting…** | The connection dropped and Kepler is rebuilding it |
| Host name | Connected. The chip takes the host's [color](#host-details) when you have set one |
| Brand fill with an up-arrow | Connected, and a newer server build is ready for the host |
| Warning triangle | The app and the server disagree on version; the popover says which side to update |
| Radio-tower glyph | This window is [forwarding ports](#port-forwarding) from the host |
| An error headline | The last attempt failed; the host's Settings page keeps the full error |

**Hover over the chip to preview the popover.** To open the whole popover and keep it open, click the chip, or focus it and press **Enter** or **Down Arrow**.

In a browser client, Kepler hides the chip, because a browser client cannot manage connections.

### The popover

Use the popover to see which machine this window is on, switch to another machine, and open Settings to manage your machines.

| Part | What it does |
|---|---|
| Header | The current machine, with its address, latency, and versions, or this window's connection progress or failure |
| Gear (**Machine settings**) | Opens the machine's Settings page |
| **Restart server to update** | Appears when a newer server build is ready. See [Server controls](#server-controls) |
| **Disconnect** | Disconnects this window only. The server keeps its sessions running |
| **Restart server** (circular arrow) | Restarts a connected server when no update is pending. See [Server controls](#server-controls) |
| **Stop server** | Stops the server on the machine until you start it again. Every other window connected to it moves to the [recovery screen](#the-recovery-screen) ([When you stop a server](#when-you-stop-a-server)) |
| Forwarded ports | Lists the ports this window forwards, and opens the host's **Ports** list |
| **Switch to** | Every other saved host, plus **Local** (*Work on this machine*) when this window is on a remote |
| **Found on this machine** | WSL distributions found on this PC, offered for one-click connect while you have no saved hosts |
| **Manage remote environments…** | Opens **Settings → Remote environments**. **⌘ ⇧ R** on macOS, **Ctrl + Shift + R** elsewhere |

The line under **Restart server to update** says what the update will stop. When nothing would stop, the update starts at once. Otherwise, the **Update server?** confirmation names the agents and terminals that stop, or says that the server could not report them.

If this app is older than the server, the header offers an update for this app instead, and says that sessions on the host keep running.

To move this window to another host, click the host's row under **Switch to**. To open the host in a new window and leave this window where it is, hold **Cmd** (macOS) or **Ctrl** while you click, or click the window icon at the end of the row. A host already open in another window is marked **Connected**. Clicking its row brings that window to the front instead of opening a second connection.

***

## Windows on a remote host

- **New Window opens on the same host.** **File → New Window** (**⌘ ⇧ N** on macOS, **Ctrl + Shift + N** elsewhere) from a remote window opens a second window on that host. A remote window also offers **File → New Local Window** when you want a local one. A new window that cannot reach the host opens on the [recovery screen](#the-recovery-screen) with the reason.
- **Windows on one host share a connection,** so another window on it opens quickly.
- **A host open in another window shows as connected.** The popover and Settings offer **Show window**, and show its latency, versions, and sessions.
- **The last closed remote window reopens on its host.** With no window open, the dock, the tray, or launching Kepler again reconnects to the host the last window was on. If you close a window that was still waiting on an unreachable host, the next window opens locally. If **Restore windows on launch** is off, Kepler launches locally.
- **A link opens on its machine.** A task or session link copied in a window on a remote machine opens on that machine, in a new window if none is open there. A link copied in a local window opens in the window you used last. If a link cannot open on its machine, it opens on this computer instead, and starts nothing by itself. If the item is not found on that machine, the notice offers **Open on this computer**.

***

## Managing machines in Settings

Use **Settings → Remote environments** to add, connect, edit, and remove machines. In a local window, **Your machines** lists your saved machines. Each row shows the host's type, whether it is connected, and how many windows already use it. From a row, you can do the following:

- To connect this window, click **Connect**.
- To connect in a new window, click the window icon.
- To bring forward a host that is open in another window, click **Show window**, which replaces **Connect** for that host.
- To open the host's page, click the row.

**Found on this machine** lists machines from your `~/.ssh/config` and WSL distributions you have not saved yet. To save one, click **Add**. If your plan does not include remote environments, **Add** reads **Try free and add** when a trial is available. Otherwise it reads **Upgrade to add**, which opens the plan page and saves nothing. To stop Kepler from offering a machine, click its eye icon to hide it. To bring hidden machines back, click **Show hidden (*N*)**.

### Host details

A host's page has a card of actions at the top:

- **Connect**. To connect in a new window, **Cmd/Ctrl**-click it. While a connection is in progress, the same button cancels it.
- **Show window** and **Connect to *machine* in a new window**, in place of **Connect**, when another window already has the host open.
- **Stop server**.
- **Remove *machine*…**, the red trash icon.

To rename the saved connection, click the pencil beside the name. Renaming changes nothing on the host.

| Group | What it does |
|---|---|
| **Connection** | Edits **Host**, **Port**, **User**, and **Identity file** for SSH, or **Distro** for WSL. Disconnect first: the fields are locked while the host is connected |
| **Color** | Tints the host's chip, its rows, and the top bar of its windows with one of the 12 task-group colors |
| **Mute notifications from *machine*** | Stops desktop notifications for sessions on the machine; alerts still appear inside its windows |
| **Sessions** | Lists the host's live agent sessions; click one to open it. For a host nobody is connected to, **Check** shows what is running there |

When you change the address of a host that the SSH wizard created, Kepler first fetches the new address's host key and shows it under **New host key**. **Trust and save** pins that key and saves the host in one step. When you change any address, Kepler notes that an install at the old address stays there.

**Kepler reads your own `~/.ssh/config` before it offers to write to it.** Kepler uses a host you have already configured exactly as you configured it, including its user, port, identity file, jump host, and any other settings. Kepler offers to edit the file only when it has nothing there to reuse. **Open in → VS Code** on an SSH environment uses that same host entry, so VS Code connects the way your terminal does.

### Server controls

The restart and update controls act on the server a window is connected to, so they appear in the popover and in a remote window's Settings. **Stop server** is also on every host's page in a local window.

| Control | What it does |
|---|---|
| **Restart server to update** | Installs the newer server build and reconnects. When something would stop, the **Update server?** confirmation lists it first |
| **Restart server** | Offered when no update is pending, for a stuck server. It always asks first |
| **Stop server** | Stops the Kepler server on the host for every connected window and device, and ends its agent sessions |
| **Auto-shutdown when idle** | Stops the server after a number of minutes with no window connected and nothing running. Off by default; the timeout defaults to 30 minutes |
| **Stop anyway after** | Stops the server after a number of hours with no window connected, even if work is running. Defaults to 12 hours |

**Auto-shutdown when idle** counts an agent that is working, or a terminal that is running a command, as something running. A shell that waits at its prompt does not count. **Stop anyway after** limits how long running work can keep the server up, so a dev server you forgot about does not keep it running indefinitely. The hours count from when the last window disconnects, and start over when a window connects.

Both settings belong to the machine, so they apply to every window and device connected to it. You set them from a window connected to the machine.

Both the **Update server?** and **Restart server?** confirmations list what a restart would stop, or say that running agents and terminals keep going. A restart reconnects this window and disconnects the other windows on the server. While an update or restart runs, the other server controls wait and say why.

**Keep agents and terminals running across restarts and updates**, in **Settings → General → Keep agents running**, is experimental and on by default. While it is on, running agents keep going through a restart or update. **Stop server** ends them either way.

### When you stop a server

A server that you stop on purpose stays stopped. This applies whether you stop it from this window, another window, Settings, or another device. Kepler does not start it again on its own, even when an automatic reconnect, a launch, or reopening the last window would otherwise connect to it. Those windows open on the [recovery screen](#the-recovery-screen), which says the server was stopped.

The server starts again only when you choose one of these actions:

- **Reconnect**, **Connect**, or **Try again**
- **File → New Window** on that machine
- **Restart server to update**

If a window stops its own server or disconnects, the window switches to local without showing the recovery screen.

### From a remote window

In a window that is on a remote, Settings shows only that host:

- Its connected card with the server controls
- **Auto-shutdown when idle**
- **Color** and mute
- Its **Ports** (SSH)
- Your other saved hosts to switch to

A remote window never shows the other hosts' addresses. To rename a host, edit a connection, or add or remove a host, click **Open in a local window**. You also need a local window to switch to a host that needs a password; its row offers **Open in a local window**.

### Connection failures

A failed connection shows an **Unable to connect to *machine*** alert with the SSH diagnostic and a **Copy error** button, so you can paste the diagnostic into a bug report. A failure on another machine does not drop this window's connection.

Common SSH failures, such as **Connection refused** or **Host key verification failed**, get a plain-language headline and a hint. **Update remote Kepler server** means the host's server is too old to take your GitKraken sign-in: update the Kepler install on the host and try again. On a WSL machine, Kepler says when the distro no longer exists, and reads **Connection failed** for anything else.

If the failure happens while you are adding a host, the wizard shows the headline, the hint, and the diagnostic in place, with **Try again**.

For Kepler's own log file, use **Settings → Help → Logs**.

### Removing a connection

**Remove *machine*…** deletes the saved entry on this desktop. If the SSH wizard created the entry, Kepler also offers to remove what the wizard set up:

| Cleanup option | What it does | Default |
|---|---|---|
| **Remove scoped known_hosts file** | Deletes the host-key trust file Kepler created for this connection | On |
| **Remove generated local SSH key** | Deletes the key the wizard generated, and its `.pub` sibling | On when such a key exists |
| **Uninstall Kepler server on the machine** | Stops the server and removes its install folder on the machine | On, unless the server is in use |
| **Remove deployed key from remote authorized_keys** | Removes the key the wizard installed on the host | Off |

Removing a WSL host offers **Uninstall Kepler server on the machine** for the distro. For a distro that no longer exists, Kepler shows nothing to uninstall.

If the server reports live sessions or connected clients, Kepler disables the uninstall until you select **Uninstall anyway, I understand sessions on this machine may be lost**. If the host is unreachable, or needs a password Kepler does not have, Kepler hides the host-side options, and the dialog states which of the two reasons applies.

***

## Add an SSH host

To add an SSH host, click **Add machine** in **Settings → Remote environments**. On Windows, choose **SSH** or **WSL** under **Machine type** first. To save a host already in your `~/.ssh/config`, use **Add** under **Found on this machine** instead.

A host taken from `~/.ssh/config` inherits your system SSH configuration, including its host-key trust. A host built in the wizard gets its own trust file, pinned at the fingerprint you accepted.

### The wizard

The SSH wizard has 5 steps:

| Step | What you do |
|---|---|
| *Connect to a machine you reach over SSH…* | **Name** (optional, defaults to its address), **Host**, **User** (optional, defaults to the machine's `$USER`), **Port** |
| *Choose authentication.* | Pick a mode (see below) |
| *Verify the machine's fingerprint.* | Kepler fetches the host key and shows its algorithm and fingerprint. **Trust and continue** pins it |
| *Verifying the connection.* | Kepler makes a real connection before anything is saved |
| *Ready to save.* | **Add** saves the host and opens its page. Nothing connects until you press **Connect**; a password the wizard verified is reused for that first connect |

| Authentication mode | What it means |
|---|---|
| **Existing key** | Use one of the keys already in `~/.ssh`. Unavailable when Kepler finds none |
| **Password** | *Re-prompt every connect.* The password is never stored |
| **Generate key** | *Keyless after first connect.* Kepler uses the password once to install a fresh ed25519 key at `~/.ssh/id_ed25519_kepler_<hash>`. Your existing keys are never overwritten |

**Generate key** needs `ssh-keygen` on your machine; the chip reads **ssh-keygen missing** when ssh-keygen is absent.

If you pick **Password**, the wizard then offers **Set up a key for this machine?** **Generate and copy key** generates a fresh ed25519 key, copies it to the host, and uses it for future connections, so you do not need the password again. **Skip** keeps the host on password sign-in.

If the host rejects a key-based connection, the host's page shows a password row so you can retry with a password. If no key is saved for that host yet, the page also offers to install one at the same time. If a connection from the popover needs a password, Kepler opens a password dialog instead.

### SSH to a Windows machine

Kepler connects to Windows hosts over SSH as well as Linux and macOS ones. Kepler detects a Windows host and installs itself accordingly.

Nothing changes in the wizard. If the host authenticates but its shell rejects Kepler's commands, the diagnostic reads **Remote shell was unable to run the command**, and the hint points at the OpenSSH default shell. Windows 10 and 11 ship PowerShell, so a changed default shell is the usual cause.

The host-side cleanup offered by **Remove *machine*…** does not run on a Windows host. See [Known limitations](#known-limitations).

***

## WSL environments

On Windows, a WSL 2 distro is a remote environment like any other, and the simplest one to set up: it needs no credentials and no fingerprint check.

- Kepler detects WSL and lists your **version 2** distros. Kepler does not offer WSL 1 distros, or Docker Desktop's own `docker-desktop` and `docker-desktop-data` distros.
- Detected distros appear under **Found on this machine** in Settings, and in the popover while you have no saved hosts, where one click connects to it. Picking one in the popover saves the distro as a host and connects to it, so the connection survives a disconnect.
- To add one by hand, choose **Add machine**, then **WSL** under **Machine type**, and enter its **Distro** (and an optional **Name**). A WSL host is edited, checked, and removed exactly like an SSH one.

***

## Port forwarding

When an agent or a terminal starts a dev server on an SSH host, its `http://localhost:3000` link points at the host, not at this computer. Kepler forwards that port over your SSH connection so the link opens here.

- **Click the link.** In an SSH window, **Cmd/Ctrl**-click a `localhost`, `127.0.0.1`, or `0.0.0.0` link in a terminal, or click one in the agent transcript. Kepler forwards the port to the host's `localhost`, then opens the local URL. If that port is already taken on this computer, Kepler picks a free one.
- **Open it from the task.** A `localhost` link attached to a task opens through forwarding too, from the task's context panel, the link's detail, or the Dashboard's resources list. Agents attach the URL of a dev server they start for you to open.
- **Add one by hand.** **Settings → Remote environments → Ports**, in the SSH window, lists this window's forwards as remote port → local URL. To add a forward, enter a **Port** and click **Add**. **Stop** ends one forward, and **Stop all** appears when more than one is forwarded.

While anything is forwarded, the chip shows a radio-tower glyph and the popover adds a summary row that opens the **Ports** list.

Forwards belong to the window that made them. Disconnecting, closing, reconnecting, or switching hosts ends them, and Kepler does not restore them. A forward that fails opens nothing rather than reaching a service on this computer. Local and WSL windows open `localhost` links as they are, with no forward.

***

## What runs where

| Piece | Runs on |
|---|---|
| Kepler's window and its native capabilities | Your local machine |
| Git operations, worktrees, and repositories | The host |
| Agent and terminal sessions | The host |
| Provider and issue-tracker data | The host |
| The interface itself | Served by this computer when the host runs the same version of Kepler, otherwise by the host's Kepler server (below) |
| Themes, and your choice of theme | Your local machine |

**Agent sessions belong to the server, not to your window.** If you close the window, lose the network, or put the laptop to sleep, the sessions keep running. When you reconnect, from this machine or a different one, the sessions are listed and you can resume them. If the server itself goes away, you can still resume the conversation.

Kepler runs agent sign-in on the host. Claude Code, Codex, and Auggie all sign in to a remote target: Kepler starts the flow on the host, the sign-in page opens in your *local* browser, and Kepler saves the credential on the host. For Claude Code and Auggie, you paste back what the sign-in page gives you. Codex signs in with **ChatGPT (device code)**, which *works on any machine*, with an API key, or with **Import local Codex login**. See [Agent Integrations](/kepler/agent-integrations).

<div class="note" markdown="1">

**Remote windows use this app's interface.** When the host runs the same version of Kepler, a remote window shows this app's interface. Otherwise, it shows the host's own interface. To keep this app's interface even then, turn on **Settings → Remote environments → Remote windows → Always use this app's interface**, and Kepler offers to update the server or this app instead. It is off by default.

</div>

**Themes belong to this computer.** Every window, including one on a remote machine, lists and installs themes from this computer's themes folder and gallery. Every window opens in the theme you chose.

In a remote window, the theme picker adds an **On *machine*** group for themes the host has and this computer does not:

- To copy a theme to this computer, click **Install on this computer**.
- When this computer has its own copy of the same theme, the host's copy says how it compares, such as **Older than yours**. Installing it asks first, then moves your copy to the Trash (the Recycle Bin on Windows).
- Kepler never overwrites a copy you installed; it stays as it is until you update it yourself.

Kepler refuses a host theme that conflicts with a built-in theme or another theme on this computer, and refuses installs when the themes folder is full or you install too many at once. See [Themes in a remote window](/kepler/settings-app#themes-in-a-remote-window).

***

## What you see while connecting

The first connection to a host where Kepler is not installed sends the server to it, so it takes minutes rather than seconds. The chip, the popover, and the host's Settings page name the current stage, such as **Uploading remote server**, with a progress bar when the total is known. Reconnecting to a host whose server is already running is much faster.

**Cancel** stops the attempt, from the popover or from the host's own **Connect** button.

If Kepler launches directly into a remote window and connecting takes more than a moment, the window shows a *Connecting…* screen with the stage and **Cancel**. **Cancel** there stops the restore for that machine only.

***

## Recovery after restart or sleep

When a connection breaks, Kepler rebuilds it.

| Event | What Kepler does |
|---|---|
| **The connection drops** | The chip reads **Reconnecting…** and Kepler retries |
| **The machine wakes from sleep** | Kepler reconnects right away to any machine it lost |
| **The connection comes back to the same server** | The page stays as it was, with your drafts, scroll position, and terminal scrollback |
| **The server restarts or updates** | The window reconnects when the server is back, and reloads onto the view it was on |
| **Kepler restarts** | Every window comes back with its size, position, view, and machine |
| **A reconnect cannot finish** | The window shows the [recovery screen](#the-recovery-screen). A host that needs a password is the usual cause |

A rebuilt connection comes back signed in, with your drafts and preferences intact.

### The recovery screen

When a window cannot reconnect to its machine, it shows a full-screen recovery screen. The screen names what happened, shows the reason it failed, and offers one action to reconnect, plus **Switch to local**. The window keeps its saved machine until it reconnects or you choose **Switch to local**.

When any window reconnects to the machine, the other windows waiting on the recovery screen reconnect too.

The action depends on what happened:

| What happened | Action |
|---|---|
| A reconnect gave up, or the server was stopped from another window or device | **Reconnect** |
| A server update or restart failed, a new window could not connect, or the window kept failing to load | **Try again** |
| Kepler launched into a remote window that could not connect | **Connect** |
| The machine is no longer saved | **Open Remote environments** |

A failed update or restart leaves the server stopped. **Try again** installs the update and starts the server. If the machine needs a password, the screen asks for it.

**If your plan does not include remote environments**, the screen says so, and offers **Upgrade to *plan*** or a free trial when one is available. You can also switch to another organization marked *Includes remote environments*, sign out, or click **Check again** to re-read your plan. Once your plan allows it, the window connects by itself.

***

## Local conveniences that still work

Some things have to happen on the machine in front of you. Kepler runs those through the desktop app rather than on the host.

| Feature | Behavior over a remote connection |
|---|---|
| **Open in…** and **Show in Finder** (**Show in Explorer** on Windows, **Show in file manager** on Linux) | Run on your desktop machine, not on the host. Kepler shows only the ones that work for this machine |
| **Desktop notifications** | Shown by your local desktop once per machine, or inside Kepler while you are in a window on that machine. A muted host shows none |
| **Dictation** | Captured by the local app. See [Dictation and Read Aloud](/kepler/voice-input) |
| **Copying from Codex** | A copy Codex makes in a remote window goes to your local clipboard, not the host's |
| **Pasting in a Windows host's terminal** | **Ctrl+V** pastes your local clipboard, even when this window runs on macOS or Linux |
| **Folder pickers** | Browse the host's filesystem, since that is where the work lives |

These 7 editors open a remote folder through their own remote extension:

| Editor | Opens remote folders on |
|---|---|
| **VS Code** | SSH and WSL |
| **VS Code Insiders** | SSH and WSL |
| **Cursor** | SSH and WSL |
| **Devin** (formerly Windsurf) | SSH and WSL |
| **Antigravity IDE** | SSH and WSL |
| **Trae** | SSH and WSL |
| **Kiro** | SSH only, not WSL |

The editor resolves the host and authenticates by itself. For SSH, the editor uses your own SSH configuration, so a host Kepler reaches with a custom identity file may still prompt in the editor.

Other editors, and the file manager, need a path that Windows can reach. WSL provides one, `\\wsl$`, but an SSH host does not. When no such path exists, Kepler does not show the option.

***

## How Kepler installs on a remote machine

The first connection to a machine downloads the Kepler server, so it takes minutes. Later updates download only what changed. The host needs nothing pre-installed beyond SSH or WSL, and Kepler installs itself to `~/.kepler-server`. If the download fails, check your internet connection and try again.

**Kepler never installs over a running server.** On connect, it replaces an out-of-date server on its own only when no running agents, open terminals, or other connected windows would be affected. Otherwise the server keeps running and the chip offers **Restart server to update**. With **Always use this app's interface** on, other connected windows and devices no longer hold the update back.

### When the server and the window disagree

When a remote window and its server run different versions, the window can show a full-screen message instead of the app:

- *This remote server is out of date*: click **Update server**.
- *This remote server is newer than this window*: update this app. If no newer version of the app is available, click **Replace server** to put this app's version on the server. Kepler asks first. If the server's data is newer than this app can read, Kepler refuses; update this app instead.
- Otherwise, **Try again** loads the matching version. If the message keeps coming back, restart the server.

**Switch to local** moves the window back to this computer.

***

## Remote access: reach Kepler from another device

**Remote Access** is the other direction. It opens this Kepler window from another device, such as a second computer or a phone, through your GitKraken account. Your work still runs here; the other device only sees the interface.

Configure it in **Settings → Remote Access**, or from the **Remote Access** button in the title bar. The button's icon is green while Remote Access is active, amber while it connects, and red on an error. Hover over it to open its popover, which acts on the machine the window is on:

- How many devices are paired and online.
- While active, a QR code and the link, with **Copy link**.
- **Turn on Remote Access** or **Turn off Remote Access**.
- **Manage Remote Access…**, which opens **Settings → Remote Access**.

### Before you start

You need a GitKraken account signed in to Kepler, on a paid GitKraken plan. Remote Access is not available on the free Community plan.

When you sign out of Kepler, each remote machine your windows are connected to learns that you signed out, and turns its Remote Access off. A sign-in that expires on its own does not turn Remote Access off.

If Kepler on the computer is not signed in, a paired device shows **Sign in**. Only the GitKraken account that turned on Remote Access can sign the computer in from there. To use another account, sign in to Kepler on the computer itself.

### Turning on Remote Access

1. Open **Settings → Remote Access**.
2. Click **Turn on Remote Access**.
3. In **Name this machine**, keep the name Kepler fills in, or enter a name you recognize. gitkraken.dev shows this name in your list of machines.

**Remote Access stays on until you turn it off.** Only you, a deliberate sign-out, or a different account signing in turns it off. When Kepler restarts, it turns Remote Access back on only for the account that turned it on. When the connection fails, Kepler keeps retrying, and the status reads **Waiting to reconnect** with the reason. **Retry now** tries at once. Paired devices stay paired through the wait. Remote Access also waits in these 2 cases:

- With no GitKraken sign-in, it connects as soon as you sign in.
- When your account has reached its limit of machines with Remote Access on, remove one you no longer use with **Manage machines on gitkraken.dev**, then retry.

This machine stays awake while Remote Access is on, except while it waits to reconnect.

To turn it off, click **Turn off Remote Access** in Settings or in the popover, and confirm. Every paired device is disconnected.

### Pairing another device

When Remote Access is active, a QR code and a link appear in Settings and in the popover.

- To pair a phone, scan the QR code. Otherwise, copy the link.
- The link opens **gitkraken.dev/integrations**, where you approve the connection with your GitKraken account.

A pairing link works once and expires after 5 minutes. To pair after that, open a new link from the computer running Kepler.

You can bookmark the address a paired browser opens on. If that browser's connection has ended, opening the address again takes you to gitkraken.dev to sign in and pair it again.

### Using Kepler on a phone

When you open Kepler in a phone's browser, it uses a phone layout: one bar at the top of each screen in place of the desktop top bar and headers. The phone layout applies to any browser window as narrow as a phone. The desktop app never uses it, at any window width. On a touch screen, Kepler also keeps the phone awake while you watch a working agent or a terminal printing output, so the connection does not drop. When the on-screen keyboard is open, Kepler fits the screen above it. In the composer, **Enter** starts a new line. To send, tap **Send**.

To open Kepler like an app, add it to your phone's home screen from the browser's menu, such as **Add to Home Screen**. The Kepler icon then opens Kepler full screen, without the browser's address bar and toolbars.

#### The menu

**Menu**, the first button in the bar, opens the **Kepler** drawer:

- **Views**: your Dashboard views, each with its count. Tap a view to show it, or press and hold it for its menu
- **Recent tasks**: the 5 most recently active tasks, each with a dot when it is waiting on you
- **Feedback**, **Settings**, and **Help**
- Your account row, with your plan or the days left in a trial

#### The Dashboard

The Dashboard's bar holds **Menu**, a view picker, **Search**, **Options**, and **New task**. The view picker switches between your Dashboard views and has **New view**. **Search** expands in the bar. **Options** opens a sheet with **Refresh** and the view's settings, such as its grouping, sort and filters.

Tapping an item opens it full screen, with a **Back to list** arrow at the left of the bar. A pull request or issue shows its title as a chip in the bar, with its own actions beside it. Tap the title to open **Switch item**, a sheet that lists every pull request and issue in your Todo list, in the same groups and order, with the current one checked. Tap another to open it in place.

#### A task

A task's bar has **Back**, the task's name, and one icon each for **Sessions**, **Changes**, **Terminal**, and **Resources**. A dot on **Back** means another task needs you.

- **Tap an icon** to go to what is waiting there first, or else the last thing you had open. Its list offers each row, an action to add one (**New session**, **New terminal**, or **Add resource**), and **Show everything in this task**.
- **Tap the task's name** to open **Switch task**, a sheet of every task in the Dashboard's order. Swipe sideways on the name to go back to the previous task.
- **Pull down on the bar** for a sheet of everything in the task: sessions, checkouts, terminals, and resources, with each row's actions.

Under the bar, a details row shows the task's stage and a summary. Expand it to see the checkout and the task's pull request and issue.

**Add resource** opens a sheet of resource kinds. Pick a kind to see what the task already holds, add more with its add control, such as **Add issues**, or use **Select** to archive or remove several at once.

**Changes** opens with one bar: **Close**, the file's name, and **Previous** and **Next**. Tap the name for the list of changed files. Everything else, from which changes to show to saving an edit, is in the bar's overflow menu.

#### Terminals

On a touch phone, every live terminal has a key row under it with the keys a phone keyboard lacks: **Esc**, **Ctrl**, **Tab**, the arrows, **Enter**, **Keyboard**, which shows or hides the phone keyboard, and **Hide keys**. Swipe up on a key, or hold **Esc**, **Ctrl**, **Tab**, or **Enter**, for the second action printed above it:

| Key | Second action |
|---|---|
| **Esc** | **Ctrl+C** |
| **Ctrl** | **Shift** |
| **Tab** | **Shift+Tab** |
| **Enter** | **New line** |
| Left and Right arrows | **Home** and **End** |
| Up and Down arrows | **Page up** and **Page down** |

Tap **Ctrl** once to hold it for the next key only, or double-tap it to lock it until you tap it again. Shift works the same way: swipe up on or hold **Ctrl** once to hold Shift for the next key, or twice quickly to lock it. With Shift on, the letters you type are capitals. Holding an arrow repeats it. **Hide keys** replaces the row with a **Show keys** button, and this device remembers the choice. The phone keyboard opens only when you tap the terminal or **Keyboard**, not on every scroll.

To select text, long-press a word, and drag before you lift to extend the selection. A pill offers **Open** when you pressed a link or a file path, plus **Copy**, **Paste**, and **Select all**. A long press on blank space offers **Paste** and **Select all**. In a program that tracks the mouse, such as a menu in an agent's terminal app, a tap clicks.

### Managing sessions from gitkraken.dev

Go to **gitkraken.dev → Integrations → Remote Access** to manage every machine with Remote Access turned on, across all your devices.

- Expand a machine to see its active connections.
- Revoke a single connection to sign out one paired device without affecting the others.
- Disable a machine to turn off its Remote Access entirely, from anywhere.

You can also manage the current machine's connections locally, in **Settings → Remote Access → Connected devices**. **Machines on your account**, on the same page even while Remote Access is off, opens the machine list on gitkraken.dev with **Manage machines on gitkraken.dev**, so you can remove machines you no longer use.

***

## Known limitations

| Limitation | Detail |
|---|---|
| **Commit and tag signing** | Signing does not work over a remote connection. Turn off `commit.gpgsign` for the repository on the remote, or commit from a terminal there |
| **Remote-connection management in a browser client** | Desktop app only. A browser client hides the title-bar chip |
| **Auto-update in a browser client** | Does nothing, because a browser cannot update itself. Update the desktop app, or update the host's server from a desktop window |
| **Port forwarding from a Windows client** | A host that signs in with a password asks for it again for each forward. Only `localhost`, `127.0.0.1`, and `0.0.0.0` links forward |
| **Host-side cleanup on a Windows host** | **Uninstall Kepler server on the machine** and **Remove deployed key from remote authorized_keys** do not work on a Windows host. Delete `~/.kepler-server` and the `authorized_keys` entry on the host yourself |

***

- [Agent Integrations](/kepler/agent-integrations): signing agents in, including on a remote target
- [Review Changes](/kepler/review-changes): reviewing and shipping the work a remote agent produced

# Kepler 0.x
URL: https://help.gitkraken.com/kepler/release-notes-current/
product: Kepler
feature: Release Notes
content_type: release-notes
audience: all
plan_required: all
status: GA
last_verified: 2026-11

Kepler is GitKraken's **Agentic Development Environment (ADE)**: one place to direct coding agents across every issue and pull request assigned to you, in as many repositories as you need, at the same time. You bring the agent; Kepler attaches the context and carries the result through to a reviewed, mergeable change.

<img src="/wp-content/uploads/release-notes-hero-amethyst-oct-2026@2x.png" class="help-center-img img-bordered" alt="Kepler's top toolbar in the Amethyst theme, with the Update available button highlighted next to the Local environment picker, beside the Kepler planet logo.">

This release notes page tracks what's new and changing in the current version of Kepler, including new features, improvements, bug fixes, and breaking changes. Use it to see what shipped in the most recent release, confirm when a capability became available, or review changes before upgrading.

**Requirements and limits**

- This page covers the current version line of Kepler, 0.x. Archived version pages will be listed here as later lines ship.
- Each entry applies only to the specific release listed under its version heading.
- Kepler is in public preview. A free GitKraken account is all you need to run it, though a few capabilities, such as [Remote Access](/kepler/remote-environments), require a paid GitKraken plan.
- Kepler updates itself. You're prompted to restart when a new version is published, and **Check for Updates** in the app menu asks straight away.

<a href="https://www.gitkraken.com/kepler/download?source=help_center" target="_blank" class="button button--basic ">Download Current Version Now</a>

New to Kepler? [Getting Started with Kepler](/kepler/kepler-getting-started) takes you from install to your first agent-run task.

***

<a id="v0-16-0"></a>
## Version 0.19.0

<kbd>Wednesday, November 11th, 2026</kbd>

### Highlights

- **Put your agents on autopilot with Automations.** Automations watch GitHub or Jira for new activity that matches a query, or run on a schedule, and start a task that runs an Action or your own prompt.
- **Bring your workspaces over from another app.** Import workspaces from Conductor, Orca, herdr and Vibe Kanban as tasks, with their chats resumed.
- **Have agent replies read aloud.** Agent replies can be read aloud from a button on each chat reply, or from "Read aloud from here" in the message and terminal menus, with Stop in the title bar.

### Features

#### Automations

- Automations watch GitHub or Jira for new activity that matches a query, or run on a schedule, and start a task that runs an Action or your own prompt.
- Open Automations from the Dashboard to see runs that need you, runs in progress and earlier runs, and open any run's details or task.
- Start from templates such as reviewing pull requests awaiting your review, planning or implementing issues assigned to you, triaging new bugs and addressing feedback on your pull requests.
- Choose whether an automation runs once per item or on each new activity, whether it ignores your own activity, the base branch, and the task group its tasks join.
- Pick whether an automation runs on any of your installs, only this one or another one, and see runs from your other installs.
- Ask Kepler can draft an automation for you to review and create, and More actions duplicates one, warning when the copy would do the same thing as the original.
- Run now checks right away, an automation that keeps running on one item stops itself to prevent a loop, and a run whose agent is signed out is skipped instead of leaving an empty task.

#### Import from other apps

- Import workspaces from Conductor, Orca, herdr and Vibe Kanban as tasks, with their chats resumed.
- Open the import from the Tasks empty state or the File menu; it lists the apps found on this machine and marks workspaces already imported.
- Cursor CLI chats you started in the terminal now appear in Cursor's history and can be resumed.

#### Read aloud

- Agent replies can be read aloud from a button on each chat reply, or from "Read aloud from here" in the message and terminal menus, with Stop in the title bar.
- Only prose is spoken: code, diffs and tables become short summaries, and the sentence being read is highlighted.
- Download the Kokoro voices for far more natural English speech, or use your system's voices.
- Settings → Voice now holds Dictation and Read aloud, each with its own downloads, and voice input is now called Dictation.

#### Task notes

- Edit a note in the code editor with syntax highlighting, find and undo, and a save that would overwrite someone else's change asks first.
- Leave review comments on a note, on a selection, a section or a line, and send them to an agent like code comments.
- See who last edited a note, and what changed between any two of its versions.
- Checklists in a note render as checkboxes you can tick.
- Copy a link to a note or one of its sections, and the link opens the note scrolled to that section.

#### Dashboard

- Type filters as qualifiers in the search box, like `group:"Release work" -progress:done`, with suggestions as you type, and save them with the tab.
- Ask Kepler can create and change Dashboard views for you.
- Group the Todo by milestone.
- A pull request's chips show whether its CI is passing, pending or failing.
- Each group in a task's Resources pane has a "+" that adds that kind of resource.

#### Command palette

- A Commands tab, or typing `>`, lists and runs commands, Settings pages and window actions.
- A Todo tab, or typing `#`, searches the Todo's pull requests and issues by title, number or link.

#### Keyboard shortcuts

- Rebind any shortcut in Settings → Keyboard shortcuts, with search, conflict checks and reset.
- New commands jump to the next task that needs attention, the next unread one, or either.
- Send chat messages with Cmd/Ctrl+Enter instead of Enter, set in Settings → General.

#### Repositories

- Repos found by scanning your repositories folder stay untrusted until you trust them, and Kepler runs no git in them meanwhile; each repo and folder has a Trusted switch in Settings.
- The guided start gains a Repos step that lists the repos and folders found on this machine for you to pick from.
- A removed repo or folder is no longer added back by the next scan.

#### Updating branches

- The batch update can publish branches that have no remote branch yet, and shows what will happen to each branch before you press Update.
- Set each repository's default update method and when to push after an update, and override both for one batch update.

#### Antigravity and Grok

- Antigravity terminals show Kepler's status line, use the workspace tools without asking each time, and take your model, mode and effort picks.
- Antigravity and Grok receive your first message right away, without waiting for you to press Enter.

#### Smaller additions

- Review comment replies show their count on the task, the Dashboard preview and session tabs, and appear in the agent's transcript.
- A setting in Settings → Tasks chooses whether a started task's panel opens beside the focused one or at the end.
- The phone terminal's key row gains Shift, by swiping up or holding on Ctrl.

### Improvements

#### Dashboard

- The Columns and Grid toggle is replaced by one layout picker: one row lays panels side by side, more rows draw a grid.
- A started or revealed task opens beside the panel you're reading, and the task list scrolls to the active panel's task.
- Clicking a row whose panel is already open focuses it instead of closing the others.
- A grid page that isn't full stretches its last panel to fill the empty cells.
- A stopped agent now reads "Agent stopped" instead of "Turn failed" in Needs attention.

#### Interface

- A narrow desktop window keeps the desktop layout instead of switching to the phone one, and folds panes away when they don't fit.
- The default agent setting is now the same agent pill as the composer, with a checkbox to start on your last pick, and Ask Kepler has its own copy of that setting.
- An agent's on/off options, like Fast mode, sit together in one Options menu.

#### Performance

- Kepler runs background git work only for repositories you're using, so a long repo list costs much less.
- The Changes overlay, All files and Go to File open faster.
- Open conversations no longer redraw on unrelated task page updates.

### Fixes

#### Agents

- A session restarted after its agent process died keeps its model and mode picks.
- A chat that ended without an error code can be continued with a new message.
- A session whose background work ends during its final answer no longer looks finished too early.
- After switching accounts, the usage gauge shows the picked account's usage.
- A finished OpenCode terminal turn is marked unread.
- Auggie 0.37.0 keeps the MCP servers from its own settings.
- Kepler refuses prompts sent by an agent that imitate Kepler's own hidden instructions.

#### Tasks

- Archiving or deleting a task with its worktrees now also ends their terminals, so the folders are removed on Windows.
- A session in a repo not yet added to Kepler no longer attaches to a folder task above it, such as your home folder.

#### Remote

- Remote Access no longer crashes with "Something went wrong" on iOS 26 and Safari 26.
- The phone of the account that owns Remote Access can sign a signed-out computer back in.

#### Connections

- With two accounts on one self-hosted installation, issues, comments, images and git all use the same account.
- Jira Server attachment images and comments load on installations with special characters in their path.
- Each provider connection gets its own section in the Todo's filters.

### Breaking changes

- The `Ctrl+\` (`Cmd+\` on macOS) shortcut that switched between Columns and Grid is gone, along with the toggle.

***

## Version 0.18.0

<kbd>Friday, November 6th, 2026</kbd>

### Highlights

- **Jump to any task or file from one palette.** F1 or Cmd/Ctrl+Shift+P, or View > Command Palette…, opens your tasks in Dashboard order, ranked by name as you type.
- **Review and commit from one list on your branch line.** One list on the branch line replaces the five-mode toggle: All changes, Working changes, each commit and the base, where you click, Shift-click or Cmd/Ctrl-click to diff any unbroken run.

### Features

#### Command palette

- F1 or Cmd/Ctrl+Shift+P, or View > Command Palette…, opens your tasks in Dashboard order, ranked by name as you type.
- Switch between Tasks and Files from the tabs under the field, or type `@` to search the files of the current task.
- Paste a task or session link to find its task.
- Alt+Enter opens the highlighted row's actions, with the same actions a task has on the Dashboard.
- A task search ends in New task and Ask Kepler rows that carry what you typed.
- Open Folder… (Cmd/Ctrl+Shift+O) picks a folder, and file search lists the folders holding a task's files.

#### Changes

- One list on the branch line replaces the five-mode toggle: All changes, Working changes, each commit and the base, where you click, Shift-click or Cmd/Ctrl-click to diff any unbroken run.
- Commit… opens a commit mode for staging and the message, and a commit that fails after you've moved on offers to take you back to it.
- The base branch's landing rows show each commit's author and tooltip.

#### Agent set-up

- The set-up dialog offers only the install methods this machine can run, including Pi's native installer and Codex's standalone installer on Windows, and says when one needs Node.js.
- It notes when the vendor's desktop app is installed but Kepler still needs the command-line tool.
- Sign-in is offered right after an install.

#### Connections

- Asana joins as an issue tracker: its tasks reach Todo and the issue explorer, and you can filter by workspace and project.
- Connect several self-hosted installations of a provider, each managed and refreshed on its own in Settings, so one failing server leaves the others working.

#### Composer

- Inline code and fenced blocks are drawn as you type, and commands, mentions and quotes are colored.
- A picked file mention shows as a chip.
- A finished quote becomes one collapsible block, and clicking it scrolls the transcript to where it came from.

#### Task notes

- Browse a note's saved versions, restore one, and bring back deleted notes from a Deleted list.
- Save a note as a Markdown file from its menu.

#### Dashboard

- Right-click a selection of tasks to set Progress, read state and stars, or shut down their agents.
- Filter Todo pull requests by author and reviewer.
- Agent Graph is offered in the New view menu.
- A panel's takeover is now Solo, with drag edges to resize it and a Maximize toggle to fill the space.

#### Codex

- A Codex session shows each sub-agent's own messages, tool calls and permission requests, with nested sub-agents underneath.
- Continue a Codex session as another account.

#### Smaller additions

- Running background tasks appear as chips above the composer.
- Open an external session right from a new session's draft.
- A task on hold can wait on any of its pull requests.
- Suggest automatically in Settings → Actions controls whether linking an item switches the launch button to its suggested Action.
- Add the web UI to a phone's home screen to open it without browser chrome.
- Open a repo on its host from its settings page.
- Delete a worktree from its row's menu in a task.

### Improvements

#### Tasks and sessions

- Only a task's own resources open as tabs; any other file from a link or Go to File opens in the overlay, with Add to task.
- A new session in a task with several live worktrees or folders starts across all of them.
- A task's resources appear in one order everywhere, and are grouped by kind on the phone.
- Tabs lose their kebab menu, and an inactive tab shows its close control on hover.
- The model picker always shows every option, and changing one on a preset reads "(unsaved)".

#### Remote

- When a server is newer than the app and no update is available, you can replace it after a confirmation, and a replacement is refused if the server's data is too new for that build.
- Preview headers start folded on the phone and in multi-row grids.

#### Settings

- The Actions page explains what an Action is and how each built-in one differs.
- The task panel and Settings are drawn as cards, like the Dashboard.

#### Performance

- The app launches faster on later starts.
- The Dashboard, the Changes list and large diffs redraw and load less.
- Ask Kepler shows your message as soon as you press send, instead of after the agent boots.
- Open terminals use less memory.

### Fixes

#### Platforms and networks

- Sign-in, account requests, provider reads and the agents Kepler launches now go through your system or `HTTPS_PROXY` proxy, and a failure through a proxy names it.
- Windows updates no longer fail with "Failed to uninstall old application files".
- On macOS without the Command Line Tools, Kepler no longer opens the install dialog on every launch and now finds a Homebrew git.
- Local connections on macOS wait while you answer the local network permission prompt, instead of failing.
- On WSL, agent lookups skip Windows-drive PATH entries.

#### Agents

- An agent's sign-in refusal is now shown, instead of the session closing silently.
- Copilot's sign-in state and usage are read correctly.
- A Codex session resumes on its own model, and Codex sign-in recovers from a ChatGPT login with no tokens.
- An install that exits cleanly without an agent Kepler can find now fails.
- A launch prompt stays as a draft when sign-in is dismissed.

#### Git

- A first push onto someone else's branch says the branch name is taken.
- Force delete is offered for branches git kept as unmerged, and a branch already gone from the remote counts as deleted.
- A teammate's open pull request no longer attaches to a task whose branch has the same name, and branch lookups no longer query contributors' gitlab.com forks.

#### Remote

- A remote window keeps its page across a reconnect that spans a sleep, and retries a reload that fails during one.
- A restore that updated its server retries until the server answers.

#### Interface

- Every visible Grid panel loads an ended session's transcript, instead of spinning until focused.
- Attachments over the 20-file limit are refused before any upload.
- Tab stays inside confirm dialogs, and focus returns after task dialogs.
- Kepler comes forward after a browser sign-in.

### Breaking changes

- Presets now belong to one agent: presets that spanned agents are removed, and the built-in Default preset is gone.

***

## Version 0.17.0

<kbd>Tuesday, November 3rd, 2026</kbd>

### Highlights

- **Build the Dashboard from your own saved views.** The Dashboard runs on saved views you name, add, duplicate, reorder and delete, each keeping its own layout, grouping, sort, filters, search and previews.
- **Put a task on hold until CI, a review or a merge wakes it.** Put a task on hold until its pull request's CI passes, a review arrives, it merges or closes, another task is done, or a time you pick.
- **See what landed on the base branch before you rebase.** A chip beside the base branch shows how much is new on it, how much overlaps your branch and what may conflict, and opens those changes to review.

### Features

#### Dashboard views

- The Dashboard runs on saved views you name, add, duplicate, reorder and delete, each keeping its own layout, grouping, sort, filters, search and previews.
- Show the views as tabs, as pills, in the title bar or down a side rail, and give each view its own icon from a larger set.
- Todo can show everything open in Kepler's repositories, not just what relates to you, narrowed to the repos you pick.
- Needs attention now lists tasks with a failed turn, failing CI or a new changes-requested review, and names the reason on the row.
- The Inbox gains Important, Not started and Later sections, and each view shows how many tasks it matches.

#### Task holds

- Put a task on hold until its pull request's CI passes, a review arrives, it merges or closes, another task is done, or a time you pick.
- The task wakes by itself when the condition is met, even if it happened while Kepler was closed, and tells you why.

#### Changes

- A chip beside the base branch shows how much is new on it, how much overlaps your branch and what may conflict, and opens those changes to review.
- Open the host's compare page from the same chip.
- Discard a folder, a single file or all working changes from the changes tree and its toolbar, keeping a partly staged file's staged part.
- Edit a file straight from a commit's view, and keep an unsaved edit when switching between File and Changes.
- Pick Stacked or Split diffs from a menu beside Search and Wrap.

#### Idle agents sleep

- Agent sessions you are not using go to sleep after a quiet spell, freeing their processes, and wake on your next message with the conversation intact.
- Set the sleep timer in Settings.
- Tasks set aside for later or archived stop their agents; their sessions resume when you open them.

#### Task resources

- A new screen lists, adds and tidies a task's issues, pull requests, repositories, files and links, with a tab per kind.
- Archive a resource to hide it from the rail and Dashboard, and undo a removal while its Undo shows.

#### Agent presets

- Save an agent, model, mode and effort as a preset and pick it in the composer, with Manage presets right in the Preset picker.

#### Smaller additions

- New worktrees copy the ignored files listed in `.worktreeinclude`, such as `.env`.
- Answer an agent's permission request straight from its task row.
- Run a command or open the worktree in an editor from the collapsed task preview header.
- Paste a task or session link into Dashboard search to find it, archived ones included.
- Alt+Shift+Up/Down steps through the task list, and Cmd+Shift+Backspace deletes the current task.
- Cmd/Ctrl+Shift+K starts a new Ask Kepler chat, Cmd/Ctrl+Shift+L starts a new chat, and panel layout moves to Cmd/Ctrl+\.
- Mark a session as read or unread from its own menu.
- Finished agent replies show their time.
- Archive an Ask Kepler chat from its header, and see each chat's state and your archived chats in the picker.
- Manage task groups from a Groups section in Tasks settings, with four new group colors.
- Agents attach files up to 200 MB, and WSL files attach by path.

### Improvements

#### Tasks

- A task's worktree catches up with its base branch when a session starts, if it has no commits of its own yet.
- New-branch worktrees an agent plans for a task are only created when the task's first session starts.
- Resuming or starting a session in an archived task restores the task.

#### Agent setup

- Set up an agent from the composer when none is installed, or point Kepler at one you already have.
- Onboarding's agents step can rescan, or continue without an agent.

#### Settings

- The Chat, Code, Terminal and new-task settings are redrawn, and the Advanced page is a searchable, foldable grid.
- Settings search stays pinned above the side list and is focused when Settings opens.

#### Remote

- A new opt-in always uses this app's interface in remote windows.
- A remote window retries a failed page load before showing the recovery screen, and keeps its loading cover up through an update or restart.

#### Windows

- Updates download and stage in the background, on ARM64 too, and swap in on restart.
- Ctrl+V in a Windows-host terminal pastes the local clipboard.

#### Performance

- Long chat transcripts open faster, loading earlier messages on request.
- Sessions start sooner, the app launches faster, and the Dashboard redraws only what changed.
- Archiving many tasks at once is quicker.

### Fixes

#### Agents

- A model or mode picked while a session is starting now applies.
- A chat session no longer leaves its view while it stops.
- Agents no longer stop when a command prints very large output.
- Prompts the agent can't accept right away are kept with their attachments instead of lost.
- Kepler's hooks work in every extra Codex login.

#### Windows

- Background processes no longer flash a console window.
- Maximized and fullscreen windows no longer draw a top border.

#### Terminal

- Live terminals no longer go blank white after others close.
- A restored terminal puts its cursor back in the right place.

#### Interface

- Popovers and menus close when you click the top bar.
- Attachments with the same name are told apart.
- Pull request lookups no longer use up a GitHub rate limit or query contributors' forks.
- A notification opens its task with the task list scrolled to it.

## Version 0.16.0

<kbd>Thursday, October 29th, 2026</kbd>

### Highlights

- **Sort your tasks into your own groups.** Make task groups with a name and a color, and group the Dashboard list and board by them, alone or nested with Inbox, Progress, Activity or Repository.
- **Comment on any line of a diff and send it to an agent.** Leave a comment on any diff or file view, then queue it for a session or send it right away. Agents reply in a thread and can resolve your comments.
- **Find, change or link to any setting.** A new **Advanced** page lists every setting, `kepler://settings` links open Settings at the setting itself, and Ask Kepler and your agents can change settings for you.

### Features

#### Task groups

- Make your own task groups, each with a name and a color, and group the Dashboard list and board by them, alone or nested with **Inbox**, **Progress**, **Activity** or **Repository**.
- Add tasks to a group from the task menu or by dragging them onto it. Reorder, recolor, archive or delete a group from its header.
- Select several tasks and act on them together from the right-click menu, or drag them together.
- Agents can read and change task groups too.

#### Review comments

- Leave a comment on any line of any diff or file view, then queue it for a session or send it right away.
- Agents reply to your comments in a thread and can resolve them. A comments list shows every comment on a task, by file or by status.
- A comment stays in place as the code changes, or is marked **Outdated** when its lines are gone.

#### Settings

- A new **Advanced** page lists every setting, and typing `@id:` in **Search settings** jumps to one setting.
- `kepler://settings` links open Settings right at the setting's control.
- Ask Kepler and your agents can find and change Kepler settings for you.

#### Ask Kepler

- A docked mode makes room for the panel instead of covering the page.
- Cmd/Ctrl+K also toggles Ask Kepler, unless a terminal has focus.
- Attach files to a new chat's first message.
- The top bar button shows whether a panel chat is working or needs you.
- Ask Kepler keeps its own default agent, separate from the one your tasks use.

#### Tray icon

- The tray icon shows the most urgent agent state: needs you, failed, unread or working.
- Clicking it opens the window that needs attention, and its menu lists your windows and opens a new one.

#### Smaller additions

- Copilot account usage shows in Kepler, and an exhausted quota is clearly marked.
- Approve or deny any approval from its alert, and on macOS from the desktop notification.
- Create a task from the worktrees and branches you selected in Settings.
- Pick a Linear project in **Add resources**.
- Jira issues link from commits and branches.
- Several active tasks can share the same pull request.

### Improvements

#### Dashboard

- Collapse the task list beside open panels. Hover its toggle to peek at it, or press Cmd/Ctrl+Shift+B to float it.
- A row's pull request and issue chips open their link card, which lists every linked item.
- Todo pull requests and issues show the tasks already started from them.
- Folded group sections stay folded after a restart, and groups follow the selected sort.
- Dragging rows and opening a selection feel quicker.

#### Agents

- **Continue as another account** and switching between **Chat** and **Terminal** now ask before stopping a session that looks busy, instead of refusing.
- A session with only background work running shows as idle, not running.
- A live session picked from another app opens read-only, with **Continue here** and **Fork live** on its task tab.
- If the browser can't open for sign-in, Kepler shows a link you can copy.

#### Updating branches

- Choose between rebase and merge when updating a branch. A clean merge applies and pushes by default.
- A failed push offers clear ways to recover, and undo keeps working after Git restores files.

#### Interface

- The task page rail shows the worktree's state, a detached HEAD and errors.
- A Linear issue synced with GitHub shows once, and both copies share the same tasks.
- Large text pastes in the composer become attachments.

### Fixes

#### Agents

- Claude browser sign-in completes even when `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` is set, and signed-in Claude accounts stay signed in.
- A signed-in agent account is no longer asked to sign in again.
- A usage limit hit by one sub-agent no longer leaves its session stuck as running.
- An npm-installed agent CLI that's missing its native binary shows as not installed.
- Repositories that use Husky.Net run their own commit hooks again in agent worktrees.

#### Windows

- Copilot CLI installed with the MSI installer is found, and VS Code's Copilot launcher is no longer mistaken for it.
- npm-installed agents and agent installers start correctly.

#### Tasks and composer

- A pasted pull request launches in its own repository, and a link that can't be read no longer stops the launch.
- A Linear issue looked up from the Dashboard starts in its GitHub copy's repository.
- The **Commits** tab no longer hangs when a branch has no base, and says **No commits** when the branch is level with it.
- Settings closes in one click from any sub-page.

## Version 0.15.0

<kbd>Tuesday, October 27th, 2026</kbd>

### Highlights

- **Ask Kepler from any page.** The Ask Kepler side panel opens over any page with a chat that knows what you have on screen, plus quick terminals. See [Ask Kepler](/kepler/ask-kepler).
- **Work on up to 16 tasks side by side.** Open Dashboard items as panels in a grid of up to 16, with resizable rows and columns, and open every visible row at once.
- **Browse, install or create your own themes.** Try and install themes from the theme gallery, load your own from a folder, or ask an agent to create one. Themes now color terminals, diffs and code blocks too.
- **Approve what your agents do.** Before an agent starts a session, rewrites a branch or changes a task's notes, Kepler shows the whole request as a card and runs it only once you approve it.

### Features

#### Ask Kepler

- The Ask Kepler side panel opens over any page from the Kepler mark in the top bar or with Cmd/Ctrl+L, with a chat that knows what you have on screen.
- The panel keeps quick terminals too, opened with Ctrl+&#96;, and docks on the left or right.
- Past panel chats stay in a history picker, and a chat can continue as a new task.

#### Dashboard

- Open items as panels laid out in a grid of up to 16, with resizable rows and columns, and open every visible row at once.
- A **Manual** sort lets you drag tasks into your own order, and task cards can be dragged between groups on every Tasks grouping.
- Rows say what a task needs from you and show its linked pull request or issue, its sessions and its running terminals.
- A task preview has a side pane for its resources and its worktree's changes, toggled with Cmd/Ctrl+Shift+E and Cmd/Ctrl+Shift+G.
- Board columns fold to a rail and resize together from any column's edge.
- Drive the list and panels from the keyboard: Cmd/Ctrl+W closes the active panel, and Ctrl+Tab lists recently replaced ones.
- Todo pull request and issue rows have a right-click menu, and a finished task's row offers **Archive**.

#### Approvals and agent teamwork

- Before an agent starts a session, rewrites a branch or changes a task's notes, Kepler shows the whole request as a card and runs it only once you approve it: once, for the session or always.
- A session waiting on an approval shows as waiting on its row, its tab and the window title, and you can approve simple requests from the alert.
- Each session has an inbox of reports from the sessions it works with, and an idle agent wakes up to read them.
- Stop or message one sub-agent without stopping the turn, and see what a running sub-agent is doing.
- Copy a task or session as a Kepler link. Links and ids in chat and the terminal open the task or session, and agents accept them too.

#### Themes

- Browse, try and install themes from the theme gallery, and update them when a new version is published.
- Pick an appearance and a dark and a light theme from theme tiles. The appearance follows your system by default.
- Load your own themes from a folder and see edits live, or ask an agent to create one. The agent checks the theme's contrast before saving it.
- Themes now color terminals, diffs and code blocks.

#### Changes and files

- An **All changes** tab shows committed and uncommitted work together, **All files** browses the whole worktree, ignored files included, and **Commits** lists the branch's commits.
- The file overlay has a file tree and a breadcrumb to browse folders.
- Cmd/Ctrl+click a file path in chat or a terminal to open it in Kepler, or Cmd/Ctrl+Shift+click to open it in your editor.
- Find text across every file of a code view, and select and copy across long files.
- Stage and discard with Space and Delete, and move between changes from the keyboard.

#### Agents

- Run Claude Code through Amazon Bedrock, Google Vertex, Microsoft Foundry or an LLM gateway.
- Past sessions from Pi, OpenCode, Copilot, Grok, Auggie and Antigravity CLI are listed and can be previewed.
- Move a session to another account, or continue as another account when one reaches its usage limit.
- Move a session between **Chat** and **Terminal** from its menu.
- Copilot, Cursor and OpenCode get plan review in chat, and their sub-agents' work nests under the call that started it.
- Terminal launches offer each CLI's own options, such as Grok modes, Pi thinking and reasoning effort, and more CLIs get the first prompt at launch.
- Chat shows when the context is compacted and offers Fast mode as a toggle. Codex's and Cursor's own questions show in Kepler.

#### Voice dictation

- A new on-device dictation engine, Qwen3-ASR, is the default for new users. It detects the language you speak and supports all of its languages. See [Voice input](/kepler/voice-input).
- Dictation learns the words you correct and suggests them for your approval.

#### Smaller additions

- Settings manages worktrees and branches together in one list, with search, filters and each branch's tasks, sessions and pull requests.
- A code font size for every code and diff view, and a **Conversation width** setting for the chat.
- Hide organizations, repositories and projects per integration.
- Connect self-hosted code hosts and trackers with a URL and a personal access token.
- Pasted Jira, Linear, Azure DevOps, Bitbucket and self-hosted links turn into chips in the composer.
- Browse Jira project backlogs in **Add resources**.
- Set, change or unset a branch's upstream from its menu.
- Rename a task or a note by double-clicking its name.
- Antigravity IDE, Kiro and Trae are offered as editors.

### Improvements

#### Getting started

- New users get a guided start through agents, theme, repositories and a first task, and existing users see it once.
- Kep, Kepler's mascot, keeps you company on loading, empty and launch screens.

#### Agents and terminals

- Agents keep running through app restarts and updates by default, and so do Run-command terminals.
- **Restart agent** picks up changes to your login shell's environment.
- Usage bars show your pace against the time elapsed, turn amber above 75% and red above 90%, and refresh when a usage window resets.
- Code blocks in chat collapse and keep their controls in view, and the transcript remembers where you scrolled.
- Desktop notifications when an agent needs you are on by default.

#### Phone and tablet

- The phone layout is rebuilt around one bar per screen, bottom sheets, touch-sized controls and a task switcher you can swipe.
- Phone terminals have a key row, long-press to paste and open links, and tap to click in full-screen programs.

#### Updating branches

- Review each AI-resolved file's versions, with the reason for every resolution, before you apply.
- Batch update also covers local branches with no worktree, and pushes updated branches that have an upstream.
- Update again or recalculate a stale result without discarding the last one.

#### Performance

- Kepler's background service idles while no window or session needs it.
- Kepler watches and refreshes only the checkouts you have open, so large workspaces stay responsive.
- The Changes overlay opens at once, and diffs are highlighted for files up to 20,000 lines.
- Long agent terminal histories use less memory.

#### Interface

- The **Add resources** dialog is rebuilt around a list of issues and pull requests, with filter presets.
- Pull requests, issues and worktrees have the same menu wherever they appear.
- Overlays can be resized from either edge, and the Changes and file overlays have a maximize toggle.
- Remote Access has its own button in the title bar and asks before turning off.

### Fixes

#### Agents

- OpenCode sign-in works and shows as signed in, with browser sign-in for OpenCode Go.
- A second Copilot account no longer signs in as another user, and a Codex login lands in the account being signed in.
- A slow-starting agent CLI gets more time to connect, and agents find PowerShell on Windows.
- A linked issue's description reaches the agent when a task launches.

#### Git and worktrees

- Deleted remote branches are pruned on fetch, and an SSH key that needs a PIN can fetch.
- A worktree whose branch and base were both deleted can be recreated, and a folder still in use says so instead of failing.
- A fork's pull request is no longer matched to your own branch of the same name, and a retargeted pull request follows its new base.

#### Providers

- Moved Jira and Linear issues are followed to their new key.
- Azure DevOps work item descriptions render, and branches match their work items by project.
- **Reconnect** fixes the failing connection instead of the primary one.

#### Terminals and remote

- A terminal keeps its size and stays readable through a dropped connection, and one shown off screen no longer resizes it.
- A remote server reconnects once and brings back all its windows after a drop, an update or a relaunch.
- The SSH wizard lists a private key that has no matching .pub file.

#### Interface

- A window reopens maximized on the monitor it was moved to, and Linux windows no longer flash light before the theme loads.
- A clicked notification opens in the window already showing its work.

### Breaking changes

- Kepler's workspace tools for agents have new names. If an agent's settings allow-list `mcp__kepler-workspace__` tools by name, update them to the new names. See [Tasks and resources](/kepler/tasks-and-resources) for the full list.
